title: Chapter 1 - System Intro
body:
55
Chapter 1 - System Intro
Overview of Changes

•  Alot of unneccessary mechanics and bloat hs been 
removed such as Tutor Points, Action Points, Training 
Pokemon, Injuries, Base Stat Relation, Loyalty, Throwing 
Range, Poke Edges, Jump Movement, Pokemon EXP , etc

•  Skill Checks have been reworked from a Target 
Number system to a Success/Die Pool System.

•  Pokemon now get mini-classes in their progression 
known as Roles

•  You can no longer capture in battle and it is relegated  
to social capturing or post battle

•  Struggles are now Basic Attacks, can be physical 
or special and can shift to the user’s types without 
capabilities like Firestarter

•  The Action System has been adjusted, having more 
Swift Options and making Full Actions cost a Standard + 
Swift but be more impactful and adding Reactions. 

•  Egg Moves, Tutor Moves and TM Lists are all 
combined into one Tutor List

•  Versatile Keyword has been added to give Status 
Attacks better usage compared to straight damage 
meta. 

•  All Afflictions are reworked, separated into Physical 
and Mental and a few added Conditions

•  All new Classes are added and reworked

•  The Initiative system has been changed to make  
combat more engaging and hopefully quicker

•  Abilities have all been reworked from the ground up 
and are more core to a playstyle, but you get fewer of 
them.
This will also include some interpretations of Pokemon 
lines, such as Annihilape being a split evolution instead 
of an evolution of Primeape, or removing Finizen as a 
pokemon and renaming Palafin (Zero Form) into Finizen 
(If you don’t agree with these, just homebrew them). 
As for all other differences, nearly everything has been 
adjusted  with  a  fine-tooth  comb  so  there  are  plenty 
of things that are the same conceptually but different 
mechanically.  Using  an  analogy,  PTU  is  a  house  and 
PTE is what happens when you refurnish it, build a few 
floors, new rooms, and paint the outside, its the same 
address, just a different experience.
The  primary  difference  between  PTU  and  PTE  is 
glaringly  obvious  and  it’s  the  lack  of  regard  towards 
the  video  game  franchise.  PTU  was  developed  in  a 
manner  that  directly  transferred video  game  content 
to a tabletop format. Obviously this comes with issues 
since it’s 1 to 1. We surely don’t need 50+ Berries. The 
only thing from the video game that has been faithfully 
kept is the type effectiveness chart because that is all 
burned into our memories. Everything else is up to our 
interpretation. This includes having homebrew Attacks, 
Abilities, Levelup Lists, etc. 
PTE vs PTU?
WE ARE NOT AFFILIATED WITH THE PTU DEV TEAM

title: Chapter 1 - System Intro (p.6)
body:
66
Chapter 1 - System Intro
Rule Book
This Document contains all the “Hard Rules” of the System. 
The Rule Book is focused entirely on information that is vital 
for a Player to know in order to play the PTE System. 
Rules  in  this  System  are  designed  to  be  less  flexible  and 
should be followed more strictly. It also contains the more 
essential information compared to information that would 
be more useful for a GM and padding to be skimmed through 
by a player .  
Information in this document can include:

•  How to build a Character, how to build a Pokemon, available 
Classes, etc
GM Guide
This  Document  contains  all  the  “Soft Rules” of  the 
System. The GM Guide is focused on information that 
is necessary for a GM to know in order to run the PTE 
System. 
These however can be deviated from depending on the 
discretion of  the  GM  and how they wish to run  their 
game,  allowing  PTE  to  be  narratively flexible  on  how 
outcomes are determined. These are a compilation of 
best  practices  however  and  provide  frameworks  on 
how a GM can run certain parts of their Campaign and 
it is ultimately how we feel PTE should be ran. Players 
should  also  read  the  GM  Guide  if  they  want  a  full 
understanding of the system but it is separated for the 
sake of digestibility. 
Information in this document can include:

•  Campaign Types, Alternate Pokemon templates, Tips 
on running PTE, Campaign Tools, etc
Documentation Links

• Digital Character Sheet - This document is where you’ll 
record all of your Character’s information when making a 
Trainer . 

• PTE Pokedex - This document has all information 
regarding statting Pokemon in PTE.

• GM Guide - This document is essential and must be read 
by GMs in order to run PTE, containing a lot of other crucial 
information listed below.

• Attacks & Ability Reference List - All Attacks & Abilities 
are listed here with information of their effects, etc.

• Homebrew Compilation - All Homebrew, official or 
otherwise, is listed here. This includes official modules 
listed in the PTE Roadmap when completed.

• PTE Linktree  - Most important files are collected under 
our linktree for organization. Great for quick access!
As  a  Player  and  GM  of  the  PTE  system,  a  lot  of 
information about specifics in the system are relocated 
in  other  documents  to  keep  everything  organized. 
In  my opinion,  this  is  essential to keep the  system as 
streamlined as  possible  and  to  prevent the  size from 
being  intimidating.  The  amount  of  people  i’ve  seen 
turned away from a 500+ Page book is numerous. 
Half of the Documents are also organized into Google 
spreadsheets (Excel) because the information is easier 
to  update  and  add  to  over  time  that  way  without 
people  needing  to  redownload  their  documentation. 
In  addition,  it  allows for data to  be  pulled  directly to 
the Digital Character Sheet. 
Please download or bookmark the following documents 
as  supplemental  PDFs  that  contain  the  rest  of  PTE’s 
Content. 
Click the blue text to go to the linked documents.
Rule Book vs GM Guide
System Documentation

title: Chapter 1 - System Intro (p.7)
body:
77
Chapter 1 - System Intro
77
Path of Elementalism 
This Module will provide a list of rules and bonus classes if you want an elemental facet in your Campaign, allowing 
Trainers to channel the elements. Similar to the Elementalist Classes in Game of Throhs, this will provide a similar 
framework but structured as a toolbox class rather than a set of predefined features. These classes give you tools to 
express your preferred style of Elemental powers.
Status - Complete [Link]
Path of the Mundane 
This Module will cover how to run a Campaign without Trainer’s being a Fighter in combat. These Campaigns will 
be more centric on the anime similarly to PTA and be solely Pokemon Support while Trainers are on the backline. 
The basis of PTE is that Pokemon Trainers contribute to the fight, usually physically, but this Module will enable 
Campaigns that do not have Trainers being a physically active combatant. 
Status - Temporary [Link]
Path of Occultism 
This Module will provide a list of rules and bonus classes or mechanics if you want occult facets in your
Campaign, allowing Trainers to gain supernatural powers. This will introduce a plethora of ways to use Occult 
Education which can be plugged into your campaign based on its setting and worldbuilding. This can include 
elements such as Oracles with Divination, Arcanists that master Arcane Weapons, Warpers that can teleport, or even 
Chronomancers that control Time.
Status - Complete [Link]
Path of the Divine 
This Module will reintroduce Legendary Pokemon that have powers beyond just normal Pokemon. It will include 
gifts that they can bestow, tiers of legendary strength, and ways to introduce legends as divine bosses. It will include 
methods of servitude and interacting with Legendaries in a divine manner , like patronage or usurpation.
Status - Not Started
Path of the Artisanry 
This Module provides anin depth system of jobs and professions that can expand character depth and introduce 
systems that let Characters interact with economic aspects of their Character . GMs can use parts of this module 
that are relevant to their Players such as a Brewing system for an Alchemist or Archeology for a Paleontologist. This 
Module includes elements such as Breeding, Farming, Fossils, Fishing, Cooking, Enchanting, Alchemy, etc.
Status - Not Started
Path of Lethality 
This Module will provide rules on how to run harder and more lethal campaigns where death and injury is fully
expected. It will also introduce less desired systems that tend to be loved by niche audiences such as attrition 
mechanics or more in depth Injuries.
Status - Complete [Link]
Path of Eras 
This Module will cover any facet of a Campaign with relevancy based on the age its played in, primarily ancient past 
and distant future. Tech Education will gain many ways of being used as GMs can use this Module to do high tech 
campaigns and Players can be put to the test if they’re thrown in an ancient world without modern technology such 
as the Pokeball. Classes and concepts will be introduced such as hacking, high tech weapons and even space travel 
or augmentation.
Status - Not Started
Book of Pokemon Gimmicks
This Module will cover all of the various Pokemon Gimmicks that have been added over the years and how to 
implement them into your Campaign. This includes Megas, Terastralizing, Z-Moves, Burst Pokemon, Contests, 
Shadow Pokemon, Totem Pokemon, Rangers, Dynamaxing, etc. As of right now they have temporary Items that can 
be implemented with GM nuance.
Status - Not Started
PTE Modules

title: Chapter 1 - System Intro (p.8)
body:
88
Chapter 1 - System Intro
8
System Terminology
We use a lot of short hand so things may be hard to understand as a new player just learning PTE. In this section we’ll 
list some common terminology that can be found. If you wish to gain more information, search this book for the listed 
term. If there’s any you feel should be added, let us know!
We highly  encourage you  to  jump  around the  book  to  read  different sections  to  gain a  total understanding. For 
example,  a  lot  of  Talents refer  to  other  game  mechanics  being  affected,  especially  Downtime  rules,  which  are 
explained in a further chapter .   
Abbreviations
PTE = Pokemon Tabletop Evolution
PTU = Pokemon Tabletop United
PTA = Pokemon Tabletop Adventures
Feat = Feature
SP = Spirit Point
CR = Challenge Rating
TN = Target Number
AC = Accuracy Check
DB = Damage Base
CS = Combat Stage
PC = Player Character
NPC = Non-Player Character
STAB = Same Type Attack Bonus
DR = Damage Reduction
Eo T = Every other Turn
Ao O = Attack of Opportunity 
Tick = 1/10 of someone’s Total Hit Points
6 m = 6 Meters
Terms 
Default Value = The Default Value of all Combat Stages are +0 CS. 
Some Features and other Effects may alter this and set or increase 
it to a different value like +1. If two sources would set the value, set 
it to the higher value. 
Naturally & Natural = It has not been altered by any source. 
Naturally Ground Type means nothing altered it to become Ground 
Type. A Natural 11 on an Accuracy Roll means that a roll that was a 
9 but had a +2 Accuracy Modifier does not mean it’s a Natural 11. 
Same concept as “Dirty 20 vs Nat 20 in D&D”
Uncapped = This allows a modifier to exceed the maximum limit of 
a specified Combat Value. 
Damaging = Either Physical or Special. Basically shorthand for 
saying “Not Status and does Damage”
Slide = Forced Movement that doesn’t provoke Attacks of 
Opportunity and does not count towards the maximum movement 
per turn.
Turn & Initiative = A Player’s Turn Starts when they use their first 
Action during the Initiative that they chose to act in. An Initiative 
Starts when a Party decides which two Combatants will act. The 
Initiative and Turns ends when both acting Combatants decide they 
no longer wish to use their Actions and take their Turn, or have 
used all desired Actions. The Term Initiative is usually mentioned 
when it’s referring to both acting Combatants and the Term Turn 
is usually mentioned when something only applies to one of the 
acting Combatants. However, they are usually interchangeable.

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation
body:
Starting your first character can be rough! Especially in a system that has vast customization as one of its foundational 
principles, it may be hard to find out where to start. In this section we’ve laid out a few tips on what to do. 
99
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
First Character Tips
9
1. Read this Chapter in detail 
The Character Creation Chapter has listed out in detail how to build a 
Character, including some examples so don’t skim it! There’s also a check list 
under this section for Character Creation.
2. Consider an Archetype 
In the Trainer Archetype Examples Section, we’ve listed out a few general 
ideas for a Trainer to be built around. If you’re running low on ideas or want 
to emulate a character in the Pokemon Series, check out that section for 
a template! Each Archetype includes Skills that are essential to them and 
possible classes you could take if you want your character to be like that.
3. Create a rough Character Plan 
Before I set anything in stone, I usually plan out my character and how 
they’d shape out in the early stages of the Campaign. This includes at 
least 2 concrete Classes that shape their identity and 4 Skills that I 
know I want to focus on improving. Planning this much out gives me a 
solid basis of who my Character is while still being flexible enough to 
adapt in the Campaign.
4. Ask other Players what they want to do 
Having a balanced party is essential to the group of players 
performing well, regardless of the game you play. You wouldn’t 
want to have a party with 2-3 Clerics in D&D so consider the 
same when making a Character in PTE. If other players have 
a solid idea of what they want their character to be, start 
forming ideas of what build would fill in potential weaknesses 
of the party. If one Player wants their central classes to be 
Taskmaster and Berserker, they’ll be very offensive and 
reckless in nature so perhaps you can counter it with a 
Provocateur Class and be more social in nature? Or maybe 
play as a leader with Commander!
5. Pay attention to Action Usage 
Once you start getting experienced with building Characters, 
especially in PTU, you’ll start to factor in the action usage of a 
Class so keep that in mind when making choices. Does this Class 
have too many standard actions? Classes like Empath tend to be 
very action heavy so pairing it with classes like Fighter who want to 
use their Standard Action to attack may not be the best idea. If you 
have an action heavy class you may want to look at some classes 
with the static frequency so you have more passive elements and 
your Classes don’t clash with each other .
6. Don’t worry about Mistakes 
There’s a section in the GM Guide regarding the idea of “Retraining” 
or redoing aspects of your Character as you learn the system. This is to 
be expected and only natural for new players!

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.10)
body:
1010
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
Step 6 - Determine your Characteristics 
As with your Concept and Background, lay out what your 
Trainer’s  Characteristics  may  be.  Characteristics  include 
their  narrative  Backstory,  their  Personality  Traits,  their 
Goals,  Desires,  Strengths,  Flaws,  Virtues,  Key  Principles, 
and any existing bonds or ties to other Trainers or NPCs. 
This doesn’t have to be extensive! Just write down a few 
foundational notes and add to it over time and as you play 
with the Trainer more. 
Step 7 - Assign your Combat Stats 
Level 1 Trainers have 10 Level-Up Stat Points to distribute 
as  they  wish  among  their  Stats,  but  remember  that  this 
system utilizes the  Glass  Cannon  Clause:  you  cannot  put 
more than 50% of your Level-Up Stat Points (rounded up) 
into a Stat. 
Step 8 - Choose your Starter Pokemon
Your GM will set guidelines for which Pokémon you can pick 
from as a Starter . It might be as simple as any traditional 
Starter, as  from  the  games,  or  your  choices  might  span 
every Underdog Pokemon. You could even be allowed to 
start with multiple Pokemon! Be sure to ask if you’re not 
told!
Step 9 - Determine your starting Wealth
Your GM might set a starting Wealth or give you starting 
Items at the beginning of your Campaign. Talk to your GM 
and determine how much money your Trainer starts with 
and what items they start with. You may even be allowed 
to look through the Item Index and pick what you want!
Step 1 - Learn the Character Sheet 
Thanks to automation and Google Sheets, the Character 
Sheet  is  able  to  streamline  all  information  regarding 
your character . Go  through each  Tab and  get familiar 
with what each cell does, and don’t edit the ones with 
code in them unless you know what you’re doing. Cells 
that are editable will be the lightest shade of blue as an 
indicator! Click here for the Sheet.
Step 2 - Think of a Character Concept 
One of the more prominent parts of Character-building 
is having a concept. If you have an idea for a character, 
you’ll have a better understanding of what mechanics 
you want them to have, which can help with selecting 
Talents and Features.
Step 3 - Create a Background 
A  Background,  or  backstory,  is  pretty  important  to 
characters in PTE. This includes your Skill Background, 
which consists of raising one Skill to Adept, three Skills 
to Novice, and lowering three Skills to Pathetic to show 
what your character is already good at and what they’re 
already not as good at. As a reminder, it’s also always 
nice  to  have reference art  for your  character, as  that 
might help you visualize their backstory a little better .
Step 4 - Choose Talents 
You  gain  2  Talents for  which  you  qualify  at  Level  1.   
Talents tend  to  lean  toward  the  domain  of  granting 
Capabilities,  expanding  your  Skills  or  even  tweaking 
them, and overall providing non-combat utility. When 
in doubt, choose a Skill Specialty! 
Step 5 - Choose Features 
You gain four Features at level 1, selecting them from 
Classes or General Features that you qualify for .  
Character Creation Checklist
Making a Character may be a lot to digest, especially if you’re new to the system, so in this section we’ll go over 
each individual aspect of creating a Character, from the Sheet to your mechanics. Consider this chapter a step-by-
step guide on creating a Character .

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.11)
body:
1111
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
Your Fluff Background consists of the remainder of your 
Background. This includes your: 

• Backstory, Personality Traits, Strengths & Flaws, Goals 
and  Desires,  Virtues,  Key  Principles,  and  Bonds  and 
Relationships with others. 
You do not need to have a super detailed background 
at  the  start, as  part  of  the  fun  is  discovering how  the 
character  would  react  when  presented  with  certain 
situations, however you should have enough of a basis 
to give yourself a foundation on how to roleplay as that 
character .
Try to have at least one small fact about each section, 
then a decent summary of the history and backstory of 
your Character . Coordinate these with your GM as it will 
give them ways to incorporate your character into the 
setting.  
Talents and Features
Talents and Features  are a  major  part  of  your Trainer 
and the brunt of all mechanics your Trainer can perform. 
This page consists of a brief explanation of each of the 
two, but if you want a greater explanation you should 
check out their respective chapters.
 
You start with two Talents at Level 1. Talents are slightly 
Mechanical but mostly Fluff-based, granting Capabilities, 
expanding  and  tweaking  your  Skill  set,  and  providing 
utility  that  can  be  used  outside  of  combat.  Talents 
may also be obtained by forgoing a Skill Rank increase 
whenever you level up if desired but you get two for free 
at the start!  Be sure to check the Prerequisites on the 
Talent to ensure you qualify.
You also start with four Features.   The  four Features 
you choose  may either  be  General Features for which 
you  qualify  or  taken from  Classes,  provided  you  meet 
the prerequisites. Class Features tend to be the primary 
use  for  Feature  slots,  as  they  grant  the  most  combat 
utility, but General Features provide you with a host of 
other  options  that  a  Class  might  not.  When  choosing 
what Features to take, first look at the section on How to 
understand PTE, so you know what benefits it provides 
in combat and the restrictions, such as only being able 
to take Features from 4 Classes in total.  
Your Character Concept
You may feel tempted to immediately jump to crunching 
the  numbers  and  optimizing  your  Trainer,  especially 
if  you’re  an  experienced  roleplayer . Don’t  yet!  At 
minimum, skim through the Rule Book and get an idea 
of what’s available before coming up with a concept for 
your character .
Your  Character  Concept  is  the  foundation  for  your 
character, so  take  as  much  time  as  you  want  to  plan 
it  out.  Alternatively, you  could  start  with  a  simple  or 
basic concept but expand it as your trainer progresses, 
depending on your campaign’s setting. 
If  you  need  assistance  in  what  kind  of  Characters can 
be  made,  there  is  a Trainer Build Examples section 
that shows a Character being built from the ground up 
and  the  decisions  being  made  when  building  them.  In 
addition you could look in the Trainer Archetype Section 
to get some insight in how they could be built if you have 
an idea in mind. 
Your Character Background
Your  Background  encompasses  many  factors,  a  small 
number  of  which  include  mechanics  and  the  majority 
of  which  are  tied  to  your  character’s fluff,  or  roleplay 
facets. 
Your  Mechanical Background consists  of  your  Skill 
Background,  which  is  a  depiction  of  your  character’s 
strengths and flaws in the Skill System when they start 
their  journey. Refer to the Skills Section  for a  more in 
depth  list  of  skills  and  their  ranks,  but  they  represent 
the training that your character uses to interact with the 
world, as well as incorporating a Trainer’s natural talent 
in certain fields. 
Choosing your Skill Background is basically determining 
what  your  Trainer  inherently  excels  at  and  struggles 
with. At the start of Character Creation you choose the 
following:
 

• One Skill to raise to Adept Rank
 

• Three Skills to raise to Novice Rank
 

• Three Skills to lower to Pathetic Rank
Once chosen, adjust their Rank value accordingly and list 
them in your Skill Background in your Trainer Tab. 
Character Creation Steps

title: Example - The Party graduated from the Pokemon Academy and
body:
GM Note - You should usually allow your Trainers to all start from 
a Supported Trainer wealth or average out their wealth. If Players 
start at different levels, obtain their consent to do so so there’s 
little starting disparity. Some players enjoy rags to riches so they 
may be fine with it.
Example - The Party graduated from the Pokemon Academy and 
were sponsored by Professor Oak, getting ample resources and a 
rare starter each!
1212
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
12
Your Starting Wealth & Items
Your  GM  will  also  determine  how  affluent  your 
Character  is  upon  starting  their  Campaign.  This  is 
heavily dependent on the setting and GM negotiations 
but  below  are  three  common  levels  that  they  could 
choose from if they desired.
Fresh Trainer -  Fresh  Trainers are  any  Character that 
is  either  starting  their  journey  without  any  support 
or  does  not  have  access  to  any  source  of  resources 
as  they  begin  the  campaign.  This  could  be  a  Trainer 
from a poor village or someone who was abandoned 
by family to go off on their own. If this is the starting 
line, these Trainers start with $1,000 - $2,000 worth of 
Money or Items whose value equals this range. If they 
are a combat trainer, they would likely have a Training 
Weapon,  being  very  crude.  They  would  likely  only 
have one Pokemon of very common origins. This could 
include starters limited to their home, limited to what 
they come across or basics like Pidgey or Gastly.  
Supported Trainer -   Supported  Trainers  are  any 
Character  they  either  are  starting  from  an  easier 
starting point or have some support network so they 
start with more resources. This could be a Trainer who’s 
been given basic supplies from their family or a Trainer 
who’s older and worked a bit to gain some resources of 
their own. If this is the starting line, these Trainers start 
with $3,000 - $5,000 worth of Money or Items whose 
value  equals  this  range. If  they  are  a  combat  trainer, 
they would likely have a simple Weapon to start with. 
They would likely have 1-2 starters or one starter that 
can be from common to uncommon origins. This could 
include Pokemon like Doduo or Phantump. 
Privledged Trainer -  Privileged  Trainers  are  any 
Character that is starting with affluence of some kind 
and  have  a  solid  support  network  for  them  to  start 
their  journey.  This  could  include  a  Trainer  who  has 
come from a wealthy side of town or lives in a well off 
community. If this is the starting line, these Trainers start 
with $3,000 - $8,000 worth of Money or Items whose 
value  equals  this  range. If  they  are  a  combat  trainer, 
they would likely have a simple weapon to start with. 
They would likely have 1-3 starters or 1-2 starters from 
common  to  rare origins.  This  could  include  Pokemon 
like Dratini or Yamask.
Your Combat Stats
Combat Stats are simple to change. Simply access your 
Combat  Tab  and  distribute  your  remaining  Level-Up 
Points into the Level-Up Cells on your Stats. Remember 
the Glass Cannon Clause: you cannot put more than 
50% of your Level-Up Stat Points into a Stat. As such, 
at Level 1, you may not put more than 5 Level-Up Stat 
Points  into  any  one  Stat.  Later  in  the  book  there’s a 
section for Combat Stats which has a full explanation 
if you wish to know what each Stat can do before you 
invest in it. 
Your Starter Pokemon
Once your Trainer’s attributes have been set up, now 
is the time to choose your Starting Pokemon! This is a 
conversation your GM will likely have with you on what 
your limitations could be for choosing one. 
Some  may  have  a  selective  pool  of  Starters or  some 
may  allow  access  to  any  number  of  Pokemon  as  a 
starter despite not being a canon Starter, such as Gastly 
or Nidoran. After your GM confirms your Starter, you 
can stat them like any normal Pokemon (Refer to those 
sections if need be). 
This  will  usually  consist  of  setting  up  their  inherit 
information  like  their  Name,  Combat  Stats,  Gender, 
Starting Attacks, Ability and Role! Refer to the Pokedex 
for this information.

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.13)
body:
1313
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
13
Trainer Creation Examples
Learning a new Tabletop System is difficult, we get it! This section 
will go through the Character Creation Checklist and create a 
Character so you can have concrete example on how to build one. 
Concept #1 - Theodore Wilson
1. Create a Character Concept
The Campaign this Character is for is set in the Sinnoh  region. 
I’ve looked through the book briefly and decided on playing a 
Trainer who was a Ranger from Snowpoint City and a nature 
conservationist. With this idea in mind it can determine every other 
facet of Theo. 
2. Create a Background
I decide to make my mechanical background first. I decide to 
make Nature Education my Adept Skill considering he knows a lot 
about the wild. For my Novice Skills, I decided to pick Athletics, 
Acrobatics and Command. Athletics and Acrobatics cover Theo 
being physically fit from being an outdoorsy character and 
Command can display his confidence and control over his Pokemon. 
For his Pathetic Skills I decide to lower Tech Edu, Focus and 
Intimidate. Tech Edu was lowered because he has a difficult time 
learning new tech and no interest. Focus was due to me deciding 
he was more scatterbrained and easily distracted. Intimidate was 
because I decided he was good at being a leader but wasn’t good at 
being threatening. 
For my fluff background, I decided to make a few additional notes 
about Theo. One was that he’s never been outside of Snowpoint 
due to his family’s religious obligations and longs to explore nature. 
Another was deciding that he has an intense rebellious spirit and 
will go against any organization to do what’s right. Lastly I decided 
that he would be a very confident personality and the leader of any 
party if given the chance to be.
3. Choose Talents
Now that i have a decent idea of how Theo will be played, it’s time 
to choose my Level 1 Talents! I skimmed through the list and wrote 
down all the possible Talents I would like on this Character . 
This includes 

• Confident, Home Advantage, Scavenger, Survivalist,  
Wild Companion and Wild Instincts. 
That’s a lot to narrow down! I decide to cross out Wild Companion 
and Wild Instincts due to the lack of exposure Theo would’ve had 
to Pokemon while in nature. After mulling it over some, I decide 
to take the Confident Talent so he has an easier time with social 
checks! Considering that I have novice Command, I qualify to take 
this! For my second Talent I decide to choose Home Advantage 
and choose Tundra for the Terrain, considering he grew up in 
Snowpoint. I decide to take Nature Researcher later so I get the 
Naturewalk I need to qualify for this! Doens’t matter if I do the steps 
out of order .

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.14)
body:
1414
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
14
4. Choose Features 
Now it’s time to take my 4 Starting Features! For these, I can choose 
either from the General Features or from any Class.
 Firstly I skim through the General Features and decide that I don’t want 
Theo to directly deal damage, but instead support his allies. With this in 
mind, I take the Assistive Combat General Feature to allow me to learn 
the Helping Hand and Coaching Attack, which will give me something to 
do in combat! I skimmed the rest of the General Features and nothing 
stood out to me immediately so now I decided to look through Classes. 
Immediately, two classes stood out as fitting my concept, Ranger 
and Nature Researcher . So for my second Feature I take the Nature 
Researcher Feature, taking one of my four possible [Classes] in the 
process. Because I took that Feature, its effects allow me to gain the 
Naturewalk Capability for Terrain of my choice, so I decided that Tundra 
would be the best fit, so I noted having Naturewalk (Tundra) in my 
Combat Page. 
For my third Feature, I decided that another feature under Nature 
Researcher stood out to me, being Survival Instincts. I also qualify for 
this because I have Adept Nature Edu from my background and I have 
the Nature Researcher Feature. Its effects allow me to cure myself of a 
Status Affliction and have a bonus if I’m in Tundra Terrain, which may be 
rare but fits Theo’s resilient nature! 
Lastly I decide to take the Ranger Feature, which counts as my second 
out of four Classes I can take. This lets me gain the Ranger Styler with 
its effect! Not only that but it grants a bonus while I have it equipped, 
which is great because I don’t have a lot of items yet.  
5. Assign Combat Stats
I now get to assign 10 Level-Up Stat Points to Theo. Considering he 
won’t be dealing damage in combat, I know Attack and Special Attack 
will be useless. I decided to put 5 Points in HP and 5 in Speed. The 
Speed will account for his nimbleness and allow him to have 2 Speed 
Evasion and the points in HP will make him more difficult to faint. 
6. Choose a Starter
I know I want something local to Snowpoint city because he was unable 
to leave the city so I decided on a Cubchoo!
7. Determine a Starting Wealth & Items
Considering my origins, I spoke to my GM and we decided I would be a 
Fresh Trainer for my wealth level, having about $2,000 to start and no 
Training Weapon considering my aversion to inflicting harm on others. 
My GM allows me to purchase items before the campaign starts so I 
decide to spend $1,000 on a Light Armor, so I can be slightly tankier to 
start since I would’ve had some equipment when I explored the wild. 
Then I decide to buy 2 Basic Healing Potions and a Pokeball to spend 
the last $1,000, just for basic supplies. And with that, Theo the Ranger 
is created!

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.15)
body:
1515
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
15
The first Trainer is created! How about we try another one out? Here’s 
the next concept. 
Concept #2 - Olivia Harper
1. Create a Character Concept
For my next character, let’s say this Campaign takes place in a Pokemon 
Academy that’s a college equivalent for advanced Trainers who want to 
take battling to the professional level! This will take place in Kalos so I 
decided to create a Trainer named Olivia Harper . She’s from a wealthy 
family in Lumiose City and her parents are tycoons in the real estate 
industry. 
2. Create a Background
I decide to make my mechanical background first. For my Adept Skill, I 
decided to take Command. Considering her background, I’ll treat her as 
being highly educated and an expert at battling, not to mention she has 
a controlling personality so Command could be her social skill of choice. 
For her Novice Skills, I decided to take Charm, Poke Edu and Focus. 
Charm will be because of her popular nature and ability to sway others. 
Pokemon Education will be because she’s well versed and studies 
battling as her profession. Lastly, Focus was chosen due to her ability to 
be studious. For her Pathetic Skills, I decided to take Intuition, Stealth 
and Acrobatics. Intuition is because I see her as fairly dense and thick 
headed. Stealth is because she has no sense of her surroundings and 
isn’t secretive at all. Acrobatics is because she is not athletically skilled 
and is clumsy. 
For my fluff background, I decided to add a few more notes to her . One 
is that she prefers to train Psychic Type Pokemon due to their cute but 
powerful nature. Another was deciding that she’s a Teacher’s Pet and 
will stop at nothing to achieve her goals, including being top at class. 
Lastly, I chose to make a list of enemies she would have in school, mostly 
for petty reasons which could all be negative bonds the GM uses to 
annoy her . 
3. Choose Talents
Next up is talents! I’m still mulling over a direction for her Classes to go 
so I’ll choose this first and skim through the list. The following Talents 
below are all ones I think would fit her . 
This Includes

•  Confident, Fashionista, Manipulator, Natural Beauty,   
Pokemon Trainer and Researcher
That’s a lot to choose from! While all of these stick out, I talked to my 
GM for a bit and we had the idea to take Researcher. We agreed that 
Olivia could be able to perform the Innovate Downtime Action in order 
to create custom [Orders] and Attacks to teach her Pokemon and her 
Allies’ Pokemon, so the Talent would grant a bonus! For the second 
Talent I decide that she takes the Fashionista Talent, qualifying with 
Focus. This is so she can make cute outfits for her Pokemon.

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.16)
body:
1616
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
16
4. Choose Features 
Now it’s time to take my 4 starting features! Firstly, I skim through the 
General Features. I find the following General Features interesting to 
take but I don’t take any yet. I noted them down as options down the 
line but I want to look at Classes first. 
This Includes

•  Alluring Combat, Commanding Trainer, Focused Commander, Skill 
Consistency (Command or Poke Edu)
Next I skim through Classes to see what kind of identity I want for Olivia, 
as there are multiple directions I could go. The following classes I could 
see Olivia take:
This includes

•  Commander, Strategist, Training Specialist, Duelist, Psychic Specialist, 
Provocateur, Debonair
Clearly, this is too many classes and I can’t take them all since I can only 
take from a maximum of 4 Classes. At this point I need to narrow down 
an identity for Olivia. I ruled out Psychic Specialist because I think it’s 
just a preference for her, not a focus for her team. When it comes to 
combat, I think she would prioritize [Orders] on her allies to control the 
battle rather than using social moves to torment enemies. With this 
in mind I then ruled out Provocateur since that is more generic social 
gameplay. Lastly I ruled out Commander since I don’t want her to have 
too many [Orders], but the features from Strategist will give her enough 
to do in battle. 
With this narrowed down, I decide her final build will be Strategist, 
Training Specialist, Duelist and Debonair. This allows her primary role 
in battle to be handing out orders and enacting strategy but on the side 
she can use her feminine wiles to manipulate her enemies, as Debonair 
has some passive and lower action Features. Now it’s time to select her 
Features!
I decided that in the early game I’ll focus more on her commanding side, 
then develop the charming side later, as I don’t currently qualify for 
Debonair or the Social Features. The first Feature I took was the Training 
Specialist Feature. This allows me to improve the Default Combat Value 
of some of my Pokemon, then grants me my first Class. 
Considering I have Adept Command, I also decided to take the Signature 
Technique Feature from the Training Specialist Class. This allows me 
to grant my Pokemon custom attack modifications and improve their 
combat output! 
For my third Feature, I decided to take the Strategist Feature. This 
lets me use Orders as a free action sometimes when i plan out the 
battlefield accordingly.
 For my last Feature, I decided to take the Initiate Protocol Feature. This 
allows me to have more [Orders] I can perform at a low level.

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.17)
body:
1717
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
17
5. Assign Combat Stats
I now get to assign 10 Level-Up Stat Points to Olivia. Her role in combat 
is shooting out Orders and sometimes being social and applying Mental 
Afflictions to enemies, so she doesn’t need Attack or Special Attack. I 
decided to put 5 Points in HP so she can be slightly bulkier and 5 Points 
into Special Defense considering I feel as though her mind is firm and 
resolute. I could add more into speed later but that’s not as important

6. Choose a Starter
With the amount of affluence her family has she could likely pick any

7. Determine a Starting Wealth & Items
Considering her origins, the GM agreed that she could start as a

considering her aversion to physical combat. However, I do come to the 
conclusion that she would be adept at playing the Violin, so the GM 
agrees to let me spend $3,000 for a Bardic Instrument with the Heal 
Bell and Screech Attacks being applied to it. I then ask to buy some 
[Small] Stylish Clothes for $2,000 which I choose to be an accessory for

And with that, Olivia the Commanding Beauty has been created, with 
a full Build planned of Strategist, Debonair, Training Specialist 
and Duelist!

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.18)
body:
1818
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
18
The Athlete
The Athlete is a Trainer who prioritizes physical prowess 
and excels in their combat abilities. Unlike other Trainers, 
they  great  not  in  commanding  pokemon,  but  fighting 
alongside  them  and  being  able  to  fend for themselves 
when push comes to shove. 
Key Skills - Acrobatics, Athletics, Combat, Focus 
Recommended Classes - Defender, Fighter, Marksman, 
Strider
Character Examples - Brawly, Korrina
Summary
Skills like Acrobatics and Athletics are the embodiment 
of your physical form and depending on if you’re more 
nimble or bulky, should be taken to represent your 
athletic prowess. Combat would express your ability to 
perform combat maneuvers which is your experience at 
fighting rather than your physical strength. Focus would 
be a representation of your discipline as an athlete and 
your fortitude. 
The Recommended Core Classes are all dependent on 
your preferred style of fighting which we recommend 
at least one Advanced class be your specialty. Examples 
include being a Defender, to represent a physical 
bulkiness and devotion to endurance. Fighter, which 
demonstrates your offensive capabilities to strike down 
others in a fight up close and personal. Marksman could 
be for Trainers with more of a perceptive mastery for 
ranged combat. Lastly, Strider can be a representation 
of acrobatic prowess and being a nimble athlete.
The Adventurer
The Adventurer is a Trainer who is driven by a sense of 
wanderlust and exploration, one who is most likely to 
partake in a journey, having no other roots to attach 
themselves  to  besides  a  passion  for excitement and 
discovery. These  types  of  Trainers are  characterized 
by their curiosity, adaptability and knowledge of the 
world outside civilized society.
Key Skills - Poke Edu, Nature Edu, Gen Edu, 
Perception
Recommended Classes - Nature Researcher, Training 
Specialist, General Researcher, Nomad, Musician, 
Chronicler 
Character Examples - Ash Ketchum, Goh
Summary
Skills like Poke Edu and Nature Edu can explain your 
expertise with exploring out in the wild. Gen Edu 
can explain your Trainer’s array of knowledge from 
traveling multiple places. Lastly, Perception could 
show your Trainer’s alertness due to traveling.
Classes like Nature Researcher can grant the 
adventurer Nature Walks, the ability to set traps 
in the wild, and the ability to adapt to their 
surroundings based on terrain they’ve experienced 
in the past. Training Specialist would be common for 
Adventurers because of their reliance on Pokemon 
to aid them in the wild and their frequent exposure. 
General Researcher could display the Trainer’s vast 
array of talents and general knowledge from their 
past journeys. Nomad would allow the Trainer to 
carry more items and better utilize them in combat. 
Musician can be taken on more of a traveling 
vagabond that is more musically inclined and 
supportive in nature. Lastly, Chroniclers specialize 
in taking notes on things they encounter and could 
represent a trainer who explores a lot. 
Trainer Archetype Examples
In this section we’ll list out some Archetype Examples of themes you could build your Character around in case you 
need some ideas.

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.19)
body:
1919
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
19
The Caretaker
The  Caretaker  is  a  Trainer  that  prioritizes  the  well-
being  and  development  of  others  around  them  above 
themselves.  They  tend  to  have a  nurturing  nature and 
ultimately have the desire to be a support for their party, 
helping everyone achieve through their specialties.
Key Skills - Charm, Intuition, Med Edu, Poke Edu
Recommended Classes - Motivator, Apothecary, 
Empath, Defender, Pokemon Researcher
Character Examples - Brock, Nurse Joy
Summary
Skills like Charm can be used to display your character’s 
outwardly warmness towards others along with their 
empathy. Intuition could be raised due to their innate 
ability to sense what is wrong with others around them. 
Med Edu could be taken if your character tends to care 
for others through medical means such as a nurse or 
even basic medical knowledge! Poke Edu can be taken 
if your Trainer has more of a breeder background or has 
taken care of Pokemon in the past rather than other 
humans. 
Classes like Motivator can grant you supportive features 
that enable your allies to succeed! Apothecary can be 
taken if you have more of a medical background, helping 
you administer medicine better in combat. Empath can 
be taken if there is a supernatural sense behind your 
empathy, allowing you to sense the emotions of others. 
Lastly, Defender can be an option if your Trainer is 
athletically capable of being a guard to others, possibly 
taking the Sentinel Class as well if you’re a defender of 
the weak!
The Battler
The  Battler is  a  Trainer who  specializes  in  Pokemon 
Battles, even beyond other Trainers that casually have 
Pokemon companions. This rank of Trainer would be 
comparable to Ace Trainers and Champions who excel 
in knowledge of Pokemon and how to command them 
so that they never even need to step into the fray.
Key Skills - Command, Poke Edu
Recommended Classes - Commander, Training 
Specialist, Type Specialist, Battle Specialist
Character Examples - Cynthia, Leon, Gary Oak
Summary
Skills like Command display your ability to hold 
sway over others and demonstrate your ability to 
command Pokemon in combat. Poke Edu would also 
be very beneficial considering that you have a lot of 
exposure with battling with other Pokemon so you’d 
know some more uncommon knowledge that could 
be relevant to battles. 
The Recommended Core Classes are all Pokemon 
Based, as we’d recommend at least one Advanced 
class to be your specialty to show prowess as a 
battler. Examples include Commander, which you 
could show to display your ability to command others 
even beyond Pokemon. Training Specialist would be 
the most generic choice as it allows you to specialize 
Pokemon based on how you train. Lastly, Type 
Specialist could be an option, such as gym leaders 
having an affinity towards using certain Pokemon 
over their career as battlers.

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.20)
body:
2020
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
20
The Innovator
The  Innovator  is  a  Trainer  that  comes  from  a 
background  in  education  and  who  excels  in  the 
creation  of  items  that  can  assist  them  and  their 
party.  Most  commonly,  these  Trainers  excel  in 
technology  but  more  generally  specialize  in  a  field  
of study. 
Key Skills - Tech Edu, Perception, Focus
Recommended Classes - Tech Researcher, Artificer, 
Jailbreaker, Operator, Geneticist
Character Examples - Clemont, Colress
Summary
Skills like Tech Edu are your basic bread and butter 
ability to discern technology and create it at your 
whim, which is central to the Innovator archetype. 
Other education skills can be swapped in, such as an 
innovator specialized in the wild and plants would be 
good at Nature Edu . Perception could display your 
ability to find fine details which would be a common 
skill when making new inventions. Lastly, Focus is 
something any innovator would need when creating 
magnificent contraptions. 
Classes you could take depend on your field of 
innovation, most commonly it’d be Tech Researcher 
but it could be a class like Herbalist, one specialized in 
utilizing seeds in combat. Tech Researcher in general 
allows you to create gadgets that can help narratively, 
while their advanced classes specialize in other 
things. Artificer allows the trainer to specialize in type 
shards and create items that can utilize the elements. 
Lastly, Jailbreaker specializes in pokeball creation and 
manipulation. 
The Criminal
The Criminal is a Trainer with sketchy origins, usually 
having some sort of specialty that has strayed them 
from  the  path  of  being  law  abiding  in  society. This 
could be involvement with some villainous team or 
possibly straying from the path normal Trainers take 
for their own self interests.
Key Skills - Combat, Guile, Intimidate, Stealth
Recommended Classes - Alchemist, Rogue, 
Taskmaster, Trickster, Ruffian, Imposter, Geneticist
Character Examples - Team Rocket, Giovanni
Summary
Skills are highly dependent on your type of 
criminality. Skills like Combat could be used more 
for thugs and to show your ability to scrap in the 
field. Guile could be better for conmen and those 
who scam others easily. Intimidate is for criminals 
who frequently interact with normal civilians and 
use fear to get their way. Lastly, Stealth can be used 
for more covert criminals. 
Classes like Alchemist could be taken by criminals 
that specifically create their own illicit substances. 
Rogue and its advanced classes like Assassin, Ninja 
and Swashbuckler are a key part to any criminal’s 
skill set and could easily fit your build. Trickster 
could be for more guile focused Trainers, lying and 
manipulating their enemies. Taskmaster could 
focus on your rough treatment of your Pokemon, 
training them in a harsh manner. Ruffian could be 
for more intimidating Trainers that focus on benign 
an imposing figure. Lastly, Imposter can fulfill the 
fantasy of duplica or team rocket, specializing in 
guile and disguises.

title: Las
body:
Las
2121
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
21
The Performer
The  Performer is  a  Trainer who  captivates others  with 
their  skills  and  talents,  usually  having  some  basis  in 
beauty or entertainment in some cases. They often use 
their performative skills to assist them and shape their 
method of combat, usually on the defensive or support 
side. 
Key Skills - Acrobatics, Command, Charm, Guile 
Recommended Classes - Acrobat, Dancer, Motivator, 
Musician, Provocateur, Performer, Coordinator
Character Examples - Dawn, Nando, Wallace
Summary
Skills like Acrobatics allow your Trainer to be nimble, if 
that’s the style of performing the do, especially if they 
take classes like Strider. Charm allows them to excel at 
the art of performance and others being charmed by 
their skills. Command can lead your Trainer to having 
more of a presence on stage and represent their 
notoriety. Lastly, Guile allows more deceptive types of 
performances, possibly including magicians and con 
men! 
Classes like Acrobat and Dancer are more on the 
combat and acrobatics side of performance, allowing 
your Trainer to be more evasive and nimble in combat or 
support others through dance, respectively. Motivators 
are more on the charming side of performance to 
support allies. Musician allows the Trainer to gain bardic 
qualities and take music combat! Provocateur can allow 
performers to spice up their combat with verbal jabs 
and improve their social qualities such as becoming 
a Debonair to sway others. Lastly, Coordinator and 
Performer can help you with your more stylistic side, 
giving special techniques to Pokemon or gaining flair on 
the field!
The Mystic
The Mystic is a Trainer who specializes in the art of the 
occult, however that may manifest in your Campaign. 
Compared to physical attributes that Athlete Specialize 
in, the Mystic specializes in mental attributes.
Key Skills - Focus, Occult Education
Recommended Classes - Occult Researcher, Aura 
Guardian, Empath, Mystic, Type Specialist, Imposter
Character Examples - Sabrina, Morty
Summary
Skills like Occult Education are the basis of the 
Mystic, as they tend to specialize in one occult topic 
in one way or another. Whether its telekinesis, the 
art of empathic connections, aura, or even ghost type 
history, there’s bound to be knowledge that can be 
pursued. Lastly, Focus can be a good measure of the 
mental fortitude that a Mystic has. 
For Classes, you have various options that all depend 
on your occult specialty. Occult Researcher is a 
generic one that grants you some special supernatural 
abilities and empowers its Advanced Class. Mystic, 
however are Trainers that are born with innate 
supernatural abilities and can provide offensive 
support similar to Fighter. Some Advanced Class 
options are Aura Guardian which give you a mastery 
of Aura similar to Lucario or Empath which provide a 
connection to the minds of others around you. You 
also could do Sage which lets you protect others or 
Esper which gives you psychic abilities like Sabrina. 
You could also go the route of a Type Specialist like 
Fairy, Ghost or Psychic and specialize your knowledge 
based on Pokemon of that category. Lastly, you could 
go Imposter, which has a supernatural element of 
copying the attacks from your allies or enemies.

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.22)
body:
2222
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
22
The Ranger
The Ranger is a Trainer who is in tune with the wild around 
them and Pokemon life in their world. The abilities of a 
ranger vary depending on your definition but they often 
serve as protectors of nature and pokemonkind, doing 
their best to keep the peace as enforcers
Key Skills - Command, Perception, Nature Edu, Poke 
Edu
Recommended Classes - Nature Researcher, Hunter, 
Marksman, Ranger, Pokemon Researcher
Character Examples - Officer Jenny, Solana
Summary
Skills like Command can help your Trainer increase the 
authority they may command along with the respect 
others grant them. Perception can be helpful if you’re in 
the path of a marksman, using ranged weapons to easily 
spot danger. Nature Edu can display your knowledge of 
the natural world around you and Poke Edu can display 
your ability to train and command Pokemon. 
Classes like Nature Researcher can allow you to gain 
tools such as Naturewalks that increase your combat 
capabilities in certain environments you specialize in. 
Hunter could allow you to have better coordination 
with your Pokemon in combat. Lastly, Marksman could 
allow you access to ranged combat so you can enforce 
the peace easier and defend the weak!
The Protector
The  Protector  is  a  Trainer  who  excels  in  defending 
their  allies  and  has  a  sacrificial  spirit  at  heart.  They 
rarely  have  any  offensive  capabilities  and  tend  to 
devote their turn in combat to protecting those who 
can. These are the quintessential tanks of the party. 
Key Skills - Athletics, Combat, Command
Recommended Classes - Defender, Bulwark, 
Sentinel, Rider
Character Examples - Kiawe
Summary
Skills like Athletics and Combat easily show your 
Trainer’s bulkiness, endurance, and ability to 
withstand damage. Command could also be used for 
a leader that is more defensive, calling the shots as 
they protect their allies. 
Classes like Defender and all of their Advanced Classes 
are the primary skills you need to excel as a protector, 
as it grants you defensive tools to withstand hits as 
you intercept for allies. Bulwark can allow you to 
defend allies easier and control the battlefield, while 
Sentinel can retaliate against those who would harm 
their allies. Alternatively there are some classes like 
Rider which mechanically allow you to act alongside 
your Pokemon and protect each other when the 
scene is dangerous. As a protector, your primary goal 
is to Intercept and defend others.

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.23)
body:
2323
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
23
The Scholar
The  Scholar  is  a  Trainer whose  skills  come  from  their 
education and what they specialize in academically. This 
can  include  general  knowledge,  medical  knowledge, 
natural  knowledge,  occult  knowledge,  pokemon 
knowledge or technological knowledge. This tends to be 
the path of most professors in the Pokemon world. 
Key Skills - Any Edu Skill 
Recommended Classes - Type Specialist, Any 
Researcher, Battle Specialist, Geneticist
Character Examples - Any Professor
Summary
All Education Skills are core to the Scholar, they just 
need to pick which one they specialize in! 
Classes like Type Specialist can symbolize knowledge 
of training Pokemon of a specific type, such as gym 
leaders. Each Researcher class also has options you 
can go based on what edu skill you specialize in. For 
example, if you’re a medical scholar, you can go 
Medicine Researcher for generic tools that help with 
potion usage. You could also specialize as an Alchemist 
if your medical knowledge is more chemical in nature, 
allowing you to use malicious potions in battle. 
Alternatively you could be an Apothecary, specializing 
in restorative medicines that help your allies. 
The Rebel
The  Rebel  is  a  Trainer  who  defies  the  traditional 
norms  of  a  Pokemon Trainer  and  is  generally a  pain 
for others  to  be  on  a  team  with.  This  could  include 
how they train Pokemon, how they act in combat or 
general attitude towards the world around them.
Key Skills - Charm, Guile, Intimidate
Recommended Classes - Taskmaster, Musician, 
Ruffian, Rogue, Provocateur
Character Examples - Gladion, N
Summary
Skills like Charm, Guile and Intimidate are all social 
skills by which you can enact rebellion and sway 
others to join your ideals in some way. 
Classes you take depend on your style or rebellion 
and how you choose to act out against society in your 
setting. Some generic examples could be Taskmaster, 
which tends to train their pokemon harsher for a 
more disciplined Pokemon in battles. Musician could 
be a supportive rebel that uses the power of rock 
and roll songs to achieve their goals! Rogues tend to 
be more ferocious in nature, such as Swashbucklers 
living by their own creed and excelling in combat 
when they’re in more advantageous positions. Lastly, 
Provocateur classes tend to focus on social prowess 
in combat such as being a Trickster and manipulative 
rebel.

title: Chapter 2 - Character Creation (p.24)
body:
2424
Chapter 2 - Character Creation
24
The Tactician
The Tactician is a Trainer that specializes in quick wit and 
mastery over the battlefield. Their innovative strategies 
and  quick  thinking  help  them  adapt  to  anything  that 
occurs within a battle and they’re often leaders in their 
adventuring party.
Key Skills - Command, Intuition, Perception
Recommended Classes - Commander, Motivator, 
Strategist, Training Specialist, Battle Specialist
Character Examples - Steven Stone, Cynthia, Ash 
Ketchum
Summary
Skills like Command are essential to Tacticians, allowing 
them to more effectively order around those around 
them and convince them of their plans. Intuition helps 
the Trainer analyze the scenario around them, granting 
them additional information that others may miss! 
Perception can also be used to find small details that 
may influence their plans. 
Classes like Commander, Motivator and Strategist are 
all essential to this archetype, allowing them to have 
influence over their allies and help assist them in battle 
to succeed as a party! Lastly you could take a Training 
Specialist class or even something like Duelist to show 
your expertise over Pokemon. 
The Specialist
The Specialist is a Trainer who specializes in a specific 
category of Pokemon, whether the basis is a type, a 
species or genus. Examples could include a trainer who 
specializes  in  canines  like  Houndour  and  Greavard, 
a trainer who specializes in Fire Type Pokemon, or a 
Trainer who specializes specifically in Vivilon breeds. 
Key Skills - Poke Edu
Recommended Classes - Type Specialist, Training 
Specialist, Chronicler, Battle Specialist
Character Examples - Gym Leaders
Summary
Pokemon Education is the primary skill that links all 
Specialist Trainers, as they need extensive knowledge 
of their current obsession. 
Classes like Training Specialist would be appropriate 
for these Trainers, as they’re always exposed to 
Pokemon and likely have their own special way of 
training and caring for the Pokemon they study. 
Chronicler can also be an option as they’re likely 
used to studying Pokemon to fulfill their specialty. 
Lastly, Type Specialists help if a Specialist is focused 
on a specific type as it allows them to excel at utilizing 
them in combat or training with them.
