title: Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes (p.142)
body:
142142
Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes
Quick Footed 
Prerequisite: Skirmisher, Novice Acrobatics or Combat 
Scene x 2 - Swift or Movement Action 
Effect: Choose one of the Effects to apply:

• You ignore Movement Penalties this Round

• Enemies cannot Trigger Reactions against you until 
the end of your Turn. 

• You become cured of the Slowed Affliction or 
Trapped Condition

• You ignore Speed Evasion this Round
Opportunist
Prerequisite: Skirmisher, 2 Skirmisher Features, 
Expert Acrobatics or Combat
Static
Effect: You may perform Attacks of Opportunity when 
an Adjacent Enemy Disengages or misses an Attack 
against you. At any point you can spend a Movement 
Action to gain an additional Reaction this Round.
Tactical Striker
Prerequisite: Skirmisher, Adept Acrobatics or Combat
Static 
Effect: Whenever you hit a Damaging Attack against an 
Enemy, all Riposte and Tactics Maneuvers you use against 
them gain the Sureshot Keyword and you have a Boon to 
their Opposed Checks until the end of the Round. 
Blade Dancing
Prerequisite: Skirmisher, 3 Skirmisher Features, Master 
Acrobatics or Combat
Scene x 2 - Swift or Movement Action 
Effect: You may use an At-Will or EOT Damaging Melee Attack 
as a Free Action, however it is resisted by an additional 
damage step. You may only use this Feature once per Round. 
Skirmisher
[Advanced] [Class] 
Prerequisite 1: Strider [or]
Prerequisite 2: Adept Acrobatics or Combat
At-Will - Free Action 
Trigger: You use a Damaging Attack 
Effect: After the Triggering Attack resolves, you may 
Disengage as a Free Action. 
Bonus: Whenever you use the Disengage Maneuver you may 
instead move a number of spaces equal to half the higher of 
your Acrobatics or Combat Rank. 
Skirmishers are nimble fighters at heart. These Trainers live in the fray 
and jump all over the battlefield going from one target to the next. Speed 
is their specialty and they can use it to confound their enemies, perform 
quick strikes and prevent them from responding to your punches.
SKIRMISHER

title: Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes (p.143)
body:
Note - : Criminal Combat’s Novice Attack List is: 

•  Blindside, Feint Attack, Gash, Hone Claws, Sucker Punch, Thief
143143
Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes
ROGUE
Masters of the shadows, Trainers that are rogues are experts in 
criminal behavior and a sketchy style of fighting. Whether its the 
sacred art of a ninja or the underground workings of an assassin, or 
even the egotistical path of a swashbuckler, Rogues always play dirty.
Rogue 
[Base] [Class]
Prerequisite: Novice Stealth 
At-Will - Reaction 
Trigger: You hit a Damaging Attack against an Adjacent Enemy 
Effect: After the Attack’s Resolution, you may perform 
a Manipulate or Tactic Maneuver against one Target of 
the Triggering Attack as a Free Action, excluding Attack of 
Opportunity or Throw.
Bonus: You may learn two Attacks from the Criminal Combat 
Feature’s Novice Attack List. 
Sneak Attack
Prerequisite: Rogue, Novice Stealth
At-Will - Free Action 
Trigger: You hit a Damaging Attack against an Enemy 
that is Flanked, Vulnerable or Unaware of your 
presence.
Effect: The Triggering Attack has a Damage Bonus 
equal to your Tier Value. 
Criminal Specialty
Prerequisite: Rogue, 2 Rogue Features, Expert Stealth
Static 
Effect: Choose a listed Criminal Specialty to gain its 
associated Ability in the parenthesis. 

• Aggression (Defiant), Infiltration (Infiltrator), 
Intimidation (Intimidate), Manipulation (Analytic), 
Thievery (Pickpocket).
Hidden Shroud 
Prerequisite: Rogue, Adept Stealth
Scene x 2 - Free Action 
Trigger: You use the Hide Maneuver 
Effect: For the Duration of the Hide Maneuver or until 
you use an Attack (Whichever comes first), you become 
Untargetable. While Untargetable, Enemies are unaware of 
your presence. Enemies may use a Swift Action to perform 
a Perception or Intuition Check opposed by your Stealth. If 
they pass, they do not treat you as having the Untargetable 
Condition. 
Cunning Bladework
Prerequisite: Rogue, 3 Rogue Features, Master Stealth
Scene x 2 - Swift Action
Trigger: You hit a Damaging Attack against an Adjacent Enemy 
Effect: Before the Triggering Attack resolves, choose an 
effect to apply. An Enemy can only be affected by Cunning 
Bladework once per Scene:

• The Target gains the Wounded Affliction and cannot cure it 
for their next Save Check

• The Target becomes Slowed and Tripped

• The Attack is treated as Super Effective. This may only 
be applied if the Target has a Status Affliction or is 
under 50% HP .

title: Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes (p.144)
body:
144144
Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes
ASSASSIN
Fighters or Rogues that master the art of hunting down a single target 
can carry the name of an Assassin. As an assassin, they choose a 
target on the field to single out with a death mark. From then they can 
have high effectiveness with critical hits or massive damage on them.
Assassin 
[Advanced] [Class] 
Prerequisite 1: Rogue [or]
Prerequisite 2: Adept Combat or Stealth
At-Will - Swift Action 
Target: An Enemy you can see 
Effect: The Target makes an Intuition or Perception Check 
opposed by your Combat or Stealth. If they fail, they become 
Marked with your Death Mark. Whenever you use an Attack 
with its only Target having your Death Mark, Enemies other 
than the Target cannot Trigger Reactions against it. 
Fatal Expertise
Prerequisite: Assassin, Adept Combat or Stealth
Static 
Effect: Choose Shadows or Toxin. For each Assassin Feature 
you have, learn an Attack listed below. Whenever you gain an 
Assassin Feature, learn an Attack listed below. If you chose 
Shadows, all Damaging Attacks gained this way are Dark Type. 
If you chose Toxin, all Damaging Attacks gained this way are 
Poison Type. 

• Assassinate, Cross Poison, Night Slash, Camouflage, 
Sharpen, Mind Reader, Lock-On, Concentration, Gash, 
Hone Claws
Assassination
Prerequisite: Assassin, 3 Assassin Features, Master Combat 
or Stealth
At-Will - Free Action
Trigger: You hit a Damaging Attack against a Single Enemy 
with your Death mark and 50% or fewer Hit Points 
Effect: The Attack is automatically a Critical Hit. An Enemy can 
only be affected by this Feature once per Scene.
Bonus: You are able to sense when an Enemy has 50% or 
fewer Hit Points. 
Lethal Attack
Prerequisite: Assassin, Novice Combat or Stealth
At-Will - Free Action 
Trigger: You hit a Damaging Attack against an Enemy 
that is Flanked, Vulnerable or Unaware of your 
presence. 
Effect: The Attack has a bonus to Critical Hit Ranges 
equal to your Tier Level. If the only Target is an Enemy 
with your Death mark, the bonus also applies to Effect 
Ranges.
Exploit Weakness
Prerequisite: Assassin, 2 Assassin Features, Expert 
Combat or Stealth
Scene x 2 - Swift Action 
Trigger: You hit a Damaging Attack against a Single 
Enemy that has a Status Affliction, has your Death 
Mark or is Vulnerable.
Effect: The Triggering Attack is one step more 
effective against the Target (Max 1.5 x Effectiveness). 
An Enemy can only be affected by this Feature once 
per Scene. If the Target has 2 or more Afflictions, the 
Frequency of this Feature is not expended.

title: Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes (p.145)
body:
145145
Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes
NINJA
Ninjas are likely the most versatile of fighters within any setting, and 
Pokemon isn’t any exception. Characters like Koga and Janine may 
follow the traditional path of a ninja, but there are plenty of other 
options! This includes an illusionary specialty, psionics and shadows.
Ninja 
[Advanced] [Class] 
Prerequisite 1: Rogue [or]
Prerequisite 2: Adept Ninja Skill
Static 
Effect: Choose a Ninja Specialty listed below. You then gain the 
associated Capabilities of that specialty.

• The Path of Deception - Blender & Illusionist

• The Path of Psionics - Pick two of Aura Reader, Mindlock, 
Telekinetic, Telepath & True Sight 

• The Path of Shadows - Dead Silent, Darkvision, Shadow Meld

• The Path of Tradition - Climber, Jumper & Quick
Note: Ninja Skills are Acrobatics, Guile, Intimidate or Stealth
Ninja’s Arsenal
Prerequisite: Ninja, two Novice Ninja Skills
Static 
Effect: Your Damaging Attacks have a 17+ Effect 
Range to cause Targets to become Poisoned. When 
performing a Crafting Downtime Action you may 
create Hazard Bags with any of the following Attacks:

• Iron Spikes, Poison Gas, Smokescreen, Spikes, 
Toxic Spikes
Precise Attack
Prerequisite: Ninja, 2 Ninja Features, an Expert 
Ninja Skill 
At-Will - Free Action 
Trigger: You use a Damaging Attack against an Enemy 
that is Flanked, Vulnerable or Unaware of your 
presence. 
Effect: The applicable Targets are treated as 
Vulnerable against the Triggering Attack. If they are 
already Vulnerable or Poisoned, it gains the Sureshot 
Keyword instead.
Shinobi Combat
Prerequisite: Ninja, two Adept Ninja Skills
Static 
Effect: You learn all the Attacks listed under your chosen 
Ninja Specialty except the one with the [Master] tag. Once 
you have 4 Ninja Features, you learn the Attack under your 
Specialty with [Master] listed next to it. 

• The Path of Deception - Double Team, Devious Strike, 
Haunting Visage, Deception [Master]

• The Path of Psionics - Imprison, Magic Powder, Psycho Cut, 
Psycho Slash [Master]

• The Path of Shadows - Shadow Strike, Shadow Snare, 
Shadow Veil, Shadow Bolt [Master]

• The Path of Tradition - Agility, Toxic, Cross Poison, 
Assassinate [Master]
Mastered Technique
Prerequisite: Ninja, 3 Ninja Features, a Master Ninja Skill
Static 
Effect: Choose two Abilities to gain; one without a Ninja 
Specialty listed and one with your Specialty listed. You cannot 
choose an Ability with a listed Specialty that isn’t the one 
you picked.

• Ambush, Infiltrator, Run Away, Copy Master (Deception), 
Illusion (Deception), Shadow Tag (Shadows), Spectral 
Cloak (Shadows), Mental Assault (Psionics), Memory Wipe 
(Psionics), Deadly Poison (Tradition), Poison Point (Tradition)

title: Command, Guile, Intimidate and Stealth.
body:
Note - Your Swashbuckler Skills are Acrobatics, Charm, Combat, 
Command, Guile, Intimidate and Stealth. 
Mechanic - Panache Coat 
This Coat may be expended as a Free Action when performing 
an Accuracy Roll, Save Check or Skill Check in Combat to roll 
twice, taking either result. If the user gains a Status Affliction 
or is Critically Hit by an Attack, any Panache Coat they have is 
expended. Whenever you expend your Panache Coat, you cannot 
gain another during the same Turn.
146146
Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes
SWASHBUCKLER
The life of a pirate is one that varies depending on the person. A 
swashbuckler could be a trainer with fighting prowess or verbal 
prowess, as they come with many skills. However all Swashbuckler 
have a sense of superiority and always end up on top in combat. 
Swashbuckler
[Advanced] [Class] 
Prerequisite 1: Rogue [or]
Prerequisite 2: Adept Swashbuckler Skill
Static 
Effect: Your Damaging Attacks have a 12+ Effect Range to 
grant you a Panache Coat. This Effect Range cannot be 
extended like normal Effect Ranges.
Panache Mechanic is explained below
Creed of the Corsair
[Ranked 3]
Rank 1 Prerequisite: Swashbuckler, two Novice 
Swashbuckler Skills
Rank 2 Prerequisite: Swashbuckler, two Adept 
Swashbuckler Skills
Rank 3 Prerequisite: Swashbuckler, an Expert and 
Adept Swashbuckler Skill
Static 
Effect: For each Rank, choose two Swashbuckler 
Techniques to learn. 
Swashbuckler Techniques are on the next page
Flourishing Finisher
Prerequisite: Swashbuckler, 3 Swashbuckler Features, a 
Master and Expert Swashbuckler Skill
Scene x 2 - Free Action
Condition: You have a Panache Coat 
Trigger: You hit and resolve a Damaging Attack 
Effect: You may perform any of the following Maneuvers 
as a Free Action against a Target of the Triggering Attack. 
Additionally, you may expend a Panache Coat to treat the 
Maneuver as if they had the Sureshot Keyword and the 
Resistant Keyword for Maneuvers is ignored. 

• Distract, Intrigue, Provoke, Terrorize, Disarm, Hinder, 
Push, Trip

title: Braggart’s Swagger
body:
Braggart’s Swagger
At-Will - Free Action
Trigger: You cause an Enemy to become Provoked by 
you or inflict a Mental Status Affliction
Effect: You gain a Panache Coat.
Combat with Style
Static
Effect: Choose two Attacks from any combination of 
the following Feature’s Novice Attack Lists to learn. 
Once you have 4 Swashbuckler Features you may 
choose two more. Alluring Combat, Criminal Combat, 
Imposing Combat, Martial Combat, Nimble Combat
Feinting Strike
At-Will - Reaction
Trigger: An Enemy would Trigger an Attack or Ability 
in response to your Attack
Effect: You may expend a Panache Coat to ignore 
its effects but the Frequency and Action used are 
refunded.
Flamboyant Ego
Static
Effect: While you have a Panache Coat, you cannot 
gain a Mental Status Affliction. 
Humbling Reassessment
Scene - Reaction
Trigger: You’re hit by a Critical Hit or gain a Status 
Affliction while you have a Panache Coat
Effect: The Panache Coat is still expended as normal, 
however the Triggering Attack is no longer a Critical 
Hit or you are immediately cured of the Affliction.
 
Nimble Superiority
At-Will - Free Action
Trigger: You’re Targeted by an Attack
Effect: You may expend a Panache Coat to have the 
Triggering Attacker perform the Accuracy Roll against 
you twice, taking the lower result. While you have 
a Panache Coat, you gain Evasion equal to your Tier 
Level.
Outnumbered but 
never Outmatched
At-Will - Free Action
Condition: You are Flanked 
Trigger: You hit a Damaging Attack against an Enemy 
that is Flanking you
Effect: You gain a Panache Coat.
Privateer’s Prowess
Static
Effect: Choose two Swashbuckler Skills to increase to 
the next Skill Rank, if you meet the prerequisites for 
that Rank.
Stylish Attack
At-Will - Swift Action
Trigger: You hit a Damaging Attack against an Enemy 
that is Flanked, Vulnerable or Unaware of your 
presence
Effect: You gain a Panache Coat after the Triggering 
Attack resolves.
Victorious Bravado
At-Will - Free Action
Trigger: An Enemy faints 
Effect: You gain a Panache Coat. If you already have 
one, you instead gain +1 CS in a Stat of your choice or 
a Tick of Temporary Hit Points
 
 
SWASHBUCKLER TECHNIQUES
147147
Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes

title: Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes (p.148)
body:
148148
Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes
PROVOCATEUR
Do you want to be a silver tongued menace? Provocateurs and their 
Advanced Classes are Trainers that specialize in using words as 
weapons. Through attacks like Charm or Taunt, they can easily inflict 
Mental Afflictions on enemies and pester them all day. 
Provocateur
[Base] [Class] 
Prerequisite: Novice Provocateur Skill
At-Will - Free Action 
Trigger: You hit a Social Attack or Manipulate Maneuver
Effect: One Enemy hit by the Triggering Attack or Maneuver 
has a penalty to all Accuracy Rolls and Save Checks equal to 
your Tier Level until the end of their next Turn. Provocateur 
can only be used once per Round. 
Bonus: You may learn two Attacks from either the Alluring 
Combat Feature or Imposing Combat’s Novice Attack List, or a 
combination of either. 
Note: Provocateur Skills are Charm, Command, Guile, or Intimidate.
Cutting Words
Prerequisite: Provocateur, a Provocateur Skill at 
Novice
Static 
Effect: Your Social Attacks have a 18+ Critical Hit 
Range. If they were to Critical Hit, roll a 1 d 4. All 
Targets hit by the Triggering Attack lose X Ticks of Hit 
Points where X is equal to the result. You have a +2 
Modifier to Critical Hit Ranges when using a Social 
Attack against an Enemy for each Mental Affliction 
they have.
Quick Wit
Prerequisite: Provocateur, 2 Provocateur Features, a 
Provocateur Skill at Expert 
Scene x 2 - Reaction
Trigger: You’re Targeted with an Attack
Effect: Before the Triggering Attack is used, you may 
use a Social Attack or Manipulate Maneuver as a Free 
Action, but it can only Target the Triggering Enemy. 
They cannot apply Speed Evasion against this Attack. 
Mind Games
Prerequisite: Provocateur, a Provocateur Skill at Adept
Scene x 3 - Swift Action 
Trigger: You hit a Social Attack used as a Standard Action
Effect: The Attack gains one of the following effects. An 
Enemy can only be affected by each effect of Mind Games 
once per Scene.

• All Targets become Provoked by you until the end of their 
next Turn.

• All Targets become Suppressed or Enraged of your choice.

• All Stats lowered by the Triggering Attack are lowered by an 
additional -1.

• Status Afflictions gained by the Triggering Attack cannot be 
cured during their next Save Check.
Under their Skin
Prerequisite: Provocateur, 3 Provocateur Features, 
a Provocateur Skill at Master
Scene - Free Action
Trigger: You’re hit with an Attack from an Enemy with a 
Mental Affliction or that is Provoked by you
Effect: If the Triggering Attack was a Status Attack, it misses. If 
the Triggering Attack was a Damaging Attack, it is reduced by 
an additional damage step. 
Bonus: You have +1 Uncapped Evasion against Enemy Attacks 
for each Mental Affliction they’re affected by.

title: Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes (p.149)
body:
149149
Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes
Some Trainers go beyond just smooth talking and their Charisma is truly 
breathtaking. Even their enemies aren’t immune to their influence, as 
Debonairs have the power of Coersion. This special Affliction allows the 
Trainer to have some sway over what Enemies do in combat.
Silver Tongue
Prerequisite: Debonair, Novice Charm or Guile
At-Will - Swift Action 
Trigger: You hit a Social Attack against a single Enemy 
used as a Standard Action
Effect: The Attack gains one of the following effects. 
An Enemy can only be affected by each effect of Silver 
Tongue once per Scene.

• The Enemy becomes Entranced

• The Enemy becomes Vulnerable until the end of the 
Round.

• Choose an Ally. the Enemy treats that Ally as their 
Fixation as well if they’re Entranced.
Charming Visage
Prerequisite: Debonair, 2 Debonair Features, 
Expert Charm or Guile
Static 
Effect: You gain the Beautiful Ability. The User’s 
Entranced Effect Ranges for Status Attacks are 
increased by +2. Whenever the user would inflict a 
Mental Affliction, they may instead Entrance 
the Targets. 
Mind Manipulator
Prerequisite: Debonair, Adept Charm or Guile
Scene - Free Action 
Target: An Enemy within 6 m that has a Mental Affliction
Effect: You may use a Manipulate Maneuver against them as 
a Free Action.
Bonus: Your Manipulate Maneuvers gain the Sureshot 
Keyword against Enemies with a Mental Affliction. You have 
a Boon to Skill Checks against or opposed by Enemies with a 
Mental Affliction.
Swayed Allegiance 
[Order]
Prerequisite: Debonair, 3 Debonair Features, 
Master Charm or Guile
Scene - Full Action 
Target: A Coerced Enemy within 3 m
Effect: You may have the Target Slide up to their Movement 
Value. The Target performs an Attack as a Free Action as if it 
had the Priority Keyword. You choose the Attack that they use 
and its Targets. The Attack used does not have its Frequency 
expended. 
Debonair
[Advanced] [Class] 
Prerequisite 1: Provocateur [or]
Prerequisite 2: Adept Charm or Guile
Static 
Effect: You learn the Cute Charm Ability. Whenever you 
Entrance an Enemy that is already Entranced, they become 
Coerced.
DEBONAIR
Mechanic - Coerced
Coerced is a Mental Affliction that cannot be cured unless the affected 
Combatant is also cured of the Entranced Affliction (By which this is 
cured as well). At the start of a Coerced Combatant’s Turn, apply one of 
the Effects below

•  Choose a Maneuver . The Coerced User cannot use that Maneuver 
until the end of the next Round.

•  Choose a Type. The Coerced User cannot use Attacks that match that 
Type this Turn.

•  Choose an Enemy. The Coerced User cannot be Targeted by 
them or Target them until the end of the next Round.

•  Choose yourself or an Ally. The Coerced User becomes 
Provoked by them this Turn.
GM Note
As a GM you can either have the Player choose Targets to Attack 
and you choose what they use or you may disclose the Target’s 
Attack List and have the user decide

title: Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes (p.150)
body:
150150
Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes
TRICKSTER
Much like Masterminds, Tricksters are Trainers who have mastered 
the art of trickery and non-violent combat. Trickster take provocation 
to the next level and torment through maneuvers and are much more 
efficient with their deception compared to other types of Trainers. 
Trickster
[Advanced] [Class] 
Prerequisite 1: Provocateur [or]
Prerequisite 2: Adept Guile or Gen Edu 
At-Will - Free Action
Trigger: You hit a single Enemy with a Status Attack
Effect: After the Attack’s Resolution, you may perform a 
Manipulate or Tactic Maneuver against the Target of the 
Triggering Attack as a Free Action, excluding Attack of 
Opportunity or Throw, provided you’re in range. For any 
opposed Checks you may use Guile or Gen Edu instead of the 
listed Skills. Trickster may only be used once per Round. 
Tormenting Wit
Prerequisite: Trickster, Novice Guile or Gen Edu
Scene x 2 - Swift Action
Trigger: You inflict a Status Affliction on a single 
Enemy
Effect: That Enemy gains a Tormented Coat. 
Whenever an Enemy with a Tormented Coat fails a 
Save Check, they lose a Tick of Hit Points for each 
Affliction they’re affected by. If an Enemy were to 
have no Afflictions, their Tormented Coat is expended.
Bonus: You have +3 Uncapped Evasion against 
Enemies with your Tormented Coat. 
Quick Trick
Prerequisite: Trickster, 2 Trickster Features, Expert 
Guile or Gen Edu
Static 
Effect: You gain the Prankster Ability.
Sly Malediction
Prerequisite: Trickster, Adept Guile or Gen Edu
Scene x 2 - Free Action
Trigger: You succeed the Skill Check for a Manipulate 
Maneuver other than Analyze or hit a single Enemy with a 
Social Attack
Effect: Choose an Affliction the opposing Enemy has. They 
cannot cure that Affliction via Save Checks until the start of 
your next Turn. Sly Malediction can only affect an Enemy 
once per Scene.
Encore Performance
Prerequisite: Trickster, 3 Trickster Features, Master Guile or 
Gen Edu
Scene x 2 - Free Action 
Trigger: You use a Status Attack with the Versatile Keyword as 
a Standard Action
Effect: After the Triggering Attack resolves, you may use it 
again as a Swift Action using the Versatile Effect, ignoring 
the restrictions of the Versatile Keyword and ignoring its 
Frequency. A specific Attack can only Trigger this Feature 
once per Scene. 
Bonus: You may use Status Attacks through the Versatile 
Keyword regardless if you used a Damaging Attack this Round 
and you may still use Damaging Attacks after resolving an 
Attack this way.

title: Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes (p.151)
body:
151151
Chapter 4 - Trainer Classes
RUFFIAN
Trainers who are Ruffians impose authority and fear on those they 
face. Whenever they speak, enemies cower and for good reason. In 
combat they also have plenty of defensive capabilties such as gaining 
grit and defense, shrugging off damage and being an outright menace.
Ruffian
[Advanced] [Class] 
Prerequisite 1: Provocateur [or]
Prerequisite 2: Adept Command or Intimidate
At-Will - Free Action 
Trigger: You hit an Attack or Maneuver
Effect: One Target of the Triggering Attack or Maneuver loses 
-1 CS in a Stat of your choice. If the Triggering Attack was a 
Social Attack, it affects all Targets instead. A Combatant may 
only be affected by this Feature once per Round.
Combat Grit
Prerequisite: Ruffian, Adept Command or Intimidate
At-Will - Free Action,
Trigger: You’re hit by a Damaging Attack or hit a 
Damaging Attack
Effect: After the Triggering Attack resolves, you gain +1 Grit 
Counter. You may have a Maximum number of Grit Counters 
equal to double your Tier Level.
Bonus: For each Grit Counter you have, you have +5 Damage 
Reduction. Whenever you restore Hit Points or gain a Status 
Affliction, you lose half your Grit Counters (Rounded Up). 
Not even a Scratch
Prerequisite: Ruffian, 3 Ruffian Features, Master Command 
or Intimidate
Scene - Reaction
Trigger: You would Faint 
Effect: You are instead set to 1 Hit Point. If you have any Grit 
Counters, they may all be removed and you gain a Tick of 
Temporary Hit Points equal to the number removed, however 
these Temporary Hit Points are removed at the start of your 
next Turn.
Fearsome Force
Prerequisite: Ruffian, Novice Command or Intimidate
Scene x 2 - Free Action 
Trigger: You hit a Social Attack
Effect: After the Triggering Attack resolves, you may 
use the Terrorize Maneuver against all Targets hit by 
the Triggering Attack. The Maneuver cannot miss but 
still performs the Opposed Check. 
Shrug Off
Prerequisite: Ruffian, 2 Ruffian Features, Expert 
Command or Intimidate
Scene x 2 - Swift Action 
Effect: Choose one of the following Effects to apply. If 
the user is below 50% Hit Points, this doesn’t expend 
the Frequency of Shrug Off. 

• The User gains a Tick of Temporary Hit Points

• The User is cured of a Physical Status Affliction

• The User removes a Coat or Mark affecting them

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
body:
152152
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Alternatively, if only one Combatant is Initiating, all 
opposing Combatants that are involved must exceed 
the number of successes of the initiator’s Skill Check. If 
it is entirely unclear who should go first, or what Skills 
would be relevant, Luck Checks may be used in place 
of Skill Checks.
GM Note: If you and your players fully agree that a certain 
Initiative Order makes the most sense, you may forgo rolling 
and simply use that Initiative Order . Make sure your players 
are on-board with this idea before you use it!\
Example:  A  Villain  is  monologuing  in  front  of  a  group  of 
players while one of his henchmen reaches for their weapon 
slowly. They perform a  Stealth Check  with  4  Successes.  All 
Players that can see this henchmen may roll a Perception or 
Intuition and if they beat 4 Successes, they start the Scene. 
4. The Initiators begin the Scene
When a Party gains Initiative, up to two Combatants 
may take their Turn. During these Turns, they can use 
any number of Actions available to them in any order 
between them. After these Turns are completed, the 
next Party gains Initiative. A Combatant may choose 
to end their Turn with unused Actions, which could be 
used if an Effect is Triggered that would require that 
Action. But unused Actions do not carry over to the 
next Round. 
5. Take Turns until there are no Combatants 
left to take Actions
Initiative will swap from Party to Party until all 
Combatants that can use an Action have done so. If 
one Party has multiple Combatants who have Actions 
left who haven’t taken a Turn yet, they can take it in 
succession until none remain, instead of just choosing 
two Combatants. 
6. Start the next Round
Once Step 5 is completed, the Round ends. Any effect 
that would apply at the end of a Round then occurs. 
This can include environment changes, Lair Actions, 
Conditions or Affliction being removed, etc. The Party 
that starts the next Round is any Party that wasn’t 
the last to act last Round. If the Enemies took their 
turns last during Round One, then the Players will start 
Round Two. At the start of this Round, all Combatants 
gain their appropriate set of Actions once more. This 
process will repeat until all members of a Party are 
Fainted or Surrender. 
Combat in Pokemon Tabletop Evolution takes place over multiple 10 second Rounds where combatants each have a 
Turn (Or initiative, used interchangeably) in which they can perform actions. 
To determine the order by which combatants take their Turns, perform the following steps below. Once you get used 
to playing, some of these steps you’ll know already and not have to determine when combat starts!
Starting Combat
1. Determine all of the Combatants
At the start of a Scene, all Combatants have a brief 
moment to enter the Field. During this Step, ask 
your Players what Pokemon they want to be active 
on the field. They may release all of these Pokemon 
as a Free Action, ignoring normal Switching rules. 
(Remember you can have multiple Pokemon active at 
a time!). During this time, create a deployment Zone 
to determine which spaces are valid to start in. 
2. Divide all Combatants into Parties
All unique groups of combatants form their own 
parties, including the Players. Each unique group 
typically has their own goal or interest separate from 
other Parties. For instance, a group of Wild Pokemon 
might want to drive off the Players that have stumbled 
into their territory, while a nearby group of Evil Team 
Grunts wants to capture the Wild Pokemon, but don’t 
care much about the Players. NPCs typically shouldn’t 
share a party with Players.
3. Determine which Party goes first
The GM determines what approach each Party is taking 
to the combat, and determines a relevant Skill to use 
for Initiative. Using the previous example, if the Evil 
Team Grunts are sneaking up on the Wild Pokemon, 
the Grunts might roll Stealth for their Initiative. The 
Wild Pokemon are watching for invaders, but are 
also acting aggressive and territorial, so they could 
reasonably roll Perception or Intimidation. The Players 
are relatively unaware of what’s happening, so they 
would likely need to roll Perception or Intuition to 
determine their Initiative.
To resolve the rolls, every involved combatant rolls 
with an appropriate Skill. This can differ within a Party - 
for instance, the Wild Pokemon mentioned could have 
some of their members roll Perception and others 
roll Intimidation. Sum the total successes rolled from 
each Party. The Party with the most Successes or the 
Party with the highest Success number goes first (At 
the group’s discretion), and the other Parties follow in 
descending order. If another Party joins an encounter 
during the fight, have them roll their appropriate Skill, 
and then insert them in the Initiative order according 
to their Successes rolled during the next Round.

title: Alternative Initiative Rules
body:
Alternative Initiative Rules
Take the Speed Stat of all Combatants and organize them in a list from highest 
to lowest. We recommend the other version but if you don’t wish to move from 
PTU, it doesn’t kill anything besides the flow of combat being less dynamic. Note 
that mechanics that reference the Initiative will not factor into this method of 
tracking Initiative. 
153153
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
153153
Alternative Initiative
There are a few additional ways you can start a Scene, listed below. 
Surprise Rounds
Sometimes  the  flow  of  a  Scene  can  be  interrupted  by  a  sudden 
action such as a Charizard suddenly using a flamethrower, or a sniper 
suddenly shooting from stealth. When this occurs, determine which of 
the following applies to the situation. 
1. Sudden Attack
If all opposing Combatants are aware of the Initiator’s presence, but 
someone  decides  to  start combat unexpectedly, they  may not  have 
time  to  prepare!  When  beginning  the  Scene,  there  is  no  Initiative 
Check. Instead, the first Combatant or Combat Pair to act are the ones 
who act first. During the next round however, the Initiative Check is 
performed at the start of the Round and it continues as normal. 
For  example,  if  the  villain  is  monologuing  in  order  to  distract  the 
players, they may suddenly call for an allied grunt to charge and launch 
an Attack! The Players however are aware of the grunt attacking but 
they won’t be able to act faster than them. This allows the grunt to act 
first, ignoring their Speed or normal Initiative conventions. 
2. Stealth Attack
If all opposing Combatants are not aware of the Initiator’s presence, 
the  Surprise  Round  may  instead  lead  to  a  Stealth  Attack!  In  this 
example, let’s say the villain is monologuing and while doing so, they 
send a secret code to a hidden Intelleon that is hiding in a nearby bush. 
The Intelleon then uses Sniper Shot on the Party and initiates combat! 
The same as Sudden Attacks, there is no Initiative Check for the first 
Round, but in addition, the Initiator treats all Enemies as if they were 
Vulnerable! 
The only difference however is that a Skill Check is required in order 
to succeed in a Stealth Attack. If the Initiator wins, they may continue 
as  normal.  If  they lose  however, any Attack the  initiator performs is 
resisted by an additional Damage step and enemies gain +9 Evasion 
against it (Basically maximum evasion value). This Skill Check is made 
upon the Attack’s declaration and can be any Skill determined by the 
GM. In this example, they could have an Intuition Check to determine 
the  body  language  of  the  villain.  Or  there  could  be  a  Perception vs 
Stealth Check to see if the Intelleon was found by the Players!

title: Example (Flanking): Aipom is currently being flanked
body:
Example (Flanking): Aipom is currently being flanked
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
154154
High Ground - A Combatant has the High Ground State 
whenever a Target is at least 2 m below them. Targets 
of  someone  who  has  the  high  ground  apply -3  less 
Evasion against the Attacks of the Combatant with the 
high ground. 
Low Ground - A Combatant has the Low Ground State 
whenever  they  Target an  Enemy  that  is  at  least  2 m 
above  them.  Targets  of  someone  who  has  the  Low 
Ground compared to them have +3 additional Evasion 
against their Attacks.  
There are a few different states one can be in during 
combat  based  on  where  they  are  on  the  field,  these 
are known as Position States, each of which are listed 
below. Consider  these  equivalent  to  Conditions  that 
persist while they’re in this position.  
Adjacent - Two Combatants are Adjacent if they occupy 
spaces that are touching each other (Including corners) 
or occupying the same space.  
Flanked -A Combatant is Flanked whenever they have 
two Enemies adjacent to them, but those Enemies are 
not  Adjacent  to  each  other . If  a  Combatant  is  Large 
Sized  or  bigger, they  need  at  least  three  Enemies  to 
become Flanked, or one of the two must be Large Size 
or bigger . While a Combatant is Flanked, they apply -3 
less Evasion against Attacks from Enemies. 
Surrounded  -A  Combatant  becomes  Surrounded 
whenever  they  have  at  least  three  Enemies  adjacent 
to them. Enemies that are Large Sized or bigger cannot 
be  Surrounded.  While  Surrounded,  a  Combatant 
cannot  apply  Evasion  against  Attacks  from  Enemies. 
Surrounded Combatants are also considered Flanked. 
Movement  during  combat  is  fairly  simple  so  we’ll 
resolve the basics in a few bullet points. 

• Pokemon Tabletop Evolution uses a square combat 
grid. Each Square (Or Space) is considered 1 meter and 
it  takes  1 m  of  movement  to  move  into  that  Square, 
regardless if it’s diagonal or not. 

• Each Combatant occupies a number of spaces 
based on their Size Category.   Small  and  Medium 
Combatants take up  a  1 x 1  Square. Large Combatants 
take up 2 x 2 and Huge takes up at least 3 x 3. Depending 
on the Combatant’s shape, Huge Combatants could be 
a custom size, such as an Arbok being 2 x 5. 

• Movement Maneuvers exist  as  options  you  can 
do,  all  under  the  Bolster  Maneuvers.  This  includes 
Disengaging,  which  allows  you  to  move  1 m  without 
Triggering  an  Attack  of  Opportunity, Jumping,  which 
allows  you  to  ignore  Terrain  and  Hazards  you  move 
over, and Sprinting, which allows you to increase your 
Movement Value per Movement Action.

• Movement can be performed as a Movement Action 
where by  default you can move up  to 6  Meters. This 
can  be  altered  by  Movement  Capabilities  or  Terrain 
you  move  through.  You  cannot  split  up  Movement 
when you use a Movement Action unless you perform 
another Movement Action.
For example, you cannot move 3 Meters, Attack, then 
move another 3 Meters, as after the first 3 m moved, 
your Movement Action is resolved. 

• Sliding  is  the  process  of  moving  involuntarily, such 
as through an Attack like Hydro pump that slides you 
away from the source. This movement does not Trigger 
Attacks of  Opportunity  but  does  apply  the  effects of 
Terrain you’re Slid  through. The  source  of  the  Sliding 
determines the path in which you take whenever you 
Slide, however the GM has the final say. 
Combat Positioning
Moving on the Field

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.155)
body:
155155
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
[Breakable] -   This  Terrain  or  an  Object  within  this 
Terrain can be destroyed when targeted by a Damaging 
Attack.  When  this  Terrain  or  Object  is  destroyed, 
something may happen, which usually can be figured 
out through an Analyze Maneuver or prior knowledge. 
Breakable Objects are automatically hit when Targeted. 
Fragile  Breakable  Objects  are  destroyed when  hit  by 
one Attack and Dense Breakable Objects are destroyed 
when hit by two Attacks. 
Example:  An  explosive  barrel  that  causes  an  explosion 
when  hit.  A  pulsating  artifact that  causes  a  buff  while  not 
destroyed.
[Hazardous] - This  Terrain  is  considered  to  have  a 
Hazard Effect in them. Whenever a Combatant enters 
the space willingly or unwillingly or ends their Turn on it, 
they’ll be affected by its Effects unless otherwise stated 
by the Hazard of its trigger conditions. A Combatant can 
only be affected by a specific Hazardous Terrain Effect 
once per Round, regardless of how many they activate. 
Only  one  Hazard may exist on  a  space  at  a  time  and 
Hazards cannot be placed on a space that already has 
one.
Example: Scorched ground that causes burns. Caltrops that 
inflict wounded. Miasma that lowers Sp Atk by -1 CS. 
[Blessed] -   This  Terrain or  an  Object  in  is  the  source 
of a buff. The GM determines how this buff is granted, 
usually  by  either  being  within  a  range  of  the  Terrain 
or  starting  your  turn  on,  ending  your  turn  on  or 
entering the Terrain. Combatants can only be affected 
by  a  specific  Blessed  Terrain  Effect once  per  Round, 
regardless of how many they activate.  
Example: A Flag that while active, grants Temp HP within 2 m 
at start of Turn. Holy ground that grants +3 to Saves while 
standing on it.
[Reactive] -   This  Terrain or  Objects  within  it  have  a 
Trigger condition. When that Trigger condition occurs, 
something  will  happen,  which  can  usually  be  figured 
out by an Analyze Maneuver . To determine this Trigger, 
either set a time limit (# of Rounds) or a range by which 
the Trigger can occur .
Example: A sizzling bomb will explode in 1 Round. Crumbling 
Terrain that will collapse after being entered. A rare crystal 
may shatter if an Attack hits a Combatant within 1 m of it. 
[Biome] - This space can be assigned with any Biome 
stated in the Naturewalk and it categorizes Combatants 
as standing in that Terrain. 
Default Terrains :  Grasslands,  Forest,  Wetlands,  Tundra, 
Mountain, Cave, Desert, Ocean, Urban, Space
The Battlefield has a lot of diversity depending on the 
area surrounding you. You could battle in a simple city 
or  basic  terrain  or  you  could  be  in  a  hazardous cave 
with a lot of lava pools and stalactites! Each space on 
the battlefield may have numerous different Terrain 
Tags  assigned  to  them  or  objects  occupying  those 
spaces, each of which adding diversity to what you may 
encounter . All Tags are listed below.
[Basic] - Nothing is special about this T errain
Example: Simple Grassland, Dirt, Pavement
[Slow] - Entering  this  Terrain  costs  2  Movement 
Value instead of 1. Slow Terrain can be ignored if the 
Combatant  has  the  Naturewalk  for  the  associated 
Biome Tag on the Terrain.
Example: Mud, Shallow Rivers, Spider Webs
[Rough] -   Ranged  Attacks  that  Target  a  Combatant 
within  Rough Terrain or  travel through Rough Terrain 
have a -2 Penalty to Accuracy Rolls.
Example: Tall Grass, Dust Clouds, Smoke
[Elevated] -   Compared  to  base  level,  assign  a  value 
of  1-4  Meters  to  this  space  to  be  higher  than  those 
around  it.  Melee  Attacks cannot  Target Enemies  that 
are  at  least  2  Meters  above  or  below  them  and  are 
not considered Adjacent when occupying an Adjacent 
space.
Example: Towers, Hills, Cliffs, Boxes
[Cover] -   If  a  Ranged  or  Line  Attack  would  Target a 
Combatant  that  is  Adjacent  to  Cover  Terrain,  it  is 
resisted by  an  additional  damage  step.  Cover  Terrain 
has no effect if any of the following is applicable

•  The Attacker is Adjacent to the Target

•  The Target is a larger size than the Cover Terrain

•   The  Cover  does  not  break  the  line  of  sight  for  the 
Attack
Example: Barricades, a Large Tree, Edge of Blocking Terrain
[Blocking] -   This  Terrain  cannot  be  occupied  by 
Combatants other than through the Phaser Capability 
and  cannot  be  moved  through.  Blocking  Terrain can 
either  be  Small or Large .  If  the  Terrain  is  Large,  it 
breaks  line  of  sight  and  blocks  Attacks  that  would 
travel through it such as Line or Ranged. If it is Small, it 
doesn’t break line of sight or block Attacks. 
Example:  Small  could  be  Barricades  or  Machinery.  Large 
could be Walls or Trees. 
Terrain Tags

title: Example (Gym Modifiers) - A Gym Battle in a Ghost/Dark Gym
body:
Example (Gym Modifiers) - A Gym Battle in a Ghost/Dark Gym 
has a small fog that spreads across the battlefield, which results in 
the Storming Weather Effect and causing the battle to begin with 
Foggy Weather . In addition, in the crowd of the gym, there are 
many ghost enthusiasts and supernatural fanatics that are cheering 
for the gym leader, some even performing rituals to boost their 
performance, resulting in the Mystical Force Effect that causes all 
Ghost Type Damaging Attacks to gain the Smite Keyword. 
156156
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Shifting Terrain - At the start of each Round, the GM may 
shuffle any number of spaces and on a failed Acrobatics 
Check with a Standard CR (2), any Combatants standing 
on them are either Tripped or follow the space to its 
new  destination.  During  this  action,  you  may  also 
create any Cover or Blocking Terrain in any pattern that 
is desired. 
Oppressive Force -   Some  kind  of  energy  or  force  is 
present  on  the  battlefield  and  negatively  affects  the 
Players and their Party. On a failed Focus Check with a 
Tough CR (3), they suffer the negative effects depending 
on their Degree of Failure…This check may be repeated 
at the end of each Round if it is present, however the 
CR is lowered by 1 each subsequent time. 
Mystical Force -   Some  kind  of  beneficial  energy  is 
present  on  the  battlefield,  positively  affecting  either 
the native Pokemon or all combatants. Examples could 
include a blessed field that cures all Status Afflictions, 
an Aura that increases Damage by +3 DB, or the energy 
of a crowd that increases all Rolls by +2.  
Sometimes  you  may  want  to  add  a  sense  of  danger 
or  realism  to  a  location  a  Party  is  going  in.  When 
determining a scene, you may add any of the following 
environmental  modifiers  depending  on  what  makes 
sense to be present. 
As a note, you should have all native Pokemon immune 
to Environmental Modifiers, as they’re usually native to 
the area and have adapted to its conditions. If desired 
you could have them affected as well but it would make 
sense  for  a  Lillipup  that  was  raised  in  a  dark  cave to 
gain darkvision and be used to the low lighting. Some 
Water Pokemon found  at  sea  may  also  not  have  the 
Gilled Capability to go underwater which would make 
more sense to ignore.
Note: Have any suggestions? Feel free to send a message in 
our Discord!
Storming Weather - Weather  will  be  persistent 
throughout the Encounter, whose type is most logical 
for the terrain. This could include Sunny Weather in a 
Volcano, Snowy Weather in a Tundra, or Foggy Weather 
in a City.  
Harsh Heat -   All  Water Type and  Ice  Type Damaging 
Attacks are resisted by an additional step. Burn Ranges 
are  extended  by  +2.  Any  Combatant  wearing  [Large] 
or  heavy equipment such  as  steel plating or  a  winter 
jacket  will  be  treated  as  Vulnerable.  It  is  likely  to  be 
Sunny in this Area. 
Harsh Cold -   Combatants that aren’t Fire or  Ice  Type 
suffer a -3 to Evasion. Chilled Effect Ranges are extended 
by +2. It is likely to be Snowy in this Area.
Underwater - Combatants  without  the  Swimmer 
Capability  treat all  spaces  as  Slow  Terrain. Whenever 
a Combatant ends their Turn without the Breathless or 
Gilled Capability, they take Suffocation Damage. 
Low Vision -   Combatants  without  the  Blindsense, 
Darkvision  or  Glow  Capability  suffer a -3  to  Accuracy 
Roll and -2 d 6 to Perception Checks. If there is instead 
no  Vision  and  complete  darkness,  those  without 
the  above  Capabilities  are  instead  Blinded  until  their 
situation would change. 
Environmental Modifiers

title: Basic Attack
body:
Basic Attack
Frequency: At-Will
Range: Melee, 1 Target 
Category: Physical or Special
Type: Normal
AC: 4
DB: 4
Effect: None
157157
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
157157
This  is  the  default  information  for  a  Basic  Attack, 
however they can be altered in numerous ways listed 
below. 

•  When performing a Basic Attack, the user may change 
the  Type from  Normal  to  any  of  the  Types they  are, 
such as a Charmander using a Fire Type Basic Attack. 

•  If the user has the Ranger Pokemon Role, the Range 
of Basic Attacks may also be 6, 1 Target. 

•   If  the  user  is  holding  a  Short  Ranged  Weapon,  its 
Range  may  be  changed  to  6,  1  Target. If  it’s  a  Long 
Ranged  Weapon, its  Range  may be  changed  to  12,  1 
Target,  but  cannot  Target  Adjacent  Enemies.  If  the 
Weapon is Melee, the DB is increased by +2 when used 
this way.
Additionally, here are some rules that apply to Basic 
Attacks

•  Basic Attacks are treated as an “Attack” and can have 
a STAB bonus for Pokemon and can have DB modifiers 
applied to them such as through Technician.

•   Basic  Attacks ignore  Ghost  Type  Immunity, instead 
being treated as if it were Resisted. 

•   Basic  Attacks cannot Trigger anything from yourself 
or  allies  that  do  not  specifically  mention  Attacks  of 
Opportunity  or  Basic  Attacks.  This  means  if  it  just 
mentions an “Attack” being used, it cannot Trigger it. 
Basic Attacks  are always on  a  Trainer and  Pokemon’s 
Battle  Attack  list  without  taking  an  Attack  Slot, 
symbolizing the simplest of attacks, such as punching 
someone or a charmander shooting a puff of flames at 
someone. 
Basic  Attacks are referred to by other sections of  the 
system,  such  as  using  Attacks  of  Opportunity.  The 
following has the information on a Basic Attack:
To those of you familiar with PTU, this is basically the 
same as a “Struggle” Attack, but expanded slightly more 
in  order  to  give  it  some  quality  of  life improvements 
and  removing  Struggle  Modifiers  like  Firestarter  or 
Fountain. 
Basic Attacks

title: Attack: Silver Wind
body:
Attack: Silver Wind
Type: Bug
Frequency: At-Will
Range: 6, 1 Target 
Category: Special
AC: 2
DB: 6
Effect: On a 18+, the user gains +1 CS in all Stats. Spirit Surge
158158
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Category - The Damage Category will also be listed on 
the Attack and will be one of 3 types, Physical, Special 
or Status. Physical Attacks are resisted by the Defense 
Stat and can be avoided via Physical or Speed Evasion 
and  use  the  Attack Stat as  the  Offensive Stat. Special 
Attacks are resisted by the Special Defense Stat and can 
be  avoided via  Special  or  Speed  Evasion and  use  the 
Special Attack Stat as the Offensive Stat. Status Attacks 
do not have Damage Bases and may only be evaded by 
Speed Evasion. 
Accuracy Check (AC) - The Accuracy Check is used when 
a Combatant uses an Attack in which they perform an 
Accuracy  Roll  with  a  d 20.  The  Accuracy  Check  is  the 
result  you  need  to  match  or  exceed in  order  for  the 
Attack to hit. 
Damage Base (DB) - The number next to the Damage 
Base indicates the base amount of Damage dealt. Refer 
to the Damage section further on to determine what the 
equation is for the Damage Roll of the corresponding 
Damage Base. Many Effects or Features could modify 
the Damage Base of an Attack!
Effect - Effects list what the Attack does in addition to 
its  Damage.  Effects do  not  activate unless  the  Attack 
hits,  or  if  the  Attack  has  the  Spirit  Surge  Keyword. 
Effect Ranges  can  be  extended  by  other  Effects. For 
example, with Silver Wind, the Effect Range is an 18+. 
If it is extended by +2, it now Triggers on a 16+. Some 
Features or external factors may extend Critical Hit or 
Effect Ranges, however they cannot be extended past 
a total of +6 from their Natural Range. If an Attack has 
a Burn Range of 19+, the most it can be extended to is 
13+. 
Attack - The first line is obviously the name of the Attack, 
which  is  what  you  declare  when  using  the  Attack. In 
this case, it’s called Silver Wind.
Type -  Next  up  is  the  Elemental  Type  of  the  Attack. 
There  are  Bug,  Dark,  Dragon,  Electric,  Fairy, Fighting, 
Fire, Flying, Ghost, Grass, Ground, Ice, Normal, Poison 
Psychic,  Rock,  Steel  and  Water  Attacks!  This  will 
determine the Type effectiveness. 
Frequency -  Frequency  determines  the  rate at  which 
you can use this Attack and how often during a Scene. 

• At-Will:   These  Attacks  can  be  performed  every  turn  if 
desired 

• EOT: Every Other Turn, these Attacks can only be used once 
every other Turn and cannot be used two turns in a row. 

• Scene: Scene Attacks have a limited number of times they 
can  be  used  during  a  Scene,  notified  by  the  number  next 
to  them.  An  Attack with  the  Scene  Frequency  can  only  be 
used once, while one with Scene x 2, may be used twice. In 
addition, these Attacks function similarly to EOT where they 
cannot be used two turns in a row. 

• Static: Given to very few Attacks, some Attacks like Wrap 
are given Static Effects which passively apply,
Range -  Range  specifies  the  distance  in  meters  from 
which the Attack can hit. Keywords are also tagged on 
in the Attack’s Range. If an Attack’s Range changes, the 
Keywords  are  not  changed,  such  as  Dash  or  Priority. 
Besides  the  standard  numerical  distances,  other 
common distances include Melee, Self and Field. Self 
Attacks simply  target  the  user, Melee  Attacks have  a 
range of  1,  and  thus  must  target an  Adjacent  Target. 
The Field Range applies to the entire Field or Targets 
every  Combatant  if  applicable,  but  rare.  When  using 
Area  of  Effect  Attacks,  such  as  ones  with  the  Burst 
or  Blast  Range,  make  a  single  Accuracy  Roll  for  the 
entire Attack. If a Target of the Attack would result in 
a  different  Accuracy  Modifier  when  Targeting  them 
specifically, only apply that modifier in the calculations 
against its relevant Target (Such as if you’re Provoked)
Attack Info
Pokemon may learn  up  to  a  Maximum  of 6 Attacks at a time   (Unless  something  would  grant Attacks that  don’t 
expend an Attack Slot). Trainers however may learn as many Attacks as they gain from sources that apply to them! 
Unless stated in the Attack’s Range, all Attacks require a Standard Action to utilize. Keywords like Versatile may allow 
some Attacks to be used as Swift Actions with different effects, and keywords like Full Action mean an Attack requires 
a Standard and Swift Action. An example of an Attack is listed below, along with an explanation of each component 
of an Attack.

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.159)
body:
159159
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Attack Keywords
Passive Keywords
Aura / Bite / Defensive / Healing / Punch / Sonic 
These  Attacks  are  referred  to  by  other  Features  or 
Abilities such as Strong Jaw.
Blessing - All Combatants allied to the user and the user 
may  benefit  from  the  Blessing’s  Effects. The  Attack’s 
Effects describe how a Blessing may become activated. 
The Blessing persists until all activations are used or the 
Scene ends. 
Coat -  Coat  Attacks  grants  the  Target  a  Coat  which 
while they have it, grants them its effects. A Combatant 
cannot  have multiple  coats of  the  same  name.  Coats 
have listed methods by which they are expended but 
are  otherwise  removed  when  the  Target  faints,  the 
Scene ends, or an effect would destroy them. 
Dash - If the user moves at least 2 m in a straight line 
towards the Target and did not start their turn within 
2 m of them, Dash may be Activated. Regardless of if it’s 
Activated, Attacks with this Keyword may choose to use 
Speed as if it were the Offensive Stat. 
Full Action - Full Action Attacks require a Full Action to 
use, taking both a Standard and Swift Action.
Groundsource -  Groundsource  Attacks  do  not  have 
their  Accuracy  lowered  as  a  result  of  Terrain  and 
ignore  Blocking  Terrain.  These  Attacks  may  also  be 
used without line of sight, however if they hit, they are 
treated as if they missed with the Smite Keyword.
Hazard  -  Hazard  Attacks  cover  a  stated  portion  of 
the  field,  turning  the  Terrain into  Hazardous  Terrain, 
applying  on  top  of  any  other  effects  applied  to  that 
Terrain.  (Allowing  Terrain  to  be  both  Slowed  and 
Hazardous). Each Hazard will specify whether it affects 
only  Allies,  only  Enemies  or  all  Combatants.  A  Space 
may only be affected by one Hazard at a time, and if 
another Hazard would be set there, it replaces it unless 
it is a Blocking Hazard. An Enemy can only be affected 
by the same Hazard Effect once per Turn.  
Interrupt -  Interrupt  Attacks may  be  declared  in  the 
middle of another Combatant’s Turn in order to allow 
the user to take an Action. They work the same Priority 
(Advanced) effects in that they only allow you to take the 
Action that has Interrupt and not a Full Turn. Interrupt 
Attacks resolve before the Triggering Condition would 
take place. 
Pass -  At  any  point  during  a  Movement  Action  used 
to  move,  the  user  may  declare  a  Pass  Attack.  Once 
declared, the user may move forward up to 4 Meters, 
moving  through  occupied  spaces  as  if  it  were  Basic 
Terrain. The  user  must  end  in  an  Unoccupied  Space. 
The  Pass  Attack  Targets  all  Combatants  that  were 
moved through in this way, but each Target may only 
be hit once. The user cannot continue their Movement 
Action after moving through the 4 Meters. Shifting as a 
result of the Pass Keyword does not provoke Attacks of 
Opportunity. In order to use a Pass Attack this way, the 
user must have sufficient Movement remaining. 
Ability Keywords
Connection (X) - The listed Attack next to the Connection 
Keyword  is  automatically  learned  when  the  Ability  is 
gained and doesn’t take an Attack Slot
Innate -  Abilities  with  the  Innate  Keyword cannot  be 
disabled,  removed  or  obtained  by  combatants  other 
than the Pokemon who took this ability.
Priority -  At the  Start of  a  Round, or  after any Action 
resolves,  you  may  declare  a  Priority  Attack to  use  it 
immediately ignoring  Initiative, as  if  it  were a  Trigger 
condition.  This  requires  that  you  have  the  relevant 
Action available this Round. No Reactions can be made 
to  this  by  Combatants  with  a  lower  Speed  Stat  than 
you.  
Reaction -  Reactions  work  the  same  as  the  Interrupt 
Keyword,  however  they  occur  after  the  Triggering 
condition is  fully  resolved. The  user  must survive  the 
Trigger condition to be able to perform the Reaction. 
In order to minimize text, Keywords are added to Attacks for common effects. There are two types of Attack Keywords, 
Passive Keywords and Effect Keywords. 
Passive Keywords are listed in the Range of the Attack to describe Attacks that have a unique category. Examples 
include Aura Attacks, Blessing Attacks or Full Action Attacks . These Keywords persist even if an Attack’s Range is 
changed, despite being in the Range Cell. 
Effect Keywords denote a common effect that is abbreviated to shorthand that are less of a category and more of an 
Attack’s Effect. Examples include Smite Attacks, Drain Attacks and Slide Attacks.

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.160)
body:
160160
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Reckless-  Reckless  Attacks usually  have  some  sort  of 
negative penalty in their Effect applied to the user and 
may be referred to by other Abilities or Features. 
Recoil - When this Attack hits, determine the Target that 
took the most Damage from this Attack. The user then 
loses hit points equal to the Damage taken multiplied 
by the Fraction listed next to the Recoil Keyword. 
Set-Up - Set-Up Attacks cannot be used without Charge 
Tokens gained from their corresponding Charge Effect, 
and  they  expend  all  their  Charge Tokens on  use.  You 
may use a Swift Action to Charge a Set-Up Attack you 
know, resolving its Charge Effect and gaining a Charge 
Token for it. If you had Charge Token(s) from a different 
Set-Up Attack, they are lost without further effect. You 
cannot Charge and Resolve a Set-Up Attack in the same 
round.  Charging  does  not  count  as  using  an  Attack, 
nor does it expend its frequency; however, you cannot 
Charge an Attack if you could not use it otherwise (i.e. 
it has no remaining Frequency, it’s Disabled, etc.).
Shield -  This  Keyword  is  attached  to  some  Interrupt 
Attacks when the Attack would prevent another Attack 
from hitting. Any Effects that activate off of being hit, 
beyond the  Shield’s Trigger, do  not  occur . In  order to 
use a Shield Attack it must be the first thing Triggered 
(Ex: You cannot use Flame Body, then Protect)
Social -  Social  Attacks are socially  manipulative based 
and may be referred to by other Abilities or Features. 
These Attacks cannot be Intercepted. 
Trigger - Attacks with this Keyword specify their Trigger 
condition  in  their  Effect  and  cannot  be  used  if  that 
condition is not met. If it is met however, it allows the 
user  to  perform  the  relevant  Action  outside  of  their 
Initiative. 
Unstoppable  -  Enemies  cannot  activate  Triggers  in 
response to an Attack with this Keyword. 
Upgrade - X - An Attack with the Upgrade Keyword will 
have a different Attack name in its brackets. If you were 
to learn the listed Attack, you must remove this Attack 
from your Attack List and it cannot be relearned. 
Note: In the base system, this only applies to Legendary 
Signature Attacks, but can also be used to homebrew 
signature Attacks for your Pokemon!
Versatile - Attacks with the Versatile Keyword may also 
be used as a Swift Action if the user has not performed 
a  Damaging  Attack  this  Round  (Excluding  Attacks  of 
Opportunity). When a Versatile Attack is used this way, 
Damaging  Attacks (Excluding  Attacks of  Opportunity) 
cannot  be  used  by  the  user  for  the  remainder  of 
the  Round.  When  using  an  Attack  as  a  Swift  Action 
through the Versatile Keyword, refer to the text next to 
“Versatile” for its new Effects or to see how the Attack 
is altered. An Attack with the Versatile Keyword cannot 
be used twice in the same Round.
Weather -  Attacks with  the  Weather  Keyword  create 
Weather on the Field while they’re affecting the Field. 
If  a  Blessing  or  Field  Effect were  to  be  removed, the 
Weather that was created from it is also removed. The 
Field can have up to two Weathers affecting it at a time, 
then  any  further  Weather  introduced  overwrites  the 
least recent Weather added to the Field. Weather itself 
doesn’t  do  anything  but  other  Attacks,  Features  or 
Abilities may reference a Weather condition and have 
a bonus effect. There are 8 Types of Weather. Windy, 
Foggy, Mystical, Sunny, Snowy, Rainy, Thunderstorm 
and Sandstorm.
Effect Keywords
Double Strike -  Double  Strike  Attacks  have  their 
Accuracy Roll performed twice. If both Accuracy Rolls 
would  result  in  hitting  the  Target, the  Damage  Base 
Value is doubled. Each hit may Critically Hit separately; 
when adding damage from Critical Hit, add the Damage 
Base before it is doubled. For example, if one Double 
Kick Attack is a Critical Hit, add 1 d 8+5 to the Damage 
Roll. If both are Critical Hits, add 2 d 8+10. 
Drain - When this Attack hits, determine the Target that 
took the most Damage from this Attack. The user then 
restores Hit Points equal to half the Damage taken. 
Friendly -  Allies  of  the  user  of  this  Attack ignore  the 
Effects of this Attack and do not take Damage from it, 
and are not treated as being hit by the Attack. 
Five Strike  -  If  you  hit  with  a  Five  Strike  Attack,  roll 
additional  Accuracy  Checks  until  you  miss,  to  a 
maximum  of  5  total  Checks.For  each  subsequent  hit 
past  the  first,  add  +X  to  the  Attack’s Damage  Base, 
where X is your Tier Level.Critical Hits and Effect Ranges 
can only be triggered from the first Accuracy Roll. 
Spirit Surge - This Attack’s Effects and Effect Keywords 
occur regardless if it hits its Target(s). If an Effect Range 
must  be  met,  the  Accuracy  Roll  still  must  meet  this 
condition. Attacks used through the Versatile Keyword 
ignore the Spirit Surge Keyword.

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.161)
body:
161161
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Slide X- All Targets are moved a number of Meters with 
the max number moved being the value of X. The user may 
determine  the  path  and  final  destination  of  the  Target, 
following listed  restrictions. Restrictions may  be  listed  in 
parenthesis  after  the  Slide  Keyword  such  as  (Towards) 
or  (Away).  If  it  specifies  Towards, they  cannot  slide  into 
spaces  further  than  the  user  and  conversely  for  Away. 
Movement via the Sliding triggers Hazards but not Attacks 
of Opportunity. Combatants cannot slide vertically.
Sureshot - Attacks with the Sureshot Keyword do not have 
an AC and automatically hit unless they would otherwise 
be avoided such as through a Shield Attack. They may still 
perform an Accuracy Roll for sake of being a Critical Hit or 
Effect Ranges. These Attacks cannot be intercepted.
Smite - Smite Attacks deal damage as if they were resisted 
by an additional damage step whenever they would miss. 
Targets dealt damage this way ignore the Effect and other 
Effect Keywords of the Attack (Excluding Damage). 
Each  Pokemon  has  two  sets  of  Attack  Pools  they 
can  learn  from,  their  Level-Up List and  their 
Tutor List. 
Level-Up Lists are Attacks they learn when they reach a 
certain level, as the name suggests. 
Tutor Lists are  a  consolidated  group  of  Attacks  that 
the Pokemon could learn from all other sources. In the 
games, this was Tutor Moves (From NPCs), Egg Moves 
(From Breeding), and Technical Moves (Learned from 
TMs). Combining it all under one list makes it easier to 
teach them these Attacks!
Learning Tutor Attacks - Pokemon can access Attacks 
from their Tutor List multiple ways. One way is through 
level  milestones,  as  some  milestones  allow  you  to 
learn a free Tutor Attack! Another way is through Tutor 
Records, our version of TMs which can be rewarded to 
teach Tutor Attacks of a specific category. One last way 
they  can  be  learned  is  through  the  Mentor  Trait and 
the Training Downtime Action!
Tutor Rules -  Whenever  a  Pokemon  would  learn  a 
Tutor Attack or be granted one, they must follow the 
restrictions below. Any of the listed DB restrictions are 
before applying STAB. 

•   Pokemon under Level 20 can  only  learn  Attacks of 
an At-Will or EOT Frequency and with a Max Damage 
Base of 7. These Attacks are listed under the Pokemon’s 
Tier 1 Tutor Attacks
 

•  Pokemon that are at least Level 20 may learn Attacks 
that aren’t Scene [x 1] with a Max Damage Base of 9. 
These  Attacks are  listed  under  the  Pokemon’s Tier 2 
Tutor Attacks

•  Pokemon that are at least Level 40 have no restriction 
and  may  learn  any  Attacks on  their  Tutor List.  These 
Attacks are  listed  under  the  Pokemon’s Tier 3   Tutor 
Attacks 

• Attacks that modify their Damage Base are all Tier 2 
Tutor Attacks, ignoring the rules above.
Note:  The  Pokedex will  be  inaccurate with  their  Tier  Lists, 
as they’ve been changed many across multiple versions I’ve 
used  the  dex  for . Please  refer to  the  rules  above  to  verify 
the the Attack has the correct listed Tier . Feel free to report 
inaccuracies as i’ll update them at some point!  
Tutor Attacks

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.164)
body:
164164
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Using Attacks
164164
Whenever you attempt to use an Attack, you must make an 
Accuracy Roll, and to hit, this roll must meet or exceed the 
Accuracy Check (AC).
An Accuracy Roll is always simply 1 d 20, but is modified by the 
user’s Accuracy Modifier, by certain Attacks and other effects. 
Note that modifiers to Accuracy Rolls do not affect effect ranges 
or critical hit ranges, as those have to be natural results before 
modifiers are applied. 
Example: If you use Flamethrower with an Accuracy Bonus of +4 and 
roll a 16  this would neither be a Critical Hit, nor inflict a Burn despite 
the Effect Range being 18+. 
An Accuracy Check is the number an Accuracy Roll needs to 
meet or exceed to hit. It’s determined first by taking the Attack’s 
base AC and adding the target’s Evasion. For example, if using 
Earthquake, which has an Accuracy Check of 2, against an 
opponent with a Physical Evasion of +4, you would need to roll 
a 6 or higher on your Accuracy Roll to hit the target. Conversely, 
it may be easier to subtract the relevant evasion from the 
result of the Accuracy Roll and compare it to the Attack’s AC to 
determine if it hits, whichever method is easier .
Here are some notes and rules when making Attacks:

•  A roll of 1 is always a miss, even if Accuracy modifiers would 
cause the total roll to hit. Similarly, a roll of 20 is always a hit 
unless avoided, such as by a Shield Attack or by an Ability.

•  Attacks, Features, Abilities, or other mechanics that trigger on 
being hit may be declared before or after damage is rolled.

•  Attacks that have multiple Targets roll once, but apply 
modifiers separately. If you Target two Enemies with an area 
of effect attack and roll a 15 and one gives you a -2 Penalty to 
Attacks against them, the first Target is treated as the result 
being 15 and the other is treated as the result being 13. 

•  When an Attack hits a Target and that Target uses a Feature, 
Ability, Attack, or other mechanic that causes the attack to 
miss, a combatant intercepts for the target, or otherwise 
redirects the attack to themselves, the original target may not 
trigger any Features, Moves, Abilities, or other mechanics that 
require them to be hit (this does not retroactively invalidate the 
mechanic that caused the attack to miss). In the case of a target 
change, the new target may activate such mechanics. 

•  A Target can willingly choose to be hit by an Attack by not 
applying their Evasion.

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.165)
body:
165165
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
When an Attack hits, you apply any effects of the Attack 
to the target, including damage. When rolling Damage, 
check the attack’s Damage Base.  This number serves 
as a guide for an Attack’s strength, which translates to 
a  specific  amount  of  damage.  Many  effects, such  as 
Same Type Attack Bonus or STAB f or short may alter 
the Damage Base of Attacks. 
After  applying  all  modifiers  that  alter  Damage  Base, 
see  the  corresponding  Damage Roll   in  the  Damage 
Charts.  This  is  the  roll  to  which  you  add  your  Attack 
or  Special  Attack  Stat.  After  you  have  added  your 
appropriate Attack Stat (Based on its Category) to the   
Damage Roll of the attack, add any additional modifiers 
that may apply. You can add a single stat to Damage 
Calculations a Maximum of one Time. (No  doubling 
up through Feature usage!)
The Target then subtracts the appropriate Defense Stat 
based  on  its  Category. Physical Attacks have  Defense 
subtracted  from  them;  Special  Attacks  have  Special 
Defense  subtracted  from  them.  If  the  target  has 
Damage Reduction, that is subtracted afterwards.
After  defenses  and  damage  reduction  have  been 
applied, apply Type Weaknesses or Resistances. A 
Super-Effective hit  will  deal  x 1.5  damage.  A  Double 
Super-Effective or  higher  hit  will  deal  x 2  damage.  A 
Resisted Hit  deals  1/2  damage;  a  Double  Resisted or 
less hit deals 1/4 th damage. See the Type Effectiveness 
Chart  to  see  how  Pokémon  Types  match  up  against 
each other .
Same Type Attack Bonus
If  a  Pokémon  uses  a  damaging  Attack  with  which 
it  shares  a  Type,  the  Damage  Base  of  the  Attack  is 
increased by +2. This is referred to as ‘STAB’ .
Hit Point Loss
Effects that say “loses Hit Points” do not have Defensive 
Stats or Damage Reduction applied to these Hit Point 
changes. 
Tick of Hit Points
Some effects use this term. A Tick of Hit Points is equal 
to 1/10 th of someone’s maximum Hit Points. 
Critical Hits
On  an  Accuracy  Roll  of  20  (Or  possibly  lower  if  their 
Critical Hit Range is extended or they have Crit Range 
Modifiers), a Damaging Attack is a Critical Hit. A Critical 
Hit  adds  the  Damage  Roll  a  second  time  to  the  total 
damage dealt, but does not add the Offensive Stat or 
Damage  Bonuses  a  second  time.  For  example,  a  DB 
6 Attack is originally 2 d 6 + 8. Because it’s doubled, it 
becomes 4 d 6+16 instead if it crit. 
Damage Formula
Putting this all together, the process for calculating damage 
is as follows:
1. Find initial Damage Base
2. Apply Five/Double-Strike if applicable
3. Add Damage Base modifiers for final Damage Base
4. Modify Damage Roll for Critical Hit if applicable
5. Roll damage
6. Add relevant attack stat and other bonuses
7. Subtract relevant defense stat and damage reduction
8. Apply weakness and resistance multipliers.
9. Subtract final damage from Target’s Hit Points.
Damage Chart Below this section is what each Damage Base 
equates to as far as Damage Rolls. Simply roll the dice shown, 
adding the modifier next to it, and then add your Attack Stat 
to determine the total damage dealt. 
Dealing Damage
DB Damage Roll DB Damage Roll
1 1 d 6+1 15 4 d 10+20
2 1 d 6+3 16 5 d 10+20
3 1 d 6+5 17 5 d 12+25
4 1 d 8+6 18 6 d 12+25
5 1 d 8+8 19 6 d 12+30
6 2 d 6+8 20 6 d 12+35
7 2 d 6+10 21 6 d 12+40
8 2 d 8+10 22 6 d 12+45
9 2 d 10+10 23 6 d 12+50
10 3 d 8+10 24 6 d 12+55
11 3 d 10+10 25 6 d 12+60
12 3 d 12+10 26 7 d 12+65
13 4 d 10+10 27 8 d 12+70
14 4 d 10+15 28 8 d 12+80
Note: These values will likely be changed once I get someone on 
the team who is good with numbers
Example (Damage Roll): A Bisharp uses the Throat Chop Attack on 
an Alakazam. Going through the steps, the initial Damage Base is 
8. There isn’t any Double Strike or FIve Strike. It has a +2 DB Boost 
from being STAB, leading to DB 10. It didn’t crit. The Damage Roll 
is 3 d 8+10 and it adds a 27 Damage Bonus considerng the Attack is 
Physical and its Attack Stat is 27 (Offensive Stat). The roll result 20 
from the 3 d 8, plus 10 plus 27 equaling 57 Physical Dark Damage. 
Alakazam  has  8  Defense,  leading  to  45  Damage  and  it  is  Super 
Effective, multiplied by 1.5. Alakazam takes 68 Damage.

title: Improvised Damage Examples
body:
Improvised Damage Examples
Ex 1: Swinging a Metal Chair at an Incineroar is determined to 
be equivalent to using the Brutal Swing Attack but it is Steel Type 
instead of Dark. The Chair however becomes dented and unusable 
afterwards. The GM Determines that the Player uses their Attack 
Stat since they control the chair .
Ex 2: The GM Determines that the Chandelier has a Physical 
Evasion of 4 but on hit, it drops in a Blast 3 Range underneath 
it. Those hit by it are hit with the Heavy Slam Attack as if it were 
Weight Class 6. It also has a 15+ Effect Range to Trip Targets. The 
GM determines this Chandelier results in strong Damage, giving it 
an offensive stat of 40.
Ex 3: The GM determines that shooting the Oil Barrel will lead to a 
DB 15 explosion, dealing Fire Type Damage with massive damage 
giving it an offensive Stat of 80. The Damage will also be a Burst 3 
Range, being very deadly to anyone inside. 
Environmental Damage Examples
Ex 1: A Steam Geyser in a cave starts sizzling, projecting a range in 
which it will attack next round. It then explodes, causing the Attack 
Scald to hit in a Burst 1 Range. It is considered strong damage, 
having 40 Special Attack. Good thing an enemy was pushed into it!
Ex 2: A Tree was knocked over after a Heracross missed a megahorn 
attack. This results in the tree performing the Wood Hammer 
Attack as if it was a Line 3 Atack opposing the direction heracross 
attacked. It was a smaller tree so it dealt weak damage with a 20 
Attack Stat. 
Ex 3: A windstorm is being caused by Tornadus, leading to 
extremely dangerous Weather . Combatants that don’t pass a Tough 
CR (3) Athletics Check each round will be attacked by a Gust Attack 
based on Tornadus’s Special Attack Stat. 
166166
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Environmental Damage 
Environmental Damage is very similar in application to 
Improvised  Damage,  but  entirely in  the  GM’s control 
on whether it occurs or not, considering it’s the setting 
reacting  in  a  way  to  damage  others.  Similarly, when 
the Environment would deal damage, choose a similar 
Attack or a damage type and category. Then determine 
its  strength  level  to  determine  its  offensive  stat. 
Then determine its range and who and how it affects 
others.  Additionally,  determine  methods  of  avoiding 
this damage such as passing a Skill Check or failing an 
Accuracy Check.
Improvised Damage
Sometimes during combat, you look at something and 
get  an  idea.  Next  thing  you  know, you’re  swinging  a 
metal chair at an Incineroar . Or even better, you shoot 
a  Chandelier  to  drop  onto  someone.  Or  even  better, 
you  shoot  an  oil  barrel  to  make an  explosion!  This  is 
similar to Environmental Damage but is  not  from the 
environment and is instead a singular source used as a 
tool to deal damage. 
It’s  basically  resolved  the  same  way  but  can  lead  to 
different  scenarios.  When  dealing  with  Improvised 
Damage,  determine  the  source  and  determine  how 
the action is best to resolve. This usually results in an 
Attack being used that the Initiator normally wouldn’t 
know, however it is a one time usage. Do not let players 
repeat prior accepted sources just for expanded type 
coverage unless  it  comes  at  a  cost  such  as  by  taking 
an  Inventory  Slot.  It  should’nt  be  a  bit  where  every 
combat, some guy goes “Do I see a metal chair neraby 
to throw at them?”
 
Other Damage Types
Any source of Damage that comes from non-Attack sources are listed below, along with the rules on how to resolve 
it. Be sure to use other Damage Types to spice up conflict and remember that the battlefield is alive! 
When using Attacks through the Improvised Damage or Environmental Damage method, the Offensive Stat you use 
is either based on the Initiator of the Damage or based on its relative power level, listed below. If the Initiator is in 
control of the Damage, use their Offensive Stat instead but if it is out of their control, use the following values:
Weak Damage (20) Strong Damage (40) Massive Damage (80) Mythical Damage (120)

title: Suffocation Damage Examples
body:
Suffocation Damage Examples
Ex 1: A Trainer is being pinned into a pond while grappling with a 
Machamp and drowned while they have dominance. 
Ex 2: An Occult Trainer is dealing with exhaustion and takes 
Suffocation damage whenever they perform a Special Category 
Attack as a representation of mana thirst and mental overexertion. 
Ex 3: A King was poisoned and the castle is suddenly being raided 
by marauders! This toxin is much deadlier than the Poisoned 
Affliction, leading to suffocation damage until he can get medical 
attention. 
Falling Damage Example
Ex 1: A Trainer riding a Braviary is 4 Meters up in the air and 
the braviary faints, causing them to fall onto a rocky surface. 
Considering it’s a tough terrain, they’re treated as falling an extra 
2 m. They take damage equal to 2 d 20. 
167167
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
167167
Falling Damage 
Before I even start, do not push people into ravines or 
chasms unless it’s intended for a Narrative Death. This 
is not meant for that kind of falling. With that out of 
the  way, Falling  Damage  is  typeless  Physical  Damage 
depending on how far you fall and some other factors. 
For each Meter you fall before landing, roll a d 6.  You 
may replace 3 Meters with a d 20 if desired for physical 
play or  lack  of  dice  or  if  you  don’t  like counting. You 
take damage equal to the result. The following factors 
may influence how much damage you take:
Where did they Land? 
Depending  on  where  they  landed  it  could  lead  to 
adding  more “Meters Fallen” or  subtracting from the 
amount as  it  softened their  blow. Did  they  land  on  a 
mattress? A 4 m Fall could be lessened to 1 m. Did they 
break their fall by landing on branches and a trash pile? 
It could be dropped to 2 m instead of 4. Did they land 
on concrete and had a harder fall? This means it dealt 
more  damage  and  maybe  felt  like  a  10 m  fall  instead 
of 4. This is all GM Discretion. If something leads to a 
harder fall add more meters to the Damage Roll, if  it 
absorbed the blow, subtract a few meters.
Was the Falling Intentional? 
Sometimes people like to jump a little further than they 
should or perhaps even fail an acrobatics check and fall 
while parkouring on rooftops. If a fall was unintentional 
such as being pushed off a cliff, proceed as normal with 
Damage Roll Calculations. If it was intentional such as 
jumping  off  a  roof  to  get  to  safety, subtract  half  the 
user’s Acrobatics Rank (Rounded Up) from the number 
of Meters fallen.
Suffocating Damage 
While rare, sometimes creatures can suffocate and lose 
the ability to breathe! When they do so, perform the 
following. 
At  the  end  of  the  Turn  of  a  Suffocating  Combatant, 
if  they’re  still  suffocating, they lose two Ticks of Hit 
Points. Then the next round if they’re still suffocating, 
they  lose  three Ticks instead,   then  this  continues, 
adding  a  Tick  each  time, maxing out at 5 Ticks. 
Combatants  only  take  Suffocation  Damage  once  per 
Round if they would have multiple Turns. This can be 
a very deadly state of being, so make sure you remove 
the source of Suffocation or resolve Combat fast or else 
it could spell disaster! 
Suffocation Damage does not need to only be from 
sources such as the inability to breathe,   but  it  is 
meant as a mechanic to deal increasing damage over 
time.  Any  of  the  following  examples  could  result  in 
Suffocating Damage.

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.168)

168168
