Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Type-Effectiveness  is  a  bit  more  complicated  if  the 
defender has two types:

• If both Types are neutral,   the  attack  of  course  is 
simply neutral

• If both Types are resistant,   the  attack  is  doubly 
resisted and does x 0.25 damage

• If both Types are weak, the attack is doubly super 
effective and does x 2 damage.

• If one Type is weak and one is resistant, the attack 
is neutral.

• If either Type is Immune, the attack misses
If a Pokémon is Immune to the damage of an Attack, no 
effect of that attack is applied to that Pokémon. 
For  Example,  rolling  a  19  on  Mud  Slap  vs  a  Flying 
Pokémon does  not  lower  their  Accuracy. If  an  Attack 
has  the  Spirit  Surge Keyword, the  effect still goes  off 
regardless if the target is Immune.
This is the Type Effectiveness Chart! Whenever an Attack 
of  one  of  the  Types  on  the  Left  Targets a  Pokemon, 
find its Type(s) on the top for Type Effectiveness. Then 
multiply  the  damage  dealt  by  its  effectiveness, after 
defenses  are  applied,  by  the  number  shown  above. 
If it’s Super Effective, it is multiplied by 1.5 x. If it’s 
Resisted, it is multiplied by 0.5 x.
Note  that  Type  Effectiveness  does  not  affect  Status 
Attacks, only Physical and Special Attacks are affected. 
Confuse Ray for example, despite being Ghost Type, can 
still hit Normal Type Pokemon. Attacks that cause loss 
of Hit Points such as Counter or Sonic Boom however 
are affected by Immunity, though not resistances. 
Unlike Pokemon, Trainers do not innately have a Type 
and all Attacks on them do neutral Damage.

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.169)
body:
169169
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Combat Maneuvers
Sometimes,  the  best  option  in  a  fight  isn’t  just  to 
hit  the  other  side  as  hard as  you can. You can gain a 
tactical advantage on the field of battle by relieving an 
opponent of their weapon, momentarily tripping them, 
or even simply pushing them in a specific direction. 
Pokémon and Trainers can use all Combat Maneuvers, 
unless  otherwise  noted  (Such  as  Minion  Pokemon). 
Maneuvers with an Accuracy Check have Targets apply 
Speed  Evasion  against  them  but  are  not  treated  as 
Status Attacks (For the sake of Abilities like Prankster).   
Each Combat Maneuver has a Category as well, which 
may be referenced by outside sources. 
The Categories are:
Bolster  -  Bolster  Maneuvers  are  Maneuvers  that 
improve your own position in battle   or  help  your 
Allies, adapting to your Environment. This can include 
Disengaging, Sprinting or Hiding.
Manipulate  -  Manipulate  Maneuvers  involve social 
methods of combat that affect your Enemies. This can 
include Provoking, Distracting, Intriguing or Terrorizing 
others.
Tactic -  Tactic  Maneuvers  involve different styles of 
Combat that affect your Enemies.   This  can  include 
Disarming, or Grappling others. 
Some  Maneuvers  have  the  Resistant  Keyword.  This 
Keyword  means  that after they’re hit with that 
Maneuver and it resolves, they have a Boon for any 
related Skill Checks for the rest of the Scene, even if 
they  won  the  Opposed  Check.  If  a  Combatant would 
Fail a Skill Check involved with a Resistant Maneuver, 
they  additionally  have  a  Bane  whenever  they  would 
use  that Maneuver against an Enemy they previously 
Targeted with it. 
This  is  meant  to  display a  Combatant’s adaptation to 
combat tactics used against them and prevent them for 
falling for the same tricks. 
Example (Resistant Keyword):   If  a  Jynx  uses  an  Intrigue 
Maneuver against a Machop and it succeeds, they become 
Entranced. 2 Rounds later the Jynx’s Ally, Salazzle, uses the 
Intrigue  Maneuver  against them  again.  The  Machop  has  a 
Boon  to  their  Focus  or  Intuition  Check.  The  Salazzle  failed 
their  Intrigue  Maneuver  this  time.  During  the  next  round, 
the  Salazzle  tries  to  use  it  again  against the  Machop.  This 
time the Machop has a Boon and the Salazzle has a Bane. 
If they fail it again. The machop will not be swayed by their 
chemical wiles, as they’ve seen it used before.
 
169169
All Combat Maneuvers are on the next few pages
GM Note
You do not need to be literal with the Effects listed and depending 
on the context you may allow different Skills to be used or different 
Effects to apply, just don’t let your players abuse this for better 
effects or better outcomes, do what makes sense. 
For example, a ruffian that is devilishly handsome may be able to 
use the Intrigue Maneuver with their Intimidate Skill, however it 
may change the skill roll. If the Target would be attracted by their 
intimidating aura, it could work as normal, however if they’re 
instead unaffected by that type of demeanor, they may gain +1 d 6 
to their opposed check.

Intercept
Action: Reaction

Attack that doesn’t have the Social or Sureshot 
Keyword

the space the Ally is in, or until you’re in a space that 
is directly between the source of the Attack and the 
Targeted Ally. If you reach the space the Ally is in, 
they are Slid into an Adjacent space, then you move 
into the Space they were in. You are then hit by the 
Triggering Attack as if you were the original Target 
and it becomes one damage step more effective (Max 
1.5 x) or if you were Immune to the Triggering Attack, it 
is treated as Resisted instead. The Effectiveness does 
not increase if you expend a Standard Action.
Intercept Notes

• If an Attack is an Area of Effect, the Ally that was 
intercepted for resists it by an additional Damage Step
if they would still be in Range.
 
Jump
Action: Movement 
Effect: Move up to half your Movement Value in a 
straight line (diagonals are allowed), ignoring Effects 
or Penalties on Grounded Terrain that you moved 
over, including Hazards (Some Hazards like Smoke or 
Smog may still apply per GM Discretion). 
 
Defend
Action: Swift Action, Reaction or Movement
Target: An Adjacent Ally
Effect: Until the start of your next Turn, while you’re 
Adjacent to them, if the chosen Ally were to be 
Targeted by a 1-Target Attack, you become the Target 
instead.

Action: Movement

Target: An Adjacent Ally

Damaging Attack this Turn and cannot use one for the 
rest of the Turn.

you’re Adjacent to is treated as Blocking Terrain and

title: Riposte Notes
body:
Riposte Notes

•  If the chosen Attack is Melee, the Combatant performing this Maneuver must be between the source of the 
Attack and the Target(s)

•  If the Triggering Attack is Melee or Close Blast, the Combatant that uses the Riposte Maneuver must be 
Adjacent to them. If it is Blast or Line, the chosen Attack must be Blast or Line and Super Effective. 

•  The chosen Attack must be either Neutral or Super Effective against the Type of the Triggering Attack. 

•  If the Accuracy Roll for Riposte resulted in a Natural 20 and/or the chosen Attack was Super Effective, multiply 
your Damage Roll by 1.5 x. Then the Triggering Attacker loses Hit Points equal to the difference in damage rolls if 
yours would be higher . Hit Points lost this way cannot exceed more than 3 Ticks worth  
of their Hit Points.
171171
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
171171
Riposte
Action: Standard + Reaction
AC: 4
Range: Field 
Trigger: You or an Ally would be damaged by a 1-Target, 
Line or Blast Attack without the Sureshot Keyword
Effect: Choose a Damaging Attack and expend a 
usage of its Frequency, then perform this Maneuver 
(The Attack is not considered to be used, ignoring its 
effects). If it hits, perform a Damage Roll as if you used 
the chosen Attack against the Triggering Enemy (Do not 
apply Damage Calculations). Subtract your Damage 
Roll result from the Triggering Attack’s Damage Roll 
(Before Damage Calculations) and if it results in 0 or 
below, the Triggering Attack instead misses all Targets 
and they are not affected by any of the Attack’s Effects. 
If the result is still positive it is the new Damage Roll 
for the Triggering Attack. If a Combatant hits this 
Maneuver, they cannot perform it for the rest of the 
Scene.
Respite
Action: Full 
Effect: This maneuver cannot be used if there are any 
Enemies within 2 m of the user. The user chooses two 
effects from the list below to apply, then all of their 
Stats with Positive CS are set to their Default Value. 
You may choose the same effect twice if desired. 

• All of their Negative Combat Stages are reset to their 
Default Value.

• The user becomes cured of a Status Affliction. 

• The user becomes cured of a Condition that isn’t 
granted by an Affliction they have.

• The user may remove a Coat or Mark affecting them.
Sprint
Action: Standard or Swift 
Effect: As a Standard Action, your Movement Value is 
doubled this Turn. As a Swift Action, your Movement 
Value is increased by +2 this Turn. 
This is your classic Beam Struggle!

Grapple
Action: Standard
AC: None
Range: Melee, 1 Target, Sureshot
Effect: You and the Target make opposed Athletics or 
Combat Checks as a Grapple Check. If you win, you 
both become Grappled and you gain Dominance in 
the Grapple. Combatants with Teleporter Speed or the 
Phasing Capability cannot become Grappled. Combatants 
that are Grappled are Vulnerable, cannot take Movement 
Actions (Not listed below) and are Provoked by the 
Combatant they’re Grappled with. See the notes below 
for further info. Resistant.
Grapple Notes

• A Combatant with Dominance in the Grapple, on their 
Turn, may perform any of the following alongside normal 
legal Actions:
Drag: As a Movement Action, they may Shift and Slide 
the Combatant they’re grappling into an Adjacent 
space. Their Movement Value is lowered by the other 
grappler’s Weight Class
Strike: As a Full Action, they may perform an At-Will or 
EOT Attack against the other Grappler as if it had the 
Sureshot Keyword.
Secure: As a Shift or Swift Action, they gain a Boon to 
their next Grapple Check. As a Standard, the opposer 
also gets a Bane to their Opposed Check 
Cease: As a Free Action they may end the Grapple.

• At the start of the Grappler’s Turn who doesn’t have 
Dominance, as a Standard Action, they may repeat the 
opposed Grapple Check. The winner gains Dominance in 
the Grapple and may choose to continue or end it. 

• A Combatant who is at least two Size Categories larger 
than a Grapple Initiator automatically succeeds Grapple 
Checks

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.174)
body:
174174
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Basic Orders
Orders are particular actions that can be shouted by a Trainer to issue a command to their allies. Similar to Maneuvers, 
all Trainers have access to using Orders, however some Trainers gain specific Orders through Features, specified by 
the [Order] tag, or as Rewards from bonding with a Pokemon or their Team. Additionally, Commander and the classes 
that branch off of it specialize in commanding others and may perform Orders better than other Trainers. 
Basic  Orders are always use a Reaction (Unless otherwise specified) and  each  Basic  Order  will  have a  different 
circumstance on when it can be used. In order for an Order to be used, one of the Trigger Conditions must be met and 
the Target(s) must be able to hear you communicate their verbal command, usually being within 10 m. Additionally, 
Orders do not stack, so multiple Trainers cannot use an Order at the same time on the same Target or a Target cannot 
be affected by they same Order multiple times. This means you cannot have 3 Trainers all shout at a Pokemon to 
dodge with the Reactive Order to stack the effects.
Design Note: Orders are meant to be mechanical ways to show the effects of a Trainer’s verbal commands on their Pokemon. 
Basic Orders are meant to emulate simple commands like “Dodge it!” or “C’mon Psyduck snap out of it!” , when it’s confused. 
Improvised Orders are meant to enable a rules-lite type of gameplay that allows Trainers to be flexible when commanding their 
Pokemon. Similar to Maneuvers, these are generic actions that can be performed so all Trainers can have a wide array of options 
to perform on their turn regardless of class choices. 
Basic Order Examples
Ex 1: A Level 3 Trainer sees their Burmy being hit by an Attack. They shout to them “Hang in there Burmy just a bit longer!” , and use the 
effect of Defensive Order, granting it 5 Damage Reduction against it as its Tier Value.
Ex 2: A Level 7 Trainer’s Psyduck is confused and suffering. A Trainer shouts at it, “Snap out of it Psyduck!” . It’ll use the Effect of Inspiring 
Order, granting it +2 to Save Checks  as its Tier Level.
 
Defensive Order
Trigger: Your Pokemon is hit by a Damaging Attack
Effect: The Target gains Damage Reduction equal to your Tier 
Value against the Triggering Attack. 
Energetic Order
Trigger: Your Pokemon hits a Damaging Attack
Effect: The Target gains a bonus to the Triggering Attack’s Damage 
Roll equal to your Tier Value. 
Inspiring Order 
Trigger: Your Pokemon would perform an Attack or Save Check
Effect: The Target gains a modifier to the Triggering Accuracy 
Check or Save Check equal to your Tier Level. 
Reactive Order
Trigger: Your Pokemon is Targeted by an Attack or Maneuver 
before the Accuracy Check
Effect: The Target gains Evasion equal to your Tier Level against 
the Triggering Attack or Maneuver
Tactical Order
Trigger: Your Pokemon uses an Attack
Effect: The Target gains a modifier to the Triggering Attack’s Effect 
Range or Critical Hit Range equal to your Tier Level. 
Basic Order List

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.175)
body:
175175
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
175175
GM Note:   Improvised  Orders  can  allow  for  Trainers  to 
basically do anything in a rules lite format so ensure that this 
is only used to enable cool moments rather than grant them 
more  “pseudo-features”  they  can  fall  back  on  for  power . 
When  a  Trainer asks,  can  I  have my Pokemon do  this,  this 
is the arena to do so with “Playground rules” . These Orders 
should only be done in the moment to enable a Trainer and 
their  Pokemon to  do  something  normally  outside  of  their 
mechanical  limits  but  makes  sense  thematically.  Typically 
these  effects shouldn’t  be  repeated so  they’re  used  every 
fight,  however some  Improvised Orders can  be  granted as 
rewards.  When  determining  Order  Effects, make  sure  the 
Action cost or Skill TN is appropriate.
If  desired,  your  GM  can  also  create  custom  Effects 
based  on  the  fluff  of  your  command  known  as  an 
Improvised Order. Performing an Improvised Order can 
allow you to affect the target in unique ways not listed 
as a Basic Order, nor does it need a Trigger, however 
it requires a Skill Check of some kind  from either the 
Order Recipient, Enemy Target or User to do so based 
on  what  they  want to  occur  and  the  effects must  be 
balanced around a Swift Action. Improvised Orders can 
also be used as Standard Actions to have their effects 
be stronger . If the Skill Check involved fails, the Order 
is deemed ineffective and the expended action is still 
used. 
Improvised Orders
Example (Pokemon Check): A Team Rocket grunt is running away from a Scene and a Trainer shouts for their 
Mightyena to “Quick, don’t let them escape!”. Nothing on the standard list would let them do so, so they use an 
Improvised Order. The GM requests that Mightyena make a Standard CR (2) Acrobatics Check or the user makes 
a Tough CR (3) Command Check. Upon passing, the GM allows the effect of the Order to be “The Target may 
perform a Damaging Attack as a Priority (Advanced) Action and may spend their Movement Action to do so”, and 
the Order costs a Reaction from the Trainer. 
Example (Enemy Check): A Trainer quickly commands their Venusaur, “Quick, bind them with your vines so 
they can’t escape!” The GM allows this as a Swift Action to “Target an Enemy within 3 m of Venusaur to become 
Trapped on a failed Acrobatics Check”. The Venusaur sends out ivy towards a Hitmonlee who makes an Acrobatics 
Check with a CR of Standard (2). They succeed and jump out of the way. Over the course of the Campaign once 
their bond with Venusaur improves, the GM grants them an Order that lets them repeat this effect. 
Don’t let Players: Make up overpowered effects for little to no action cost or exchanging penalty.
Do let Players: Use fluff to enable utility that a Pokemon otherwise wouldn’t have access to.

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.176)
body:
176176
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Flier -  As  a  Swift  Action,  when  declaring  Movement, 
the  user  may  become  Airborne  and  use  Movement 
to  move  up  the  Z-Axis.  The  user  cannot  exceed  4 m 
in  the  air  this  way. While  Airborne,  the  user  ignores 
the  Effects  of  any  Hazard,  Terrain Effects  that  apply 
to non-Airborne  Combatants, or  Movement Penalties 
as  a  result  of  Terrain. At  the  end  of  their  Turn, they 
must spend 1 SP or else they are no longer Airborne. 
Pokemon  with the Flier Capability that are Dragon or 
Flying Type or with GM permission may exceed the 4 m 
restriction while outside of combat. All Creatures with 
the  Flier  Capability  are  also  considered  to  have  the 
Glider Capability.
Glider -  The  user  is  Immune  to falling damage  unless 
their method of gliding is restricted somehow. 
Grounded  -  The  user  cannot  perform  the  Jump 
Maneuver .
Jumper -  When  using  the  Jump  Maneuver  you  may 
instead  move  up  to  your  whole  Movement  Value 
instead of half.
 
Quick - The user’s Movement Value is instead 8 m.
Slow - The user’s Movement Value is instead 4 m.
Burrower - As a Swift Action, when declaring Movement 
as  a  Movement  Action,  select  a  Space  in  which  you 
could  reach  via  movement.  The  user  automatically 
appears in that Space. This Movement cannot Trigger 
Reactions or Attacks of Opportunity. This may only be 
used  if  the  spaces  you  travel through  are  connected 
by ground or breakable in which you can dig a tunnel. 
For example, a Diglett cannot use this Capability while 
they’re suspended on a platform in the air since there 
is no connected ground or if they’re in a building with 
metal tiling. 
Climber - The user may climb Vertical Surfaces, Slopes 
or Cliffs without any Movement impairment or without 
needing to make any Skill Checks. If desired, the user 
may  end  their  Movement  Actions  while  sticking  to  a 
vertical  surface,  provided  they’re  less  than  4 m  up  in 
the  air, such  as  climbing  a  Tree without  Skill  Checks 
required.
Capabilities
Capabilities are assigned to and can be gained by each Trainer and Pokemon to denote what is special about them. 
If a Pokemon like Gastly has the ability to phase through walls, it could have the Phaser Capability. Capabilities can 
also be gained, such as if a Trainer is wearing a Winter Coat, they could temporarily gain the Naturewalk (Tundra) 
Capability. Capabilities are described in the next few pages and broken down into 3 sections. 
Movement Capabilities - There are many Pokemon that can move in unique ways! Movement Capabilities describe 
the ways in which Pokemon can interact with the environment and can deviate their movement when using Movement 
Actions. This can include Pokemon that are faster, can teleport, can swim or jump higher , etc.
Combat Capabilities - Combat Capabilities are effects that can primarily influence battle such as being able to see in 
the night, change forms mid battle or blend in with the shadows. They still can have narrative utility but their primary 
effects can assist in combat.
Narrative Capabilities - These Capabilities have little to no combat utility, primarily serving as narrative tools. This can 
include seeing aura, seeing souls, being able to make no noise or be immune to mind invasiveness! 
Note: All numbers on a Capability are subject to GM Discretion and should only be followed verbatim on a standard usage. If a 
Combatant is exceptionally weaker or stronger than the standard norm, you may adjust the numbers in a Capability. A Weaker 
example could be a new Aura Guardian who needs to pass a Standard CR (2) Focus Check in order to see the aura of a Pokemon, 
as they haven’t trained with it to the point where it becomes Intuitive. A Stronger example could be that a Trainer made a bond 
with Lugia and Lugia’s Telepathy ignores the 10 m Range and they can always communicate provided they’re in the same region 
MOVEMENT CAPABILITIES

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.177)
body:
177177
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Form Change-  The user is  capable of  changing forms 
through  an  Attack,  Ability  or  other  effect.  Keep  a 
different Character Sheet for each of the user’s forms. 
All Forms must have the same total HP Stat Value and if 
anything (such as an Ability) alters the user’s base stats, 
all forms are affected in the same way.
Groundshaper  -  As  a  Swift  Action,  the  user  can 
transform the terrain around them in order to create 
Slow  Terrain, Rough  Terrain, or  Basic  Terrain.  When 
this  Capability  is  used,  they  may  select  any  number 
of  spaces  within  2 m  of  the  user  to  become  affected. 
Spaces can have different types of alterations applied to 
them during one instance, such as 3 Spaces becoming 
Basic Terrain and 4 becoming Rough Terrain. At the cost 
of 1 SP , the user may also select any number of spaces 
within  a  Zone of  10,  Ranged Blast 3.  At the  cost of  2 
SP , the  user  may  also  create  Blocking  Terrain that  is 
[Breakable - Fragile] 
Invisibility -  The  user  may  turn  invisible  as  a  Swift  + 
Movement Action. They cannot perform Actions while 
Invisible other than becoming Visible once more as a 
Free Action or using Actions to move. While Invisible, 
Enemies  have  a -4  penalty  on  Accuracy  Rolls  against 
them and a Bane to Perception Checks against them. 
Enemies  ignore  the  Provoked  Condition  if  they’re 
Provoked  by  you  and  you’re  currently  Invisible.  If 
anything  would  break  their  concentration  while 
Invisible, they will need to pass a Focus Check or pay 1 
SP or else they become Visible. 
Living Weapon- The user can possess a Weapon owned 
by its Trainer as an Extended Action. While possessing a 
Weapon, it takes the form of that Weapon. If a possessed 
Weapon is equipped by a Trainer, the Pokemon is not 
considered part of the Party and cannot be used. The 
Weapon is also treated as normal, but their Damaging 
Weapon Attacks are Ghost Type instead of Normal. 
Mountable - Any Creature is able to mount or unmount 
this  Willing  Active  Pokemon  as  a  Swift  Action  while 
Adjacent  to  the  User . While  a  Creature  is  Mounted, 
whenever they perform a Movement Action, they are 
treated as having the mounted Pokemon’s Movement 
Value  and  Movement  Capabilities.  Whenever  either 
the  User  or  the  Mounted  Creature  would  perform  a 
Movement  Action,  both  Combatants  move.  Lastly, 
both  Combatants are treated as  Occupying  the  same 
Space. If either the Mounted Creature or the Mounted 
Pokemon would  be  Slid,  both  Combatants  move  the 
required distance. If the Mounting Creature or Mounted 
Pokemon would  trigger  an  Attack of  Opportunity  via 
movement,  the  attacking  Enemy  may  choose  either 
Combatant to Attack, but not both.  
Phaser - As a Swift Action, when declaring Movement, 
the  user  may  move  through  spaces  occupied  by 
Blocking  Terrain and  may treat Occupied  Spaces  as  if 
they were not Slow Terrain. The user cannot end in a 
space with Blocking Terrain in it. This Capability cannot 
be used if the User is suffering from a Mental Affliction, 
unless the user spends 1 SP per Mental Affliction they 
have 
Swimmer - The user treats Ocean Terrain as if it were 
Basic Terrain instead of Slow Terrain when in a Space 
affected by Water or in an Underwater affected Area. 
Teleporter -  As  a  Swift  +  Movement  Action,  select  a 
Space that is a number of meters equal to or less than 
your Movement Value. The user automatically appears 
in  that  Space,  ignoring  all  spaces  between.  This 
Movement cannot Trigger Reactions. The user can only 
select a space by which they have line of sight and must 
end  Teleporter  Movement  touching  a  surface  (They 
cannot land in the middle of the air unless they have 
the Flier Capability). This Capability cannot be used if 
the User is suffering from a Mental Affliction unless the 
user spends 1 SP per Mental Affliction they have.
Blender -  The  user  is  able  to  blend  their  body  with 
their  immediate  surroundings  through  some  form  of 
camouflage method or extreme stealth. The user may 
use the Hide Capability as a Swift Action if desired. The 
user may gain a Boon to Stealth Checks if they’re able 
to blend in with the surroundings. 
Blindsense -  The  user  cannot  be  Blinded  and  gains 
the  Darkvision  Capability.  Blindsense  may  have 
different limitations or specifications depending on the 
user,  such  as  increased  hearing,  supernatural  smell, 
awareness  of  the  environment  or  echolocation.  If  it 
were  echolocation  for  example,  this  capability  could 
be disabled in a crowded area. At the cost of 1 SP , the 
user may enhance one of their senses that are affected 
by this capability for up to 30 minutes. This grants the 
user a Boon to any Perception or Focus Check related 
to that sense
Darkvision -  The  user  ignores  Accuracy Penalties due 
to Darkness and can see through it as if it were bright. 
COMBAT CAPABILITIES

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.178)
body:
178178
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Underdog  - These users are Pokémon that have a Base 
Stat total of 45 or less. Some exceptions apply.
Wallshaper -  The  user  can  create  Illusionary  or 
Invisible walls within 5 m of them while concentrating 
as a Standard or Extended Action. If used as a Standard 
Action,  the  wall  occupies  up  to  4  unoccupied  spaces 
that  are  connected,  If  used  as  an  Extended  Action  it 
can create up to 10 m of wall that are connected. This 
Wall is  treated as  Blocking  Terrain and  is  Immune  to 
all  Physical  Damage.  Creatures  with  a  Weight  Class 
of 4 or more cannot stand on a Wall created this way 
and  cause  it  to  be  destroyed if  they  do  so.  The  User 
may allow creatures to phase through this wall as if it 
weren’t Blocking Terrain whenever they desire. 
Wielder (X)  -  The  user  may be  given one  [Equipment 
-  Weapon]  Item  to  hold  as  if  it  had  the  [Pokemon] 
tag. They add the associated Weapon Attacks to their 
Attack List. The Wielding Pokemon cannot benefit from 
any Weapon Effects other than its Weapon Keywords. 
Wielder  will  often  have  a  Weapon  Type  or  Category 
listed in parenthesis next to it, which denotes the only 
type of Weapons it can equip. If it says Wielder (Arcane), 
they cannot equip a martial weapon, for example. As a 
Swift Action, the Wielder can use any Damaging Attack 
as if it were a Weapon Attack, but its range is replaced 
with the Weapons’ Range.
Alluring - The user is considered to smell very nice or 
they can expel a sweet smelling substance.
Amorphous - The user has an inconsistent body shape. 
They can flatten and reform like putty and stretch their 
body material and condense it. They’re able to shape 
their body by squeezing through tight spaces or doors. 
Aura Reader -  The  user  can  read  the  Aura  of  other 
living beings. Aura conveys two pieces of information. 
First,  its  hue  or  color  reveals  something  about  the 
personality  of  the  Target.  The  hue  of  an  Aura  may 
change over time if an individual undergoes significant 
changes in personality or worldview. Second, Aura also 
appears  brighten  or  darkened  at  times.  Bright  aura 
can  reflect  good  mood  or  intentions,  whereas  dark 
aura can reflect a sour mood or deceptive or negative 
intentions.  An  Intuition  or  Perception  Check  may  be 
required for a clearer view of aura but the longer the 
user is exposed to the target the more accurate their 
assessment of this info may be.
Naturewalk (X) - Naturewalk is always listed with Terrain   
types in parentheses, such as Naturewalk (Forest and 
Grassland). Users ignore the  penalties  of  Slowed and 
Rough Terrain within their listed Terrain. 
The possible Terrains by default include: Grasslands, 
Forest,  Wetlands,  Tundra,  Mountain,  Cave,  Desert, 
Ocean, Urban, Space
Reach  - A User has the Range of their Melee Attacks 
and  Maneuvers  (Excluding  Attack  of  Opportunity) 
increased  based  on  their  size  category;  Small  and 
Medium  Pokémon may  make  Melee  attacks from  up 
to 2 meters away, and Large and bigger Pokémon may 
make Melee attacks from up to 3 meters away. 
Shadow Meld  -  As  a  Standard  Action  or  Extended 
Action, the  user  can merge with  a  Shadow  casted by 
an Object or Creature and become Untargetable. If the 
Object or Creature faints or is destroyed, the user no 
longer  becomes  Untargetable.  While  Untargetable, 
they  cannot  perform  Actions  other  than  losing  the 
Untargetable  Condition.  While  Untargetable,  they 
follow the Object whose Shadow they’ve merged with 
and  are  always  considered  Adjacent  to  them.  They 
also  cannot  be  noticed  except  with  a  Severe  CR  (4) 
Perception or Intuition Check. The user may re-emerge   
from  the  Shadow  as  a  Movement  Action,  losing  the 
Untargetable Condition and appearing in a Space that 
is Adjacent to the Object whose Shadow they merged 
with. If you’re outside of Combat, you may spend up 
to 10 minutes in a shadow, but need to spend 1 SP for 
every additional hour spent in the shadow. 
Telekinetic  -  The  user  can  lift  objects  within  10 m 
using their Mind and utilizing the Focus Skill instead of 
Athletics to determine their Power Rank. When lifting 
objects  this  way, the  user  may  expend  1  SP  to  gain 
+2 Power for an Hour . If the user performs any of the 
following Maneuvers, its Range changes to 6, 1 Target 
and Focus must be used for the user’s Opposed Checks 
instead of listed Skills: Disarm, Hinder , Push, Trip.
Threaded -  The  user  can  form String-Like Threads  or 
Vines which function as appendages. The Power Rank of 
these appendages have strength equal to the number 
of dice they roll for Focus plus half of their Power Rank. 
The  user  may  perform  Tactic   Maneuvers  (Excluding 
Throw or Attack of Opportunity) as if their range was 
5, 1 Target and when performing the Push Maneuver 
this way, they instead slide the Target towards the user . 
Truant  - The User’s Damaging Attacks take a Full Action 
instead of a Standard Action. 
NARRATIVE CAPABILITIES

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.179)
body:
179179
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Illusionist - The user may create minor visual Illusions 
as a Swift or Extended Action. These Illusions cannot be 
more than half a meter in any dimension and produce 
no  sensory  sensations  outside  of  sight.  Any  physical 
contact noticeably disrupts an illusion, otherwise they 
appear  life-like  and  can  be  made  to  move.  Illusions 
cannot  move  further  than  10 m  from  the  user . Any 
one  of  these  restrictions may  be  ignored  at  the  cost 
of 3 SP minus your Tier Level, but when doing so, you 
must hold your full concentration otherwise it will be 
disrupted. 
Magnetic -  The  user  can  lightly manipulate magnetic 
fields.  With  this,  they  can  repel  or  attract  iron  and/
or  steel,  holding  it  to  their  body  or  pushing  it  away. 
Through  this  magnetic  manipulation,  they  can  also 
sense  magnetic  fields,  discern  magnetic  north  and 
sense  disruptions  within  magnetic  fields  within  50 m. 
Users with the Magnetic Capability may communicate 
with  other  Magnetic  users  as  if  they  each  had  the 
Telepath Capability. 
Mender -  The  user  can  create  something  that  has 
medicinal properties using its body. This Capability has 
the same effects as a First Aid Kit (Item).
Mindlock -  The  user  gains  a  Boon  to  all  Opposed 
Focus  Checks.  You  are  automatically  aware  of  all 
attempted uses of the below Capabilities against you. 
If you succeed on an Opposed Focus Check against the 
initiator of said attempt, you discern who attempted to 
use the Capability, roughly where they are (a direction 
and “near”  or “far”), and are immune to this attempt 
and any further attempts to use these Capabilities by 
said initiator until the end of the Scene. The affected 
capabilities  are  Aura  Reader, Dream  Reader, Empath, 
Mind  Weaver,  Soul  Seer,  and  Telepath,  as  well  as 
Channeling and any other effects targeting your Mind 
or Spirit. 
Mind Weaver -  If  the  user  is  touching  a  Creature’s 
head, they may perform opposing Focus Checks, unless 
willing.On a success, you can view all of their Memories 
within the past 24 hours. You may choose to erase any 
Memories within this span. If you succeed by at least 
2+, spend 2 SP ,  or if you spend a Downtime Action (1 
Hour  equivalent), you  may  view  Memories  that  span 
a month ago and erase any of those (Or longer at GM 
Discretion). If you fail, this Effect does not apply and you 
have a Bane to all future attempts with that Creature.
Note: Please ensure that your Players are okay with this being 
used on them before you plan on doing so. Manipulating a 
Player Character’s Memory  is  intrusive and  be  a  boundary 
for some. 
Breathless -  The  user  does  not  need  to  breathe and 
cannot suffocate. 
Chilled - The user emits cold. Depending on the size of 
the Chilled Source, the size of the cold differs. If it’s a 
Small Source, 1 m. If Medium, 3 m. If Large, 5 m. Spaces 
within this range are colder, resulting in the user and 
Combatants  in  this  range  ignoring  the  effects of  the 
Harsh Heat Environmental Modifier .
Dream Reader - The user can view dreams of sleeping 
creatures they are adjacent to. At the cost of 1 SP , you 
may either shape the dreams of a sleeping creature you 
have  physical  contact  with,  or  you  may  project  their 
dreams for those around to see in an illusory form. 
Dead Silent -  The  user  does  not  noticeably  breathe 
or and can control the rate of their heartbeat (Or not 
have one at all). The user does not make noise when 
they  move  unless  they  want  to,  provided  they  can 
concentrate. 
Empath - The user can sense the surface level emotions 
and  feelings  of  others  around  them  within  a  10 m 
range, even if  they don’t  show any body  language to 
indicate those  emotions  that could be  determined in 
an  Intuition Check.  At the  cost of  1  SP , the  user  may 
perform a Focus Check to target a creature within 5 m 
and sense any deeper emotions beyond their surface 
level,  with  the  Challenge  Rating  being  based  on  how 
guarded the Target is with their emotions.  
Engine -  The  user  has  a  special  relation  to  motors 
and vehicles. They can merge with vehicles or motors 
and treat it as their new body. If used by a Varoom or 
Revavroom,  they  may  gain  an  Attack  or  Capabilities 
depending on the type of motor or vehicle.
Gilled -  The  user  does  not  take  Suffocation Damage 
when acting in Underwater Areas.
Glow -  The  user  emits  light.  Depending  on  the  size 
of the Glow Source, the size of the light differs. If its a 
Small Source, 1 m. If Medium, 3 m. If Large, 5 m. Spaces 
within this range are Illuminated, resulting in the user 
and  Combatants  in  this  range  ignoring  the  effects of 
the Low Lighting Environmental Modifier .  
Heater - The user emits heat. Depending on the size of 
the Heater Source, the size of the heat differs. If its a 
Small Source, 1 m. If Medium, 3 m. If Large, 5 m. Spaces 
within this range are warmed, resulting in the user and 
Combatants  in  this  range  ignoring  the  effects of  the 
Harsh Cold Environmental Modifier .

body:
180180
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
may determine the former details. If the user is more than 
5 m away from their Target, they cannot discern the nature 
of a soul.  
Telepath - The user may project their thoughts to the minds 
of  others  and  read  the  surface  thoughts  of  others  within 
10 m.  If  the  mind  being  read is  unwilling,  they  must  make 
an Opposed Focus Check in order to succeed. If the Target 
does not pass a Tough CR (3) Intuition Check and does not 
see  the  user, they  are  unaware of  the  Telepath Capability 
being used and cannot oppose it. The user can only focus on 
one mind at a time. If a Telepath attempt fails an opposed 
Check, they cannot attempt to read their mind for another 
Hour . When  the  user  successfully  reads a  mind,  they  may 
choose to expend SP equal to 3 minus their Tier Level, then 
make a Focus Check, with the CR depending on the secrecy 
of the thoughts or the mental fortitude of the Target. On a 
success, the user will be able to read their deeper thoughts 
beyond surface level  
Thermal Vision - When focusing for at least a Minute, they 
can switch their vision to Infrared, sensing infrared radiation 
around them. When observing the world this way, objects 
with higher sources of heat will stand out in shades of red, 
while objects that are colder will stand out in shades of blue.   
Tremorsense -  The  user  can  sense  the  Location,  Size  and 
Shape of Objects in or on the ground within 10 m of them. 
If the surface of the ground isn’t earth-like (Such as Mud or 
Metal), a Standard CR (2) Focus or Intuition Check may be 
required to use this Capability. 
Tracker - The user has a strong sense of smell that they can 
use to follow other Pokémon or People. If the user has direct 
exposure to a scent of their Target or an object they’ve had 
contact with, it requires a Standard CR (2) Perception Check 
to know the direction of where they are or where they’ve 
been.  The  user  can  also  recall  past  scents  they’ve  had 
exposure to, which is a Severe CR (4) Perception Check. 
True Sight - The user can see through Illusions and Invisibility 
as if their form were visible but ephemeral and translucent.     
Wired - The user has a special relation to electronic devices. 
They  can  enter  machines  and  travel  through  connected 
electronics through any cords that connect them instantly. 
If used by a Rotom, Rotom may take control of the machine 
from within, gaining an Attack chosen by your GM based on 
the machine  
X-Ray Vision - When focusing for at least a Minute, the user 
may see  what lays beyond Blocking  Terrain in  the  form of 
blurry  shapes.  The  maximum  distance  this  Capability  can 
allow  you  to  see  through  is  within  2 m  of  you,  everything 
beyond that range becomes distorted.   
Pack Mon - If the user is a Trainer, they have a Boon for 
all Command Checks involving a Pokemon. If the user is a 
Pokemon, whenever a Skill Check for the following Skills 
is  used  against  them,  it  has  a  Boon  if  the  user  doesn’t 
have an associated leader and it has a Bane if they have a 
leader they respect. Command, Intimidate, Charm, Guile. 
Premonition -  The  User  can  sense  when  a  disastrous 
event would occur within the near future. This can either 
be  an  innate  feeling  or  through  some  sort  of  ritual  the 
user performs, and as such may be limited in how much 
information they  can  obtain.  The  further  they  are  away 
from the source of the event, the more blurry the details 
are  with  a  chance  at  inaccuracies  or  not  sensing.  If  the 
event would occur  within  an  Encounter, they  may get a 
brief glimpse, such as an Entei they’re fighting causing a 
volcanic eruption. This would occur one Round before the 
Event is expected to occur . The extent of the Premonition 
is  limited  to  the  Pokemon’s method  of  future  seering, 
such  as  Gothitelle  only  being  able  to  predict  the  future 
through the star alignment or Absol being able to sense 
natural disasters with its horn. The user may expend SP 
to gain more clarity in one of their visions, with the level 
of detail and accuracy increasing with each expended SP .
Repulsive - The user is considered to smell very bad   or 
they can expel a nauseous smelling substance.   
Shapeshifter -  The  User  can  change  their  shape  at  will, 
taking  on  different  forms  as  an  Extended  or  Standard 
Action.  When  using  this  Capability,  the  user  cannot 
increase  or  decrease  its  total  mass  by  more  than  50%, 
and  they  cannot  replicate  complex  machines  such  as 
computers or phones. They may take on the appearance 
of  these  devices,  but  they  will  appear  simplified  in 
comparison  and  be  non-functional.  They  can,  however, 
transform  into  other  moving  forms  such  as  acting  as 
someone’s prosthetic limb, a living lever or pulley system, 
or  a  Pokémon comparable in  size. Note in  this  last case 
that  the  Shapeshifter  doesn’t  gain  any  qualities  of  that 
Pokémon  without  actually  using  the  Attack  Transform. 
Anyone  closely  examining  a  Shapeshifter  User  may 
determine  its  true  nature  with  a  Perception  Check 
opposed by the User’s Guile or Stealth.  
Soul Seer - The User can see the souls of creatures around 
them.  The  lighter  the  soul  is  then  the  more  likely  they 
are to do good and the more darkness that is in the soul 
means the more likely someone is to do something bad. 
When  a  soul  is  smaller  that  means  the  person  is  more 
injured, and the opposite is true the larger it is. If the soul 
has cracks on it then that means the person has suffered a 
traumatic event and they will only heal once those events 
have been overcome. Upon first view of a soul it normally 
starts foggy, but after a minute it takes shape and the user

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.181)
body:
181181
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Status Afflictions
Poisoned

•  At the end of a Combatant’s Turn they lose a Tick of 
Hit Points. 

•  The Combatant’s Special Defense is lowered by -2 
CS and cannot be increased while Poisoned. When 
Poisoned is cured, unless the Combatant prevents 
its CS from being lowered by this Affliction, the 
Combatant’s Special Defense is raised by +2 CS.

•  Poison and Steel Type Pokemon cannot become 
Poisoned.
Slowed

•  The Combatant has their Movement Value halved 
and cannot apply Speed Evasion.

•  The Combatant cannot perform Reactions
 
 
Burned

•  At the end of a Combatant’s Turn they lose a Tick of 
Hit Points

•  The Combatant’s Defense is lowered by -2 CS and 
cannot be increased while Burned. When Burned is 
cured, unless the Combatant prevents its CS from 
being lowered by this Affliction, the Combatant’s 
Defense is raised by +2 CS.

•  Fire Type Pokemon cannot become Burned.
Chilled

•  The Combatant gains the Vulnerable and Weakened 
Condition while they have this Affliction.

•  Ice Type Pokemon cannot become Chilled.
Paralyzed

•  The Combatant cannot use Bolster Maneuvers 
(Excluding Respite) and becomes Vulnerable.

•  The Combatant can only take two Actions per Round   

•  Electric Type Pokemon cannot become Paralyzed.
Wounded

•  At the end of a Combatant’s Turn they lose a Tick 
of Hit Points, or two if they shifted more than half of 
their Movement Value.

•  The user cannot restore Hit Points.
Status Afflictions are divided into 2 Categories, Physical and Mental Afflictions. Physical Afflictions have a physical 
detriment that usually tends to inflict damage over time. Mental Afflictions tend to result in more debuffs compared 
to inflicting damage and deal with the psyche of the Combatant. 
While they don’t have distinct differences, there are some Abilities or Effects that can only heal a certain type of 
Affliction or be better at curing one category. Unlike the video games, there is no limit to the number of Status 
Afflictions that a single target can have. The next few pages will list all of the Status Afflictions and Conditions, along 
with their effects which are granted to the Combatant while they have the Affliction or Condition.
Removing Afflictions
Afflictions can be removed through any of the following methods:

•  At the end of each Combatant’s Turn (After applying Affliction Effects), if they have a Physical or Mental
Affliction they may make one d 20 Save Check. If meet a Target Number of 15, they are cured of one Affliction.

• At the end of a Scene, all Afflictions are cured.

•  Combatants may perform a Respite Maneuver to recover from Status Afflictions they’re affected by.
PHYSICAL AFFLICTIONS

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.182)
body:
182182
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Enraged

•  While a Combatant is Enraged, they cannot use 
their Standard Action for anything other than using 
a Damaging Attack (Or something that results in a 
Damaging Attack being used by them) and cannot use 
Status Attacks

•  When an Enraged Combatant is hit by a Damaging 
Attack, they become Provoked by the Attacking 
Combatant. If they are already Provoked, they become 
Provoked by the new Attacker .
Entranced

•  When a Combatant gains the Entranced Affliction, 
the Combatant who inflicted it becomes their Fixation 
while Entranced. If their Fixation faints or is recalled, 
they are cured of this Affliction. You cannot be 
Provoked by your Fixation unless otherwise specified.

•  The Combatant cannot Target their Fixation with 
anything unless they’re the only possible Enemy to 
Target. 

•  The Combatant’s Damaging Attacks are reduced by 
an additional Damage Step if their Fixation is within 
3 m of them. 
Suppressed

•  Whenever a Suppressed Combatant uses an EOT 
Attack, after Damage Calculations, they become 
Vulnerable until the end of the next Round. 

•  Whenever a Suppressed Combatant uses a Scene 
or Daily Attack or Ability, after its resolution, they 
become Vulnerable and Weakened until the end of 
the next Round.

•  Combatants with a Boss Template are automatically 
cured of the Suppressed Affliction when they end 
their last Turn in a Round.
 
Cursed

•  The Combatant has a -3 Penalty to Accuracy, Evasion, 
and Save Checks.

•  When a Cursed Combatant misses an Attack or fails 
a Save Check, they lose a Tick of Hit Points (Max: 2 
Ticks per Round).
Dazed

•  When the Combatant performs an Action (Excluding 
Free Actions), roll a 1 d 2. On a 2 they lose a Tick of Hit 
Points or Two ticks if the Action was an Attack. (Max: 2 
Ticks per Round)

•  The Combatant cannot perform Tactics Maneuvers 
and fails all their Opposed Checks.

•  The Combatant cannot use Actions to cure 
themselves of any other Affliction.
Disabled

•  When a Combatant gains the Disabled Affliction, 
something is specified or chosen (Usually an Attack or 
Ability). While a Combatant is Disabled they cannot 
use or benefit from anything chosen to be Disabled. 
Instances of the Disabled Affliction may stack and 
be cured separately depending on the source. 
Combatants cannot have more than 3 instances of the 
Disabled at a time.
Drowsy

•  While a Combatant is Drowsy, their Damaging 
Attacks are resisted by an additional damage step. 

•  While a Combatant is Drowsy, anything they do 
requires a Full Action instead of the normal Action 
cost. 
MENTAL AFFLICTIONS

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.183)
body:
183183
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Conditions
Provoked
While a Combatant is Provoked, any Attacks they make 
that  do  not  include  the  Provoking Combatant have a 
penalty  of -6  to  their  Accuracy  Roll.  While  Provoked, 
a  Combatant may not  have a  total accuracy modifier 
higher  than  0  against  Combatants  that  are  not  the 
Provoking  Combatant.  This  Condition  is  cured  if  the 
Provoking  Combatant  Faints,  its  associated  Status 
Affliction no longer would grant it, or the Combatant is 
Provoked by another source. If a Provoking Combatant 
can  no  longer  be  Targeted, the  Provoked Combatant 
ignores  the  penalties  of  this  Condition  until  they  are 
Provoked by  a  different Combatant  or  the  Provoking 
Combatant becomes Targetable again
Trapped
While Trapped, the affected Combatant cannot exceed 
more than 3 m away from the Combatant who Trapped 
them unless the inflictor moves out of this range. If the 
Afflicted Combatant is a Pokemon, they also cannot be 
recalled. This Condition is cured if the Combatant that 
inflicted  it  Faints,  its  source  is  removed,  the  Inflictor 
moves out of this Range, or the user Faints. 
Tripped
While Tripped, the affected Combatant cannot perform 
Movement  Actions  except  to  cure  this  Condition 
and  all  Accuracy  Checks  suffer -6  to  Accuracy  Rolls. 
While  Tripped, the  affected Combatant is  Vulnerable. 
This  Condition  can  only  be  cured  when  the  affected 
Combatant uses a Movement Action to stand up. If the 
Combatant is in Slow or Rough Terrain, they also need 
to use a Swift Action to stand up.
Untargetable
The  user  cannot  be  targeted  by  any  Effect  (Attacks, 
Abilities,  etc.).  You  cannot  use  or  benefit  from  any 
Effect that would make you Untargetable if  you were 
Untargetable during the previous Round.
Weakened
While  Weakened,  the  affected  Combatant  has  their 
Damaging  Attacks resisted  by  an  additional  step  and 
they  resist  all  Attacks  one  less  step  (Max  Neutral 
Effectiveness). This  Condition  is  cured  after  its  listed 
Duration expires or  its  associated Status Affliction no 
longer would grant it. Combatants with a Boss Template 
are automatically cured of the Weakened Condition at 
the end of their last Turn in a Round.  
Fainted
A Combatant that is at 0 Hit Points or lower is Fainted, 
or “Knocked Out” . Any Static Effects are also disabled 
while Fainted. The Fainted Condition can only be cured 
by being ‘Revived and then brought above 0 Hit Points’ . 
When a Combatant faints, they are cured of all other 
Afflictions and Conditions, excluding Fainted, and their 
Combat  Stages are  reset  to  their  Default Values. The 
only action you can take while Fainted on your Turn is 
to recall or swap Fainted Pokemon you own, or swap 
yourself  out  if  you’re  a  Pokemon.  No  other  Actions, 
Abilities or  Features may be  taken or  Triggered while 
Fainted unless otherwise specified.
Blinded
While Blinded, the affected Combatant has a -6 Penalty 
to  Accuracy  Rolls  and  is  Vulnerable.  When  making  a 
Movement  Action  to  move,  they  must  either  move 
with half of their Movement value or make a Standard 
CR (2) Acrobatics Check. If Failed, they become Tripped. 
Combatants  with  the  Blindsense  Capability  cannot 
become Blinded. 
Marked
An effect that applies the Marked Condition on a Target 
will specify that Mark’s effects. A Combatant can never 
apply a Mark from the same effect to more than one 
Combatant at a time unless specified to have multiple 
Targets. If they apply a Mark to a new target, the old 
one  is  removed,  unless  specified  to  have  multiple 
Targets. A  Combatant can never have more than one 
of  the  same  type  of  Mark.  If  a  Marked Combatant is 
recalled or the applying Combatant Faints, they lose all 
instances of the Marked Condition.
Vulnerable
While  Vulnerable,  the  affected  Combatant  cannot 
apply  Evasion against Attacks. This  Condition is  cured 
after  its  listed  Duration  expires  or  if  its  associated 
Status Affliction no longer would grant it. Combatants 
with  a  Boss  Template are  automatically  cured  of  the 
Vulnerable Condition at the end of their last Turn in a 
Round.  
Conditions are not considered Afflictions but are tracked in a similar manner . Conditions persist for either a timed 
duration or persist as long as their associated Affliction is still on the combatant . If a Condition associated with 
an Affliction or another Condition is cured, it is immediately re-applied if they are still afflicted with the associated 
Affliction or Condition. 
When a Pokemon is recalled, they lose all Conditions they’re affected by except Fainted unless it is inflicted by an 
Affliction they still possess. For example, if a Combatant is Chilled and cures the Vulnerable Condition, it is immediately 
reapplied because they’re still Chilled and are “Vulnerable while Chilled” .

title: Chapter 5 - Combat Rules (p.184)
body:
184184
Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
Your Party  is  looking  worse  for  wear!  Your Team has 
traveled through the forest and taken a bit of damage, 
so how do you go about recovering those HIt Points? 
The following ways are all of the ways you can recover 
Hit Points. 
Item Usage -   The  quickest way  to  recover  hit  points 
is  through  item  usage  such  as  Potions.  This  takes no 
time to administer and can even occur during battle! 
Be wary however as your Inventory is limited and you’ll 
have to prepare for the journeys ahead.
You end a Scene or Excursion -  Whenever  you  have 
around 30 Minutes to an Hour of time that isn’t spent 
in combat, each Player and Pokemon may recover half 
of their Max Hit Points.  
Resting Period -  Whenever your GM determines that 
your Party is going to sleep and gets a full 6-10 Hours 
of  uninterrupted  sleep,  they  recover  all  of  their  Hit 
Points. If the Sleep was interrupted or it was a napping 
period of 1-4 Hours, they instead recover only half of 
their Max Hit Points. This also applies when you’re at a 
campsite while on a Journey. 
Medical Facilities - If your Party comes across a medical 
facility  and  has  more  than  30  Minutes  of  treatment, 
they recover all of their Hit Points.  
Resting & Recovery
Sparring Fainted - If the context of the battle is simply 
a spar on one or both sides, when a Combatant Faints, 
they  are  simply  unable  to  continue  fighting  and  step 
off the field to general safety. They are still conscious 
but cannot contribute to the battle, nor do they have 
the strength to do so, losing their initiative and having 
all  mechanical  effects they  provide  become  disabled 
(Such as static effects where they stand). As a Trainer 
however, you can still recall and send out Pokemon in 
your Party as a Free Action as a Trigger when their active 
Pokemon  faints.  You  however  cannot  perform  other 
actions while in this state. After the Scene resolves, the 
Combatant revives and is set to 1 HP .
Lethal Fainted* - This type of fainting will be set up in 
the Path of Lethality Module
Unlike the default PTU, PTE does not follow an Injury 
system.  This  is  currently  being  playtested with  more 
restrictive restorative usage but may be changed down 
the line! By default, whenever a Combatant is reduced 
to 0 Hit Points, all excess damage is ignored and then 
they  gain  the Fainted Condition.   As  a  GM,  you  then 
determine  the  conditions  of  the  Fainted  Condition, 
with a few examples listed below. 
Non-Lethal Fainted - Non-Lethal Fainting refers to the 
rules  listed  in  the  Fainted Condition  verbatim.  These 
combatants  are  unconscious  and  no  longer  relevant 
on  the  battlefield,  losing  their  initiative.  Combatants 
fainted this way recover and are revived and set to 1 
HP after 1 to 24 Hours without assistance but can be 
woken up if assisted by another Combatant outside of 
an Encounter . 
Fainting

Chapter 5 - Combat Rules
GM: The Snovers look firm in their stance, almost like 
they’re  guards  for  the  path.  The  cubchoo  however 
looks more resolute than cubchoo normally are.
Caleb: That seems odd. With that Poke Edu roll, what 
would I know about Cubchoo’s typical behavior?
GM:  You  recall  that  Cubchoo  nearly  always  have 
a  dismissive  and  passive  demeanor  due  to  being 
protected by their parental figures and if they’re ever 
not around them, they’ll be fearful. Cubchoo that don’t 
have authoritative figures tend to be more bold in the 
wild,  as  though  to  prove  themselves.  Though  that  is 
just the standard behavior, you wouldn’t assume that 
it means no Beartic live somewhere in an area like this.
Caleb: “It seems like these guys won’t let us pass. Let’s 
skip the pleasantries and knock them aside before any 
bigger threats come along”
Mirai: “Agreed. If i stay up here any longer my hair is 
going to freeze solid”
GM: The Pokemon, already weary, sense your hostilities 
and immediately start to try and drive you off. Time to 
start combat!
The  following  few  pages  will  be  a  full  example  of  a 
combat encounter . 
Context
The Party consists of two Trainers, Mirai (F) and Caleb 
(M). Mirai has a Vulpix and Caleb has a Pawniard. For 
the sake of a simple combat, Mirai only has Defender 
Class  and  a  few  supporting  Features  and  Caleb  has 
the  Dark  Specialist  &  Rogue Class.  Let’s also  say  that 
they’re only  Level 2  and  their  Pokemon are Level 10. 
I’m not fully statting sheets so the math will be just 
estimates. 
GM:  As  you  all  travel  up  the  pathway  to  the  frozen 
peak, you feel a harsh wind start to pick up. While you 
were clearly  told  how  cold  it  would  be,  you’ve never 
experienced it this cold, although that is likely fitting for 
a place rumored to be the home of Articuno.
After around an hour of hiking, you reach the apex of 
one of the mountains. You see a large shrine gate up 
in front of you, covered in snow while this area seems 
to  be  heavy  covered in  spruce  trees,  small  Pokemon 
scurrying  around  quick  enough  to  evade  your  sight, 
if  you  weren’t  so  focused  to  reach  the  top  that  is. 
Though as you get closer to the top, you come across 
what seem to be a cluster of sentient trees and a small 
bear that is blue and white in color, seemingly just as 
freezing as you are. 
Caleb: Do I know what those are?
GM: Roll me a Pokemon Education, CR 2. 
[Caleb rolls a 4, 6 & 2]
GM:  You can  easily  recognize the  tree  Pokemon as  a 
Snover, something  you’ve  studied  when  looking  into 
Articuno.  The  bear  however  is  known  as  a  Cubchoo, 
a  more  rare  Pokemon in  tundras  due  to  them  rarely 
leaving their caves. On 3 Successes, you’d usually know 
that its mother Beartic is usually not too far away
Mirai: Do they look hostile at all? If a Beartic is nearby 
we may want to just ignore them.
GM: Gimme an Intuition. CR 3
[Mirai rolls a 6, 4 & 1]
Combat Example

title: Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon
body:
188188
Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon
Switching Pokemon
Battling with Pokemon
Battling  with  Pokemon  is  essential  for  a  Pokemon 
Campaign so there are a few rules to follow! The rules 
below allow for multiple styles of battling and strategies 
with multiple Pokemon on the Field, but remember the 
default and easiest method of Player is just having 
one Pokemon on the Field.
1. Each Trainer may carry up to 3 Pokemon   that 
consist  of  their  Pokemon Party .  This  limit  may  be 
modified at the GM’s discretion but the limit is solely 
for attrition and combat speed reasons. Additionally if 
they had 6, they’d have a counter to almost anything 
you throw at them, and it’d take way too long  
2. Each Player gets one set of Commanded Pokemon 
Actions per Round. In addition to your own Standard, 
Swift,  Reaction   and  Movement  Action,  you  also  get 
one  Standard,  Swift,  Reaction  and  Movement  Action 
that can only be used by your Active Pokemon on the 
field.  This  set  of  Actions  can  be  split  between  your 
Active Pokemon. Even if  you’re fainted, you still have 
a set of Commanded Pokemon Actions, allowing your 
Pokemon to act on their own volition.
3. Players may have Multiple Pokemon on the Field 
at a time.   Unlike  normal  Pokemon,  you  can  have 
any number  of  Pokemon on  the  Field  at  a  time.  This 
however does not change the fact you only have one 
set  of  Commanded  Pokemon  Actions  per  Round.  If 
you have an Infernape, Skarmory and Meowstic all on 
the Field, Actions can be split amongst them, but they 
can only  use  Actions  when  it’s their  Initiative (Unless 
it’s  triggered).  You could  decide  halfway  through  the 
round that you want to have Infernape attack, so if they 
take Initiative,  they’ll  use  a  Standard  Action,  but  the 
Skarmory’s  nor  Meowstic  can  use  a  Standard  Action 
when their Initiative is up, however they can use any 
other available Actions such as Movement or Swift.
Whenever a new Pokemon is switched into battle, they 
may  only  use  Actions  if  there  are  available  Pokemon 
Actions this Round. 
Note: Whenever a Pokemon or Trainer enters a Scene 
or  is  Recalled,  their  Combat  Stages  are  set  to  their 
Default value. 
Full Switching a Pokemon
Requires:  Trainer  or  Pokemon’s  Standard Action. 
If they’re Fainted,   it  can  be  a  Trainer’s  Movement 
Action.
Recalling or Releasing a Pokemon
Requires: Trainer’s Movement or Swift Action
Trainers  can  Switch  their  Pokemon  in  battle,  which 
returns  their  current  Active  Pokemon  into  their 
Pokeball and sends out another Pokemon to take their 
place. This is often done as one Action , known as a Full 
Switch, but can be broken up into separate Recall and 
Release Actions. 
When Switching out a Pokemon you can release them 
to  a  space  within  5 m  and  only  Recall  them  if  you’re 
within 5 m of them. A Trainer cannot perform a Recall 
Action or  Release Action unless  they’re in  possession 
of their Pokeball.   If you faint, your Pokemon can still 
Switch  themselves  out  using  their  Standard  Action, 
even if they’re within a Pokeball.
Using Overleveled Pokemon
Your Players have caught something over their 
maximum Pokemon level, so what happens?! In 
order for that Pokemon to listen to their commands, 
each turn, they must pass a Command Check with 
a CR equal to 1+X, where X is the number of tiers 
they’re above your maximum Pokemon Level. For 
instance, if you’re a Level 2 Trainer, a Level 20 
Pokemon would require a CR 3 Command Check. 
The following occurs depending on how they fared 
compared to the required successes. 
Crit Failure - The Pokemon will actively spite the 
Trainer or their allies somehow. 
Failure - The Pokemon will do what it thinks is best 
towards succeeding the encounter.
Success - The Pokemon will obey the command.
Crit Success - The Pokemon will obey and no more 
obedience checks need to be performed.

title: Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon (p.189)
body:
189189
Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon
Leveling Up Pokemon
Battle Attack List
Unlike Trainers, Pokemon have two Attack lists, Battle 
and Known. Their Battle Attack List consists of 6 Attack 
Slots by default .  During  an  Encounter, the  Pokemon 
may utilize any of the Attacks in their Battle Attack List. 
Known Attack LIst
Whenever  a  Pokemon  learns  an  Attack  but  doesn’t 
want to replace an Attack on their Battle Attack list, it is 
instead added to their Known Attack List. 
Whenever  the  Pokemon  is  Trained  as  a  Downtime 
Action,  they  may  relearn  these  Attacks  and  swap 
them  between the  Battle and  Attack List!  This  allows 
Pokemon to accumulate learned Attacks over time and 
to mix and match based on what challenges they may 
face ahead! There is no limit to the number of Attacks 
on this list. 
Think of this as the explanation on why Pokemon in the 
anime know more than 6 Attacks and a mechanic for 
Pokemon not magically forgetting how to use an Attack 
they’ve used in the past.
While Trainers Level Up based on milestones and the 
number  of  Sessions  they  complete,  Pokemon do  not 
have  experience  or  Level  Up  normally. Instead,  their 
Level is  tied  to the  Trainer they  belong  to.  (If  they’re 
Wild they can be set to any level)
At Trainer Level 1, the Maximum Level their Pokemon 
may be is 5. Each time the Trainer Levels up, this Max 
is increased by +5, all the way to Level 100 when they 
reach Trainer Level 20! 
Additionally,  whenever  a  Trainer  Levels  up,  all  of 
their  Pokemon may be  increased  by  up  to  +5  Levels. 
This  allows them  to  keep up  with  their  Trainer as  far 
as  combat  output.  While  this  may   be  jarring  to  not 
have Pokemon levelup immediately, think of it as the 
same  progression  as  Trainers!  Whenever  they  Train 
a Pokemon via a Downtime Action,   they  may  also 
increase their Level by up to 20 (Unless it would exceed 
their Max Level)! 
Example (Level 1): A Trainer starts with a Level 5 Charmander . 
After the Trainer Levels up to Level 2, the Charmander also 
gains +5 Levels and is set to Level 10.  
Example (Level 8): A Trainer that is Level 8 has a Maximum 
Pokemon Level of 40. They find a wild Nidoran that is level 7 
and convince it to join them. The Trainer Levels up, increasing 
their Max Pokemon Level to 45 and increasing the Nidoran 
to Level 13. During their next Downtime, they decide to Train 
Nidoran a little and as a result, it gains 20 Levels and reaches 
Level 33! If the Trainer performs another Downtime Action 
to Train it, it’s set to Level 45 because it cannot exceed their 
max!  If  you  find  it  a  little jarring  to  suddenly  jump  from a 
NIdoran to Nidoking, you could have them gain fewer levels 
per Training, have stipuations involved with evolving, or just 
acknowledge  that  as  a  higher  Level  Trainer, you’re  more 
efficient at Training!  
Whenever your Pokemon Levels Up, follow the list 
below to grant the Pokemon benefits. 

•  They gain +1 Stat Point to distribute how they please 
(They follow Glass Cannon Rules as well)

•   They  may learn an Attack on their Level-Up list if 
their level is equal to or higher than the number next 
to it.

•  They may switch any Attack(s) between their Battle 
Attack List and your Known Attack List.

•  Check to see if your Pokemon has the possibility of 
evolving!

title: Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon (p.190)
body:
GM Note - You may choose how many of these effects apply to Pokemon opposing the Party. Applying them all of course 
will take longer to stat but will lead to stronger Pokemon! If some pokemon are meant to be weaker, instead pick and choose 
what they gain. Perhaps this wild mankey doesn’t have a role or only has a basic ability! This way it gives you less on your 
plate to think about in combat. Ensure however that if one of these Pokemon are captured, they can be retrained to gain full 
progression benefits.
190190
Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon
190190
Similarly, Pokemon also have a progression system they follow when reaching level thresholds and leveling up. 
Unique Level Thresholds stop at Level 50 so all of the effects are front loaded for shorter campaigns, the maximum 
level for Trainer owned Pokemon is Level 100. (But yes, GMs, you can still have a Level 240 Mewtwo because why 
not)
At Level 1 

• You learn all of your Species Starting Attacks.

• You learn an Ability on your Dex Ability List

• You choose a Skill to become Trained. Trained Skills roll an additional +2 d 6. 

• You gain a Pokemon Role and choose two of its listed Starting Stats to gain +5 Stat Points in.  
These are added to their Base Stats Automatically. You cannot select the same stat. 
At Level 10

• You are qualified to benefit from the Rank 1 Effect of the Pokemon Role you chose at Level 1

• You may learn a Tier 1 Tutor Attack from your Tutor List
At Level 20

• You may learn a Tier 1 or Tier 2 Attack from your Tutor List.

• You may choose a Skill to become Trained. This cannot be the same Skill chosen at Level 1 if it was Proficient or 
Mastered.
At Level 30

• You may either gain another Pokemon Role or gain an additional Ability on your Dex Ability List. (you don’t gain 
the stats from the second ability) 

• You may learn a Tier 1 or 2 Attack from your Tutor List
At Level 40

• You gain +5 Stat Points in two different Stats of your choice, which go in the extras column.

• You may learn a Tier 2 or 3 Attack from your Tutor List
At Level 50

• You may learn a Tier 2 or 3 Attack from your Tutor List

• If your Base Stat Total is 45 or below, you gain +5 Stat Points in two different Stats, which go in the extras column.
At Level 25/50/75/100 (Requires GM Approval - optional bonus)

• You may gain a custom upgrade based on how your Pokemon has been raised or how it differs from normal 
species. If a Pokemon has not been with its Trainer long enough, one of these milestones may be skipped at 
GM Discretion until they develop a bond. This can be an alteration or improvement to an Attack, Role, Ability, 
Capability or Item they have. These are similar in application to Variant Effects and should not be gained if you 
already have one, they’re just optional standardized custom effects. (See: GM Guide). 
Examples
1. My Carkoal enjoys using the Detonator Role to throw out explosive pieces of Coal on the Field. It becomes 
upgraded which allows it to set 3 Hazards as a Standard Action as well as the base effect. 
2. My Quilava loves to use Rollout and Flame Wheel as its signature attacks. It has the Quick Curl Ability added to 
its Dex Ability list, which I retrain Flame Body so I can take it. At Level 50, Its Flame Wheel Attack is improved to be 
aligned with a Tier 3 Attack and gains a bonus while it has a Rolled Coat. I rename it to “Infernal Dash”
Pokemon Progression

title: damage step or it is no longer a Critical Hit.
body:
Example (Sturdy Evolution) - A Shieldon Intercept an Attack and 
then evolves, upon hit they resist the Attack by an additional 
damage step or it is no longer a Critical Hit. 
Example (Empowered Evolution) - A Wartortle who rolled a Critical 
Hit Hydro Pump suddenly evolves with the power its exerting. The 
Hydro Pump’s Range is changed to Line 10 as a result, blasting its 
enemies to shambles. 
Example (Dramatic Evolution) - A Pawniard would faint but is left 
standing at 1 HP as the smoke clears and a Bisharp is standing. 
It gains two ticks of Temporary Hit Points and becomes Enraged, 
ready to strike back
Example (Emotional Evolution) - A Kirlia desperately tries to heal 
its Trainer with Heal Pulse and its emotions lead it to evolve into 
a Gardevoir . This empowers their Heal Pulse and it instead heals 8 
Ticks of Hit Points instead of 5. 
Example (Changes Beliefs) - A Trainer’s Ekans refuses to believe 
it needs to evolve in order to protect its allies. When their Trainer 
faints during a battle, Ekans is shocked, evolves into Arbok, then 
becomes Enraged and gains +2 CS in Attack to avenge its friend.
Example (Needs Strength) - A Charmeleon is weaker than the 
average Charmeleon of its kind. After speaking with a Professor, 
they’ll inform them that some Pokemon need supplements to gain 
the strength to evolve. This Charmeleon will require a Fire Stone to 
evolve as well as meeting the level prerequisites, however once it 
evolves, for the next two sessions, its Default SP ATK CS is set to +3. 
Example (Improved Bond) - A disloyal mankey finally sync’s with 
their Trainer, agreeing with their orders mid combat and throws a 
punch at an enemy Zangoose. Mid-punch, it evolves into Primeape 
and is allowed to change their Attack into one that primeape 
knows. 
Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon
191191
Evolution
Mid-Battle Evolution
Whenever a Pokemon reaches the threshold to Evolve, 
and  their  Evolution  does  not  require  a  Trigger, they 
can  also  perform  Mid-Battle  Evolution.  If  a  Player  is 
planning to perform this, make sure they prepare their 
Pokemon Sheet  before the  session  so  as  to  not  spoil 
combat  pacing.  In  order  to  Evolve during  battle, it  is 
a  Swift Action,  Interrupt from the  evolving  Pokemon. 
Then  once  they  evolve,  they  may  benefit  and  boost 
their power in battle depending on when they evolved. 
Refer to the examples below for some ways a Pokemon 
can evolve. 
Triggered Evolution
Also known as Narrative Evolution, some Pokemon may 
refuse to evolve until a Trigger occurs. Once this Trigger 
occurs,  the  emotional  shock  or  circumstances of  the 
scenario will lead into a sudden evolution and power 
boost! This can be kept secret from players but do not 
use it to punish them, as lower evolution stagers will be 
weaker in battle. In addition, if you do keep a Pokemon 
unevolved for longer, it  could  lead  to  a  power bonus 
to compensate, especially if it has ties to the narrative.
Whenever your Pokemon meet an Evolution Threshold, 
usually stated in the Pokedex, they may evolve at any 
point  into  their  next  Evolution  stage!  This  involves 
several  changes  occurring  in  the  Pokemon, including 
the following
1. Their Base Stats will change . You may also retrain 
your Pokemon’s Stats at no cost.
2. Their Ability List changes. When evolving, you can 
replace your Abilities granted from Level Up Progression 
with Abilities on their Evolution’s Ability List. If the List 
only has one Ability instead of 3, you must replace it 
and this is not optional. 
Note: Your GM must approve you evolving without replacing 
abilities  as  it  doesn’t  make  sense  for  some  Abilities  to  be 
carried  over, such  as  Metapod  keeping  Battle  Armor  on  a 
Butterfree who is very fragile by comparison. However this is 
kept optional by default to expand ability options.
 
3. Their Skills and Capabilities can change.
4. They learn an Evolution (Evo) Attack, listed in the 
Pokedex. 
Evolution  can  be  performed  in  three  different ways, 
depending  on  GM  Discretion  and  Player  preference. 
Considering Trainers can only level up after a session, 
so  can  Pokemon, so  be  flexible with  the  fluff of  your 
Pokemon’s special moment! 
If you don’t want to have power imbalances, you can 
just stick with standard off-screen Evolution, but these 
methods enable cooler and more cinematic evolution 
moments!  (Remember  that  if  Players can  evolve  this 
way, you can have enemies perform this as well!)
Off-Screen Evolution
If  you  want  to  be  simple  and  do  a  classic  Evolution, 
Pokemon  can  simply  evolve  after  a  battle  or  while 
downtime is occurring or between sessions. Nothing is 
special about  this but it certainly leads to less power 
imbalances so it is the safest bet. Off-Screen Evolution 
is the most convenient as it doesn’t involve character 
sheet changes mid battle and is the most common way 
to evolve Pokemon that don’t battle often.
 
Example (Off-Screen Player) - While being trained in a nearby city, 
a Player’s Swinub evolved into a Piloswine.
Example (Off-Screen NPC) - After meeting with their Rivals again 
after the 2 nd Gym, the Rival’s Totodile evolved to Croconaw.

title: In addition to normal Evolution, Pokemon can
body:
192192
In addition to normal Evolution, Pokemon can 
alternatively undergo a process known as Spirit 
Evolution. This allows a Pokemon to get stronger, 
however their physical form won’t change into their 
typical next stage. Previously in PTU this was known 
as being an “Underdog” , however, this is now an 
alternate path in your Pokemon’s progression. What 
this allows you to do is keep a prior form without 
sacrificing the strength of an evolution, fulfilling an 
effect like Ash’s Pikachu being as strong as a Raichu.
How to Spirit Evolve 
In order to have a Pokemon undergo Spirit Evolution, 
they must meet the requirements of one of their 
listed Evolutions. For example, if a Treecko were to 
Spirit Evolve into Grovyle, it would need to be Level 
15, then Level 30 to advance to Sceptile, all while 
physically remaining as a Treecko. 
The following properties change when a pokemon 
Spirit Evolves. 
1. Their Base Stats change to their chosen Evolution
2. Their Level-Up Attack List and Tutor Attack List 
changes to their chosen Evolution
3. Their current Skill Ranks are treated as being one 
evolution step higher . 
Unlike normal Evolution, the following properties do 
not change when a pokemon Spirit Evolves. They are 
preserved from their previous evolution. With GM 
Discretion, some of these can be changed but are not 
recommended. 
1. Their Species does not change.
2. Their Type does not change
3. Their Ability list does not change 
4. Their Capabilities do not change
5. Their Skills do not change to their Evolution’s Ranks
Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon
192192
Spirit Evolution
Example (Ability Discretion) - My Graveler Spirit Evolves into 
a Golem at Level 35, allowing him to learn Sheer Force from its 
Ability List by retraining. This is normally not allowed but the 
GM doesn’t think this abuses anything. Another player decides 
to Spirit evolve his Nincada into a Shedinja and take the Wonder 
Guard Ability, to which the GM reprimands him and denies it. The 
ethereal bug shall suffer .
Example (New Attacks) - My Chewtle Spirit Evolves into a Drednaw 
and is able to learn Jaw Lock at level 20 despite being a small guy. 
This is fluffed as him biting ankles really hard. 
Example (Apperance Changes) - My Eevee Spirit Evolves into a 
Flareon, having its fur become slightly more red and it gains the 
Tutor List of Flareon, being able to learn Flamethrower at Level 40 
as well. It doesn’t however gain the Heater Capability

Detonator
Starting Stats: Attack, Special Attack, Speed
Effect: As a Swift or Movement Action, you may create 
an  Explosive  Hazard  within  3 m  that  are  [Breakable 
- Fragile]. As a Free Action (Priority) when you would 
Faint or as a Swift Action + Reaction, you may destroy

Starting Stats: Attack, Special Attack, Speed
Effect:  As  a  Swift  Action,  you  can  Target  an  enemy 
within  10 m  and  learn  their  current Hit  Points and  its 
percentage based on their Max HP . Whenever you use

Points or has a Status Affliction, they cannot apply Stat 
Evasion against it.

Starting Stats: HP , Special Attack, Special Defense
Effect: Your Special Attacks grant an Energy Token upon 
either missing all Targets or on a 17+ (Max 3). Energy 
Tokens act  as  Spirit  Points  for  Mental  Affliction  Save 
Checks and non-Physical Attack Accuracy Rolls. Energy 
Tokens are removed at the end of a Scene.

Starting Stats: Attack, Special Attack, Special Defense
Effect: As a Swift Action, you may use a Physical Attack 
as if it were the Special Category or vice versa. If the 
Attack matches one of your Types, this is a Free Action 
instead. 
Ranger
Starting Stats: Attack, Special Attack, Speed
Effect: As a Swift or Movement Action you may choose 
a 1-Target Attack you know. Until the end of your Turn, 
that  Attack’s Range  becomes  “5,  1  Target”  if  it  was 
Melee, or its existing range is increased by +2 meters. 
Whenever  an  enemy  within  5 m,  but  not  adjacent  to 
you, misses an Attack on you, you may trigger an Attack 
of Opportunity against them, ignoring Range.
