Starting Stats: HP , Attack, Special Attack
Effect: As a Swift or Movement Action, you create a 2 x 2 
Zone within  8 m.  Then  choose  a  Natural Blast or  Line 
Attack  within Frequency. At the end of the next Round 
if you haven’t fainted, the chosen Attack is used as a 
Free Action on all Enemies in this Zone (unless it affects 
the field like Hazards). This Role may also be activated 
with Priority at the start of a Round. If you do so, the 
Attack is used at the end of the Round rather than the 
next one.
Behemoth 
Starting Stats: HP , Attack, Defense
Effect:  Your  Size  Category  is  increased  by  one  step. 
As a Swift Action, until the end of your turn, you may 
use your Melee Attacks as if their Range were Burst 1 
or Close Blast 2. If any Attacks are used this way, you 
cannot perform Save Checks until the start of your next 
Turn.  
Brawler 
Starting Stats: HP , Attack, Defense
Effect: Whenever you resolve a Melee Damaging Attack 
used as a Standard Action, you may use another Melee 
Attack  or  Basic  Attack  against  a  different  adjacent 
enemy as a Movement Action + Reaction; or a Reaction 
if  the  triggering  Attack missed.  This  Attack is  resisted 
by an additional step for each Status Affliction you are 
affected by. 
Corruptor
Starting Stats: HP , Special Attack, Special Defense
Effect:  Whenever  you  inflict  a  Status  Affliction,  one 
affected enemy may become Marked with a Corruption 
Mark while that have that Affliction. Enemies with your 
Corruption Mark must lose a Tick of Hit Points or have 
a Stat with Positive CS lowered by -2 in order to perform 
a Save Check or use a Self Attack.
A Question you may ask yourself is, what distinguishes one Alakazam from another? Are they all the same? No they are 
not, each of them have their own style of combat preference which gives them assistance on the battlefield. Similarly 
to Trainer Classes, Pokemon also have Roles they can take when they’re born which grant them multiple effects to 
vary their playstyle. Maybe the Alakazam is an artillerist that sets psychic mines that explode on the battlefield!
When a Pokemon is born at Level 1, they gain a Pokemon Role , then they may choose two different stats listed 
under that role to gain +5 Stat Points in (Which automatically apply to their Base Stats). At Level 10, they’ll learn the 
Rank 1 Effect of the Role they chose. At Level 30, they can either gain another Role or gain another Ability (They don’t 
get the stats of their second role). The next few pages will list all Roles.
OFFENSIVE ROLES

title: Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon (p.196)
body:
196196
Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon
196196
In the video games and PTU, you may be familiar with Capture Rolls and throwing a Pokeball in the heat of 
battle to see if a Pokemon is captured! We don’t do that here. The primary reasons are as follows:
1. When it doesn’t work, it ruins combat pacing. 
In the games, a Pokemon cannot be captured if it faints. Anyone who’s faced a legendary knows the woes 
of bringing a legend down to red health, inflicting a status, then throwing as many Timer/Dusk/Ultra Balls as 
humanly possible until luck decides you earned the capture. 
Now imagine that but in a TTRPG where most people only get a turn once every 10 - 30 Minutes. If you don’t 
capture it, all your friends simply wait and pass turns until it’s your turn again, while the victim can still act. Is it 
really fun or just the way things are? Even then, the latest Pokemon games have out of battle captures. 
2. When it works, It kills the suspense of a scene. 
If people adjust the modifiers enough and game the system, someone could easily get lucky and capture an 
enemy before it even has time to act. Capturing a Pokemon is the same as fainting it in regards to removing it 
from the encounter so it essentially is a button for Players to press in order to not see the full potential of that 
Pokemon in combat. The only way to prevent this is by GMs to either have important Pokemon have a higher 
capture rate modifier or deny it from being capturable, but at that point why allow it at all? 
Think of it this way. If i gave you an item that said, “As a Standard Action, make a Pokemon within 5 m faint  if 
you meet a TN on a d 100” would it be balanced? Maybe, by sheer hit or wasting an action. Would it be fun? 
No, especially if the GM could use it against you. After all, how many people enjoy when Fissure or Sheer Cold 
hits them? Very skillful. 
3. It’s high risk gambling. 
Capturing in battle is using an execute move. Your turn is either skipped or you 
remove a combatant. It’s either unfun for the player and they wasted a turn 
(especially those who are salty against dice rolls), or it’s unfun for the 
GM and it removes all the plans they had for that pokemon before 
they were even fainted. If the goal is to have characters battle in 
a scene, let them battle. 
4. It doesn’t even happen in the Anime.
Capturing is always done as the conclusion of a scene. 
Either they make a point to “weaken” the Pokemon first 
before using a Pokeball or it never escalates into a fight 
in the first place. By the way, Legends ZA likely will allow 
capturing when a Pokemon is knocked out. Its canon.
Thus the solution is written in the Pokeball Item, 
where you can only capture willing wild Pokemon or 
unconscious wild Pokemon. Either way the Pokemon 
will have been interacted with and it leads to a 
satisfying capture. 
The next few pages will detail how you can capture 
Pokemon in PTE, either after battle or through social 
interaction. 
Capturing Pokemon

title: Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon (p.197)
body:
197197
Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon
197197
Capturing  via  knocking  a  Pokemon  unconscious  is  a 
very simple concept. After a battle is fully resolved, a 
Trainer as an Extended Action may expend a Pokeball 
to target a Fainted Pokemon and capture them. That’s 
it. From this point, there are three directions you can 
go:
1. The Pokemon treats you normally
They  are  set  at  a  Neutral  Bond  Level.  Depending  on 
your  setting  it  may  be  different,  but  being  defeated 
in battle and captured isn’t something that inherently 
makes  a  Pokemon  hate  you.  It’s  a  very  normalized 
concept to many Pokemon and some may even respect 
you for defeating them in battle, possibly even making 
them like you more! While capturing willing Pokemon 
is the easiest outcome to becoming friends, capturing 
them after battle shouldn’t be an option that’s always 
penalized. Unless a Pokemon has a reason to dislike the 
Trainer, just have them start at neutral terms.  
2. The Pokemon dislikes you
They are set to a Distrusted Bond Level. Sometimes a 
Pokemon doesn’t  start  on  amicable  terms,  especially 
if it’s unwilling and captured while unconscious. Think 
of Pikachu in the anime as disliking ash at the start. If 
the Pokemon has conflict with its Trainer or is naturally 
stubborn,  it  may  start  with  a  lower  bond  and  dislike 
them. Be sure to make it aware to the Player why this is 
the case and give them opportunities to grow together 
to improve their bond
3. The Pokemon hates you
They  are  set  to  an  Disliked  Bond  Level.  Sometimes 
capturing  Pokemon  isn’t  always  rainbows  and 
sunshine.  Sometimes  your  Players  may  be  genuine 
bad guys, seeing a loving couple of Mr . Mime and Jynx, 
then decide to capture one of them and separate the 
lovely  duo  despite  clear  resistance.  Sometimes  they 
may  use  a  snag  ball  and  steal  a  pokemon  from  the 
Trainer it adores. In these circumstances, make it aware 
to the Player why they don’t like the Trainer and give 
them  clear  goals  over  time  to  be  able  to  restore the 
relationship, if possible. As  a penalty, these  Pokemon 
will tend to need a narrative moment to bond with the 
Trainer before they even get to Neutral Bond Level. 
Capturing via Fainting

title: Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon (p.198)
body:
198198
Chapter 6 - Managing Pokemon
As a Gm, you stat a Pokemon in a specific way to suit your 
Scene. You could have a grimer be an Artillerist and have 
a lot of Special Attack so it can throw sludge from a hill 
far away. Once a Player captures a Pokemon, they may 
immediately retrain them and restat them however they 
want. 
This is allowed because if a Player wants a litten to be 
a bulky tank and you stat them to be speedy, they will 
not have fun using something they don’t have control 
over . But at the same time, you as a GM don’t want the 
Pokemon you made to lose its character integrity of how 
you made it, so the solution is to compromise with your 
Players each time a Pokemon is captured. 
Refer to the following questions when a Pokemon is 
captured:
1. What aspects can I change about 
this Pokemon? 
A Trainer may want to change the stat alignment, levelup 
movelist, its advancement options and pokemon roles, or 
even part of its personality! It’s up to the Player and the 
GM to communicate what can freely be changed each 
time something is captured. If a Pokemon is more of a 
blank slate, you should generally allow anything to be 
changed.
2. What aspects of this Pokemon must 
stay? 
Secondly, a GM may specify that certain attributes of a 
Pokemon, listed prior, cannot be altered lest it become a 
different Pokemon. This may include a Pokemon having 
a grudge against you, having a specific role such as not 
wanting to be an Enhancer, or preferring to deal a lot of 
damage and having offensive stat investment. 
3. How can these aspects be altered? 
If there are any aspects that must stay, all of them must 
have a method by which they can be retrained over time 
and the GM must provide a method of doing so. This 
could be using downtime to slowly train the Pokemon 
into becoming an Enhancer , or bonding with it to 
decrease its stubbornness, or bringing it to a Pokemon 
caretaker who is more knowledgeable on training! So 
long as the Player can achieve their desired results, you 
can make them go through steps to make it fulfilling and 
keep its original character integrity. This allows them to 
go througha character arc and earn their new retrained 
status. 
198198
Retraining Pokemon

title: Example of a session divided
body:
Example of a session divided 
into Time Phases
Midnight- The Party is out in the wild at a Campsite. Andrew sleeps 
for 4 Hours and scouts the area for the other 4. Marie sleeps for 4 
Hours and scouts the other 4, alternating with Andrew so they’re 
not attacked. They’re both tired and have a Bane to Skill Checks.  
Morning - They both spend the morning phase meeting with a 
professor that consults with them about their current quest of 
investigating a cave. After which, Andrew will spend some time 
crafting a Darkvision Gadget for him and Marie. Marie will spend 
some time socializing with miners around the area and asking 
about the cave and what they may find inside. She gains some 
information about a dangerous Pokemon inside. 
 
Afternoon- Andrew decides to continue his prior action of crafting 
Darkvision Gadgets, resulting in 2 Darkvision Gadgets. Marie 
decides to take the chance to nap for 4 Hours and get a full night’s 
rest before their quest. This allows her to no longer apply Banes to 
Skill Checks.
 
Evening- Andrew and Marie go and explore the cave. They find 
what they’re looking for and defeat an encounter . 
 
Night - They spend the night phase leaving the cave and 
backtracking, returning to the city and reporting to the professor . 
199199
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
199199
4. Time Specific Activities
Some quests can only be performed at specific times 
of  day.  Allowing  certain  activities  to  be  time  locked 
allows  your  Players  to  strategize  what  they  do  with 
their  day.  For  example,  a  Gym  could  only  be  open 
for  being  challenged  in  the  Morning,  Afternoon  and 
Evening Phase. A black market shop may only be open 
at Midnight. Your Players may have school during the 
Morning and Afternoon  phase but can have free time 
in the rest of the day.  
5. Time Specific Pokemon
Some  Pokemon  can  only  be  found  or  can  be  found 
more commonly at certain times of day. If your Player 
is trying to hunt a Noctowl which is nocturnal, they may 
only  be  able  to  do  so  during  the  Night  and  Midnight 
Time  Phase.  If  your  Players are  going  out  at  night,  it 
may also factor into what they encounter and how your 
Encounters are shaped. 
Using Time Phases, you can structure your sessions in 
a  more  granular  way so  your  Players know  how  long 
actions take and they can plan what they want to do 
during a session. 
There are 5 Time Phases, each listed below.
Midnight [12 AM - 8 AM]
Morning [8 AM - 12 PM]
Afternoon [12 PM - 4 PM]
Evening [4 PM - 8 PM]
Night [8 PM - 12 AM] 
Interacting with Time Phases
There  are  multiple  ways you  can  use  Time  Phases  in 
your Campaign, some of which are listed below. 
1. Allocating Campaign Content
When  performing  specific  actions  during  your 
Campaign,  each  of  them  take  a  specified  number 
of  Time  Phases  at  your  discretion as  the  GM.  If  your 
Players  are  doing  a  Gym  Battle,  you  may  determine 
that it takes all of the Evening Time Phase to do so. If 
your Players are traveling from Viridian to Pewter City, 
you may determine that all the encounters take up the 
Morning Phase to the Evening Phase and they arrive in 
Pewter at Night, meaning the Pokemon Center may be 
less staffed at that point. 
2. Performing Downtime Actions
A  Time  Phase  can  be  used  to  perform  a  Downtime 
Action, each of which costs 4 Hours of in game time. 
This will be the primary usage of Time Phases whenever 
your Party doesn’t have something specific they need 
to do. For example, if your Players need to fight a Gym 
which  is  only  open  from  Morning  to  Afternoon, they 
could spend the Morning Phase Training or gathering 
intel. 
3. Resting 
Players need at least 8 Hours set aside each day purely 
for resting. By default, this is assigned to the Midnight 
Time  Phase  so  this  doesn’t  have  to  be  thought 
about. Players can forgo resting in exchange for more 
Downtime Actions if desired but suffer consequences 
if they do. If a Player ends a Day with little to no Sleep, 
they have a Bane to alll Skill Checks until they get a full 
8  Hours of  sleep.  Alternatively, instead of  sleeping  at 
Midnight,  they  could  Sleep  in  2  other  Time  Phases, 
allowing them to act while others are normally sleeping 
in your setting. 
Time Phases

title: Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
body:
200200
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
Downtime Phase
How to Resolve Downtime Actions
Player decides to spend their Night and half of a Midnight 
Phase  to perform their  [Downtime Action -  Research]. This 
allows them to roll twice, adding both results to the TN.
2. What Downtime Actions will they 
perform? 
Players  may  choose  how  to  spend  their  time  by 
performing  Downtime  Actions.  The  list  further  on 
has a few options as examples but GMs can come up 
with  new  ways  if  they  desire!  The  party  usually  will 
spend  their  time  on  their  own  doing  separate things 
but  players can  also  choose  to  work  together! If  two 
players perform the same Action during a phase, they 
must choose which one of them will be the initiator and 
which will assist. The Initiator performs the Downtime 
Action roll and the Skill Check is considered an Assisted 
Check.  If  multiple  Players  instead  work  together  for 
a  Long  Term Project,  they  instead  both  perform  the 
action separately, gaining no benefits together .
Ex - Two Players are going to a bar to [Socialize] with someone 
they’re  planning  on  robbing.  One  Player  leads  while  the 
other is the wingman. The assisting player has Expert Charm, 
so the initiator gains 1 d 6 and a Boon to the Check. Two other 
Players are at the library as they both try to [Research] and 
find  information  on  an  artifact  they  found.  The  Artifact  is 
a TN 50 Long Term Research Project. They both roll Occult 
Edu, one getting 14 and the other getting 21. Their total is 35 
and they are closer to meeting the Target Number! 
Once the following questions have been answered, take 
turns resolving each action person by person.
Whenever your Players have a gap in activities or have a 
Time Phase where they aren’t doing anything, you could 
have them perform a Downtime Action. Whenever you 
use  a  Time  Phase  for  Downtime  Actions,  it  is  turned 
into what we call a Downtime Phase. When performing 
a  Downtime  Phase,  answer  these  questions  below. 
Ex - The Players know the Gym is open until the Night Phase 
so they plan on using the early half of the day to prepare for 
the upcoming battle, using the Morning and Evening Phase 
to use the Training Downtime Action.
1. How much Time will they spend 
on Downtime Actions? 
Each  Downtime  Action  takes  4  Hours  to  perform, 
meaning  a  full  Time  Phase.  The  only  exception is  the 
Midnight phase which can allow a Trainer to perform 
up to 2 Actions within it, at the cost of sleeping less. 
If  they simply  spend  one  Time  Phase  on  it,  they may 
perform  the  Downtime  Action  as  normal.  However, 
if  they  spend  multiple  Time  Phases  on  the  same 
action,  instead  of  repeating  the  action,  they  gain 
a  bonus.  For  each  additional  Time  Phase  spent  on 
the same action, they add 2 d 6 to their dice roll (This 
may exceed 6 d 6).  If  it  was a  Long  Term Project, they 
roll  multiple  times  instead  for  each  phase  spent.  
Ex -  One  of  the  Players  decides  to  spend  their  morning 
pickpocketing  strangers  by  using  the  [Downtime  Action 
-  Working].  They  only  spent  1  Time  Phase  so  they’ll  roll 
normally. If they spent 2 Time Phases to do so, they’d add 
a 2 d 6 Modifier To their Roll instead of rolling twice. Another 
2. Factor in Skill Check Modifiers 
Once you determine what the Players are going to roll, 
all  of  the  Modifiers  are  determined.  This  can  include 
Assisted  Checks  and  other  Players  performing  the 
Action  alongside  them.  This  also  includes  factoring  in 
any  sources  of  Boons  or  Banes  that  may  apply  to  the 
Skill. For example, Socializing with  a  Primeape may be 
more difficult than normal Pokemon, leading to gaining 
a Bane on the Check. Socializing with their Togepi who is 
very trusting and bonded to them after hatching may be 
easier, resulting in a Boon. 
4. Have them Roll! 
Once  all  factors  have  been  adjusted,  the  Player 
performing the Downtime Action may roll!
5. Determine their Result
Calculate how many Successes they rolled and then refer 
to that Downtime Action’s result chart to determine the 
result.  The  more  successes  they  have,  the  better  the 
result!
Your Players have decided what they want to do, great! 
Now  you  go  around  to  each  player  and  perform  the 
following steps. 
1. Have the Player explain their Goal 
with this Action. 
The first thing you’ll do is have the Player explain what 
their goal is with this Downtime Action and what they’re 
looking  to  gain  from  it.  At  this  point  you’ll  determine 
what  type  of  Downtime  Action  it  is.  For  example, if  a 
Player suggests they want to go learn about a Zygarde 
Cult at the local library, it may be a very basic Research 
Downtime  Action  with  a  TN  of  15.  It  may  not  even 
require a Skill Check if it’s simple enough!
During  this  step  you  also  tell  the  Player  which  is  the 
relevant Skill to use for its associated Skill Check. If the 
Player is  doing  an  Action  such  as  Questing,  you’ll  also 
need to determine the Challenge Rating for the Quest.

title: Books are Long Term Research Projects and the GM determines
body:
Example (Long Term Basic) - A Player has discovered a book in a 
library with the subject matter of “How to bond with your Egg” . 
Books are Long Term Research Projects and the GM determines 
the TN to be 30. The Player spends the Afternoon and Night Time 
Phase to perform 2 Downtime Actions, using the Pokemon Edu 
Skill to roll twice and add to their Progress Value. After succeeding, 
the Player learns how to more efficiently hatch eggs, being able to 
permanently gain more Nurture Points each time they gain some.
Example (Long Term Milestone) - A Player has found an ancient 
compass in a pawn store and stole it in order to research its origins. 
Due to the rarity, it was deemed to be a Mythical Long Term 
Research Project with the TN being 150. The Player is intrigued and 
spends a few Night Time Phases for the next few sessions studying 
it with Occult Edu Rolls. When the Progress Value reaches 80, they 
make a breakthrough and realize one of the symbols came from a 
cult in Snowpoint City that served Regigigas. After completing the 
Research Project, they determine that the Compass is actually a key 
to the entrance of Snowpoint Temple. 
Example (Long Term Limitation) - The Player finds an ancient 
tablet, however it is in Unown Script, meaning it’s indecipherable 
until they find an NPC that can help translate it. Another player 
finds a high tech gadget with the Aether Foundation logo, however 
has no clue how to reverse engineer it until they meet an NPC that 
is an Aether grunt and has worked with that technology in the past. 
GM Note - Do you not have enough screen time to dedicate to 
Downtime during the session? What you could do is relegate it to 
“Off-Screen” . Every week that passes between a session, a Player 
gains one Downtime Action they can describe how they use at 
the start of next Session or resolve it before then.
201201
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
1. The Project’s Target Number
By  Default  there  are  four  different types  of  projects 
which determine its TN. If the Project is Basic, the TN 
is 15 or 30. If it is Intermediate, the TN is 50.  If it is 
Advanced, the TN is 100. If  it  is  Mythical, the TN is 
150. 
 
2. What Skills may be used
Similar  to  designating  a  Skill  to  be  used  in  other 
Downtime  Actions  like  Socializing,  the  GM  also  must 
determine what Skills are valid to use for this Project. 
It doesn’t have to be one Skill and could be multiple, 
depending  on  how  the  Player is  attempting to  tackle 
the challenge. For example, if an Advanced Innovation 
Project  is  creating  a  device  for  reading  dreams,  one 
player could use Occult Edu flavored as studying books 
on  Somnology.  Meanwhile  another  player  uses  Tech 
Edu to progress the project as they flavor it as actually 
creating the device. 
3. Are there any Project Milestones
There  could  possibly  be  milestones  set  within  the 
greater  Target  Number,  whereas  whenever  each 
Milestone  is  met,  a  piece  of  information  is  gained 
or  something  of  significance  is  revealed.  This  is 
recommended for longer Projects so each action feels 
like they’re progressing and not throwing numbers into 
a void. An example, if they’re creating an Item, could 
be at the halfway point they gain a working prototype 
but its effects aren’t as effective. If they’re researching 
something  a  milestone  could  be  that  they  reveal  a 
crucial plot clue. Drip feeding content in a Long Term 
Project ensures it always stays exciting!
4. Are there Project Limitations
Sometimes a Player can’t simply throw time at a project 
and get all the answers. A Player simply can’t say I want 
to make a Gengar Mega Stone and will it into existence. 
Whenever you give them a Project you deem to not be 
possible at the moment, you may place Limitations on 
the Project. Until they solve this Limitation, they won’t 
be  able  to progress past a  certain point. Examples of 
limitations  could  be  needing  a  plot  device,  needing 
information  or  needing  to  be  a  specific  Skill  Rank  in 
order to even work on it. 
Long Term Projects
Unlike normal Skill Checks that measure the number of 
Successes you roll, Long Term Projects are meant to be 
a cumulative Skill Check that is chipped at over time. 
In order to succeed in a Long Term Project, you need 
to  meet  the  Project’s Target Number (Abbreviated 
as TN).   Some  Downtime  Actions  like  Researching 
and  Innovation  follow  the  Long  Term  Project  Rules, 
alongside some edge cases like if you were Crafting a 
complicated item. 
Whenever a Player uses a Downtime Action on a Long 
Term Project,  they  perform  a  Skill  Check  as  normal, 
however instead of counting the number of successes, 
you add all the values of the dice .  If  you  have  any 
Boons on the Check, roll an additional +2 d 6 (This may 
exceed 6 d 6). Conversely if you have any Banes on the 
Check, roll two fewer dice. Additionally, if you use the 
Exertion Modifier, you  perform the  Skill  Check  twice, 
adding both results instead of rerolling, and it must be 
used before the roll is performed.  
The result of adding all the dice becomes your Progress 
Value or is added to an existing Progress Value. In order 
to  complete  the  Long  Term  Project,  your  Progress 
Value must meet or exceed the Project’s TN, then 
you’ll gain all associated rewards or info of the project. 
When  a  Long  Term  Project  is  created,  the  GM  will 
determine the following:

title: Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules (p.202)
body:
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
Working
Sometimes players just need extra money to fund their 
expenses and hobbies! Whenever a Trainer wishes to 
work  during  their  Downtime, they  must tell  you how 
they work and it must be an established way they’ve 
made money in the past or a confirmed way they can 
make money.
The GM will then tell you what Skill it takes to perform 
this job. The Income Value by default for all Trainers 
is $300   but  can  be  adjusted  based  on  the  perceived 
“Hourly  Rate”  of  what  the  Player  is  Doing.  If  they’re 
able  to  work  for  a  high  end  restaurant as  a  waitress 
their rate may become $600 instead! Or this could be a 
high end circus performance and they get $800 as their 
Income Rate since it’s a one time show. 
This should vary based on what the Player can feasibly 
do at this point in the campaign so be sure to give them 
opportunities  for  higher  rates  of  working!  Be  wary 
however that you don’t make an income rate too high 
and they have more money than they know what to do 
with (You don’t want them to make more money from 
Working compared to quest rewards, so make Working 
a source of extra income when they don’t have enough 
or have a big money sink)
Recommended Skills
The  Skill  Check  should  be  relevant to the  work being 
done.  If  they’re  a  bodyguard,  Intimidate  or  Combat 
could  work.  If  they’re  a  charlatan  or  magician,  Guile 
could work. If they’re a Martial artist and tutoring for 
some kids, Command or Combat could work. If they’re 
a Pokemon Caretaker, Pokemon Edu could work.
Results (Based on # of Successes)
0 - They gain Money equal to 3 x the Income Value and 
your Employers aren’t pleased with your performance
1 - They gain Money equal to 4 x the Income Value
2 - They gain Money equal to 5 x the Income Value
3 - They gain Money equal to 6 x the Income Value
4 - They gain Money equal to 8 x the Income Value and 
improve a relationship with a NPC at their job
5+ - They gain Money equal to 10 x the Income Value  
and improve a relationship with a NPC at their job
Downtime - Working
This list will compile a few of the most essential Downtime Action, their recommended skills and the suggested rewards 
based off of how many successes they get!
Downtime Action List
202202
Example (Work Example) - A Trainer is part of Team Rocket and 
wishes to bodyguard a dangerous shipment in their downtime. 
Luckily it was only ambushed by some novice thugs and with 3 
Successes in a Combat Check, the shipment was protected. The 
base rate for this job was $500 so they ended up with $3,000!
Example (Limited Opportunities) - A Trainer made their money by 
mining out rare ore which was their specialty, however they’re in 
the middle of a Grassland encampment so they’re unable to work 
as a Miner or even perform the action at all while in the wild.
My Players want to do something not on the Downtime List!
Just make one up! At first, try to match their action to a listed one, 
especially if it’s a mechanical fit. Then if not, either determine if 
it’s a long term project or something that a single skill check could 
complete. Lastly, check the Modules to see if something more 
appropriate is there, because these are only the most generic 
types of actions that could apply to any setting. Then if you want to 
make it something custom, determine if it’s something that can be 
done outside of the Downtime Phase or if it’s something you want 
to give a bonus to.
Ex - A Trainer makes custom [Orders] through Innovation Action.

title: Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules (p.203)
body:
203203
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
Downtime - Training
Training
Sometimes  players  will  want  to  train and exercise, 
either  with  their  Pokemon  or  training  their  own 
physique. Whenever a Player wants to Train, they either 
designate themselves or a number of Pokemon they’re 
allies with to Train equal to half of their Command Rank 
(Rounded Down). 
As  for  rewards,  the  trained  Pokemon  or  Trainer  will 
recover Spirit Points! A Character can have a Maximum 
of 3 SP at a time. For further info on SP , there is a section 
in an earlier chapter for their full usage.
 Lastly, whenever a Pokemon is Trained, you may do the 
following:

• Swap any Attacks between their Battle and Known 
Attack List.

• Raise them up to 20 Levels, provided they don’t 
exceed your Max Pokemon Level
 
Recommended Skills
The Athletics or Combat if a Trainer is Training, Command 
or  Pokemon  Edu  if  they’re  training  a  Pokemon.  If  a 
Trainer has a specific Training  method you may allow 
other Skills such as training via meditation.
Downtime - Socializing
Socializing
Sometimes players want to hang out with other NPCs 
or their Pokemon   and  improve  their  relationships 
with  others  around  them.  Whenever  a  Player  wants 
to improve their Bond with someone else, have them 
specify who they’re socializing with. Then, have them 
tell  you  how  they’re  socializing  which  will  determine 
the Skill Check.
If  your  GM  is  using  the  Favor  Points  mechanic,  this 
would be the primary way of gaining them. 
 
Recommended Skills
Charm  is  the  default  Skill,  however  depending  on 
how  they  socialize  it  may  be  different. Socializing  by 
hiking may allow Nature Edu or Athletics. Socializing by 
dancing would instead be Acrobatics.
Results (Based on # of Successes)
1 or Less - The Trained Pokemon or Trainer gain +1 SP .
2 or 3 - The Trained Pokemon or Trainer gain +2 SP .
4 or 5 - The Trained Pokemon or Trainer gain +3 SP .
6+ - The Trained Pokemon or Trainer gain +3 SP . SP 
gained this way can exceed the maximum limit of 3 SP 
per Character .
Example (Pokemon Training) - Trainer is letting their Hitmonchan 
spar against some other Pokemon. He performs a Command Check 
and gets 2 Successes. This allows them to bond a little and during 
their next combat they will be hyped and ready to fight.
Example (Trainer is Training) - One Trainer is deciding to calm 
down before a gym and go to their dojo and meditate in peace 
to refresh their mind. They perform a Focus Check and get 4 
Successes, leading to restoring their SP to 3. 
Results (Based on # of Successes)
0 - Their time spent together had some sort of 
unfortunate twist or something bad happened 
1 or 2 - They spend some quality time together and had 
an overall good time.
3 or 4 - They had a great time and their relationship has 
gotten slightly deeper in some way
5+ - They had a great time and their relationship has 
gotten deeper in some way. Something good happened 
as well that provides some sort of benefit to the player .
Example (Socializing) - An Trainer is attempting to obedience 
train his Tropius and improve their relationship who currently 
dislikes him. They try to reinforce the Tropius by feeding it fruits 
and teaching it orders. The GM determines this type of socializing 
would be a Command Skill. The Trainer is inexperienced, only 
having Untrained Command. He rolls 2 Successes resulting in a 
decent amount of improvement with their bond.

title: Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules (p.204)
body:
204204
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
204204
Crafting
Sometimes  players  want  to  create Items   from  their  learned 
recipes. Whenever a Player wants to craft items they know how to 
create, have them tell you which Item Recipes they want to make 
and assign a Skill for them to make a Skill Check in. It doesn’t have 
to  be  a  specific  Item  but  it  does  have  to  be  a  specific  category. 
For instance, if a Player is creating Potions, they can create both a 
Healing Potion and a Malady Potion during this action.
Lastly, the Player needs to spend Money or Ingredients based on 
how much they crafted. This can be determined by taking half of 
the Shop Price and applying it to each Item crafted or coordinating 
with your GM on how many resources it would take to make the 
Items requested.
Another thing to consider is that you may want a crafting project to 
be a Long Term Project if it’s something complicated. For example, 
a Player making a Mega Stone could have the project be a TN 150 
Occult Edu Project and at the end they craft one. 
 
Recommended Skills
Relevant Education Skill associated with crafting the Item
Downtime - Crafting
Example (Small Crafting) - An Engineer wants to make some Pokeballs for 
the Party. They perform a Tech Edu and result in a 1 Success. Pokeballs cost 
$500 in the store so he can make them for $250 each. He can craft up to 
$1000 of value so he can craft up to 4 Pokeballs, expending $1000 in the 
process.  
Example (Expensive Item) - An Armorer wants to make a Longbow (Fine 
Weapon) for an ally. It costs $10,000 so it’ll take $5,000 in resources to 
create. He only gets 2 Successes, being able to craft up to $2,000 in value. He 
subtracts from the Item’s total cost, resulting in $3,000 left. The downtime 
phase resolves with the Longbow being half finished and will be worked on 
later .
Example (Long Term Project) - A Player is creating a device that can disable 
an electronic lock, requiring a TN 50 Tech Edu as a Long Term Project.
Results (Based on # of Successes)
0 - The Player may craft Items up to $500 in value.  
1 - The Player may craft Items up to $1000 in value.
2 - The Player may craft Items up to $2000 in value.
3 - The Player may craft Items up to $3000 in value.
4 - The Player may craft Items up to $5000 in value.
5+ - The Player may craft Items up to $5000 in value 
and they’re efficient with their materials so they may 
craft up to $1000 in value at no cost. 
Granting Recipes
As a reward or possibly by spending 
money, a  Player could  be  granted a 
Recipe,  allowing  them  to  create  a 
new Item!
Example (Reward) - A Player forges a 
bond with a baker and is taught how to 
create Pokemon Food for their Axew. 
Over time the recipe also evolves and 
they can create Pokemon food for all 
Dragn Types. 
Example (Research) - A Player borrows a 
book from the library that teaches them 
how to perform a ritual to Xerneas. 
After finishing the book, they gain a 
recipe for ritual materials.

title: Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules (p.205)
body:
205205
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
Downtime - Innovation
Innovation
Sometimes  players  want  to  discover and create 
something new. Whenever a Player wants to innovate 
and  create  something  new,  they  must  specify  what 
their goal is and gather all ingredients needed that are 
required by the GM to perform such a task.
Then,  you must set  a  Target Number  for how  hard it 
is to create the Item they’re intending to create, if it’s 
even  possible.  Then  inform  them  of  the  associated 
Skill  for  creating  this  Item.  Before  allowing  them  to 
innovate,  make  sure  that  it  is  something  that  you’re 
fine with allowing to mechanically exist in your world 
and not something that would be unfeasible to create. 
Do not let people make snag machines in a world you 
don’t want them to exist. 
Innovation  is  a  Long Term Project   so  refer to  those 
rules and the example below
Downtime - Researching
Researching
Sometimes the Players want to research something in 
the pursuit of gaining information. Whenever Players 
want  to  Research  or  Study  something,  they  must 
specify  what  they’re  studying.  Then,  you  must  set  a 
Target Number of how hard it is to Research this and 
associated Skill for researching the topic.
Researching is a Long Term Project so refer to those 
rules and the example below
 
Recommended Skills
Associated  Education  Skill  or  Focus.  For  example, 
researching  an  ancient  runic  language  would  be 
General  or  Occult  Edu.  Researching  what  medicinal 
properties an  unknown  plant  would  have is  a  Nature 
Edu or Medicine Edu Check. 
Example (Innovating a Cure) - An alchemist has found a Wartortle 
with a strange disease. They want to create an antidote for it 
however they don’t even know what the disease entails so the 
Pokemon Researcher starts a Research Downtime Action in order 
to study the Wartortle.
Once they discover the negative effects and source of the 
disease, the alchemist starts to innovate a remedy which the GM 
determines is an Advanced Project with a TN of 100. However 
when the Progress Value reaches 70, they discover a makeshift 
remedy that they can craft that temporarily removes the effects of 
the disease for one scene. When they reach 100, they discover the 
recipe for the antidote and can craft it to cure them permanently!
Example (Resarching) - The Party finds a strange relic in the Ruins 
of Alph that nobody has ever seen before with unown hieroglyphics 
on a tablet. The GM sets the TN at 100 and a milestone when they 
reach 50. The party is full of low level trainers so there is little way 
they can research it all soon but one trainer is interested in the 
occult and has Adept.
When he’s first able to, he spends the first Night Time Phase and 
half of Midnight obsessing over the relic, even using an Exertion 
Modifier! His first roll is 14 from Night Phase Action. The Midnight 
Phase Action results in a 13 and the roll from Exertion results in an 
8. The final result leads to a 35 but in the process he gets a Bane to 
all Mind Skills during the next day. He gains some momentum but 
feels burnt out and doesn’t study it until a bit later . Later down the 
line he gains more time to study and gets some help with a friend, 
increasing the Progress Value to 50 and gaining a clue since they 
met the 50 Milestone marker which unlocked a quest for them! 
Later again he starts researching and has their Progress Value reach 
100, uncovering what the glyphs mean. 
Recommended Skills
Skill  is  based  on  the  creation. For example, making  a 
herbal remedy would be Medicine or Nature Education. 
Creating  an  anti-invisibility  device  would  be  Occult 
Edu. Making a custom Order for your allies would be 
Command or Pokemon Edu.

title: Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules (p.206)
body:
206206
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
206206
Exploration
Sometimes players want to explore their surroundings and 
gain  more  information  about  where  they  are.  In  this  case, 
players  can  explore  or  scout  with  their  free  time.  When  a 
Player wants to explore or scout an area, they must tell the 
GM what area they wish to gain information about. The GM 
will then determine relevant Skill Check based on how they’re 
exploring.
 
Recommended Skills
Perception if  it’s simply  scouting  or  looking  around.  Stealth 
if  they’re  hiding  from  potential  threats.  Nature  Education 
if  they’re  exploring  the  wild.  Skill  is  based  on  the  location. 
Could even be something like Charm to talk to locals to gain 
information about the area and flirt with those who pass by!!
Downtime - Exploration
Example (Recon) - A Player is scouting a prison to observe the guard shifts 
and possible ways of entry. The area they’re scouting from is fairly guarded 
so they’ll suffer a Bane to the Check. Their Skill Check is Perception since 
they’re far away. With one Success they could learn some info about how 
the guards are acting. If they 3+ Successes they could notice that they could 
infiltrate from a nearby building that isn’t as secure and away from sight.
Example (Wild Exploration) - Another Player is scouting a nearby campsite. 
With 0 Successes and a failed Luck Check, they could be attacked by a 
stealthed predator while exploring. With 3 Successes hey could find a small 
encampment of Mightyena nearby and while they’re on the way back, they 
could notice a small cave with a den of teddiursa nearby!
Example (4+ Reward) - A Player is spending time walking around town, 
talking to the locals about a local town Myth, trying to gain information. 
With a 4+ they find someone who actually had first hand contact with 
the Mythological Pokemon, being able to direct them exactly to the site 
where they found it and describing in detail what happened to them. On 2 
Successes they may have just gained brief information about it being in the 
nearby forest and some of its powers that the rumors suggest. 
Results (Based on # of Successes)
0 - The Player is unable to find information about the 
intended location. Perform a Luck Check and if it was 10 
or less, they suffer a setback as well.
1 - The Player finds a decent amount of information. 
Perform a Luck Check and if it was 5 or less, they suffer a 
setback as well.
2 - The Player finds a decent amount of information 
without being compromised.
3 - The Player finds all the information they were looking 
for and even learns something they didn’t expect
4+ - The Player finds all the information they were looking 
for and notices something very interesting nearby or finds 
something that could help them.

title: Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules (p.207)
body:
207207
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
207207
Downtime - Questing
Questing
Sometimes  players  don’t  have  a  lot  of  time  to  focus  on 
the  smaller  picture but  they  still want to help out   those 
they’ve met along the way! Whenever  a Player wants to go 
questing, this is treated as a mini-session of sorts. Anything 
that  can  happen  “Off-screen”  is  possible  here.  Basically, 
anything  you  don’t  want  to  make  a  session  around  and 
waste time on it is something that’s possible for Questing.
In order to go on a quest, the Player will offer what they want 
to  do. Unlike other Downtime Actions, this Skill Check 
will require a Challenge Rating based on how difficult the 
Quest is. Depending on your Degree of Success, you’ll get a 
result listed below. The GM can inform you of the potential 
rewards and risks before you embark on the Quest.
 
Recommended Skills
The relevant skill is entirely dependent on the Quest. If the 
quest is finding a Pokemon in an area, it could be Perception 
or Pokemon Edu. You could potentially do a Luck Check as 
well to simulate quests without a clear skill such as combat 
related ones,  in  that  case  set  a  Target Number  and  each 
interval of 5 determines an additional success. 
Example (Find a Pokemon) - A Trainer determines that in their downtime 
while preparing for a mission they need a Magnemite to scramble the 
security system. This miniquest requires an initial Skill check of Poke Edu or 
Perception to find the Magnemite with CR of Standard (2). With 2 Successes, 
they find it. If they had 1 Success, they could’ve found it but it was hostile. 
If they had 0 Successes they could’ve been unable to find one. After they 
find it, another skill check is required to convince it to join with CR of Trivial 
(1) since it isn’t hostile. The Player gets 3 Successes and the GM sets a little 
scene where they meet it and they bond a little.
Results (Based on Degree of Success vs CR)
Failed by 2+ - The Player did not succeed in the Quest 
and some complications arose. The quest’s importance 
determines its severity.
Failed by 1 - The Player succeeds in the Quest, but some 
complications arose.
Met the CR - The Player succeeds in the Quest, gaining 
the baseline rewards that were stated.
Succeeded by 1 - The Player succeeds in the Quest, 
gaining a little more than baseline rewards. This could be 
a boosted bond, more money or finding a rarer thing.
Succeeded by 2+ - The Player easily succeeds in the 
Quest, gaining more than baseline rewards. This could be 
a boosted bond, more money or finding a rarer thing.

title: Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules (p.208)
body:
208208
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
[Resource] Items:  Resource  Items  follow  the  same 
rules as [Small] Items but if a [Resource] Item occupies 
an  Inventory  Slot,  you  can  have  any  amount  of  that 
Item (or its subtypes) in the slot for quantity.
[Trinket] Items: Trinket Items do not take an Inventory 
Slot and are always considered to be on hand for the 
owning  Character . These  Items  tend  to  be  Items  of 
little or niche mechanical value that wouldn’t be worth 
bringing  on  a  Journey  (But  may  be  handy  in  a  niche 
situation!),  plot  items  that  should  always  be  carried 
but shouldn’t penalize an Item Slot, or Items that are 
centric  to  a  Character  that  would  always  be  carried 
by them. Examples include a secret key, teddy bear or 
guitar . Trinket Items  are  always  treated  as  Equipped, 
but  may have a  stronger bonus  effect if  they take an 
Equipment Slot. 
Deck of Fate -   This  seems  like an  enchanted deck  of 
playing cards. While this Item occupies an Equipment 
Slot, you gain the Metronome Attack and its Frequency 
is changed to EOT .  [Equipment] [Medium] [Trinket]
[Equipment] Items: Equipment Items only have their 
Effects applied  while  they occupy an  Equipment Slot. 
If  they  are  disarmed,  moved  to  an  Inventory  Slot  or 
unequipped,  their  Effects  are  ignored.  Equipment 
Items may also  have the Weapon or Armor   Tag. You 
can’t  have  two  Large  Weapons  or  two  Large  Armor 
Items  equipped  at  the  same  time.  You can  however 
have one Large Weapon and two other Small Weapons 
equipped!  For  example  this  could  be  a  Rogue  that 
carries a Large Spear but also has a Small Crossbow and 
Knife in their pocket. 
[Pokemon] Items: These Items may also be equipped 
and used by Pokemon. Pokemon gain no effects from 
Items without this Keyword Tag.
[Throwable] Items: These Items can be expended with 
the  Throw  Maneuver  and  if  the  Maneuver  hits,  the 
Target has the Item’s Effects applied to them. 
[Consumable] Items: These Items are expended when 
they’re used and can only be used one time. 
Each  Trainer has  a  total  of 6 Inventory Slots   and  4 
Equipment Slots.   Each  Pokemon  has  a  total  of  2 
Equipment Slots, however any Item they Equip must 
have the [Pokemon] Tag. Inventory Slots are reserved 
for  their  carry-on  storage  such  as  a  backpack  and 
Equipment  Slots  may  only  hold [Equipment] Items, 
symbolizing what the Character is wearing. 
Inventory Slots   are  specifically  for  Items  you  are 
carrying on you that are not currently in usage but can 
be  swapped  at  the  holder’s  whim  as  a  Swift  Action. 
Their Effects are not applied as they are not “Equipped 
or Used” (Unless otherwise specified). For example, a 
Potion can be stored in an Inventory Slot in order for 
the Trainer to use later . Non [Equipment] Items within 
an Inventory Slot can however be used/activated using 
its  listed  Action  or  a  Standard  Action  by  default.  A 
Backpack  in an Inventory Slot cannot hold Items in  it 
because it  is  not  “Equipped” . You cannot have more 
than 12 Inventory Slots by any means.
Alternatively,  Equipment Slots are  reserved  only 
for  [Equipment] Items  and  while  they’re  in  these 
Slots,  they’re  considered  to  be  Equipped  and  their 
effects  apply.  These  Slots  can  have  any  [Equipment] 
Item  occupying  them,  however you  cannot  have two 
[Large] [ Equipment - Weapon] Items  or  two  [Large] 
[Equipment - Armor]   Items  equipped  at  the  same 
time.  The  Last  restriction  for  these  Slots  is  that  you 
cannot equip two of the same Item with the same 
effect. They don’t stack.
Remember that all Players should have a Storage area 
where they can keep Items they don’t have equipped 
safely with an infinite limit. 
Item Keywords
[Large] Items:  Large  Items  take  two  Equipment  or 
Inventory Slots. 
[Medium] Items: Medium Items take one Equipment 
or Inventory Slot.
[Small] Items:  Small  Items  take one  Equipment  Slot. 
Up to three Small Items can occupy one Inventory Slot. 
Example: One Slot can have 3 Pokeballs in it. If you want 
to take 5 Pokeballs, this takes up 2 Slots, one with 3 
Balls and one with 2. 
Item Keywords & Slots

title: Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules (p.209)
body:
209209
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
209209
2. Make sure all Players have equal 
access
The power level of your Party is fine at any level provided 
you  give  them  appropriate challenges  and  there’s no 
inequality in access. All Players should roughly have the 
same amount of special or altered items so there’s no 
feelings of favoritism.
3. Use existing Items as frameworks 
for new Items
If  you’re  making  a  new  weapon,  use  an  existing 
weapon  as  an  example  or  equivalent  of  power . This 
goes for anything customly created such as being given 
a custom move to a character’s starter pokemon. 
4. Grant the Item Keywords based 
on its usage
Let’s say your  Party is  performing a  heist.  What  they 
know is that they need to carry a lot of items out but 
they also want to be prepared and bring in necessary 
healing  supplies  to  deal  with  whatever is  inside.  One 
member of the party decides that instead of bringing 
his weapon, he’ll be a pack mule and carry an additional 
backpack for more storage space. However, he already 
is wearing a backpack and using his Armor Slot! Not to 
worry, the GM is flexible and will allow them to carry 
it  in  their  Weapon  Slot,  granting  it  the  [Equipment - 
Weapon] Keyword, so now he’s carrying 2 Backpacks! 
Though as a tradeoff, he’s weaker in combat and may 
be slower if he’s carrying a lot. Alternatively you could 
fluff it is a big storage box he’s carrying. 
All  of  the  following  Items  are  considered  essential 
and always carried by the party. They do not take any 
Inventory Slots,  similar  to  Trinkets and  are  always on 
hand  when  needed.  As  a  GM  you  may  adjust  what 
you  consider  to  be  ‘Essential’  based  on  your  Party’s 
circumstances.  Your  party  does  not  need  to  spend 
money on any of this to consider it to be on hand, don’t 
tax them for rations. 

• Tech like  Pokedex, Party  Pokeballs,  Phone,  Money, 
Water  and  Rations,  Basic  Baggage,  Towels, Clothing, 
Water Filter, Lighter, Collection Jars. 
Creating Items
Part  of  the  fun  of  being  a  GM  is  creating  new  and 
unique Items, so here are a few considerations when 
making your own. 
1. Be careful of the Power Level of 
custom Items and Trinkets
It  is  fine  if  you  have  custom  Items  require  Inventory 
Slots to bring, especially if they’re niche in usage. If you 
do  create Trinket Items,  have them  be  in  one  of  two 
categories.  The  first  category  is  fluff heirlooms.   This 
could be a family crest that has no other effect other 
than  being  ID  for  a  noble  family. It  could  be  a  scarf 
given by a character’s mother . It could even have small 
effects like the  crest giving a  +2  to Command  Checks 
as  their  family  has  notoriety. The  second  category  is 
plot devices. This could be a magic orb that allows the 
Party to communicate to Yveltal. This could be a parcel 
or  package  meant  to  send  to  a  professor . This  could 
be  a  Zygarde Cube  that holds  cells  they’re collecting. 
Basically  if  it  would  feel  bad  to  need  to  waste a  slot 
on  it,  make it  a  Trinket. If  any of  the  items have vast 
mechanical  effects,  such  as  a  guitar  weapon  being 
blessed  by  meloetta  and  giving  Sound  Lance,  they 
should take an Inventory Slot. 
Essential Items

Pokedex
Effect: While in your Inventory, whenever the 
User performs the Analyze Maneuver, they 
gain a Boon to any  Pokemon Edu Checks they 
perform as a result. As an Extended Action, 
the User may Target a Pokemon within 10 m 
with the Pokedex and scan them. Scanning 
takes a Minute and provides basic information 
about the species such as Attacks known, diet, 
habitat, height, ability list, etc. This Item may 
have additional functionality at your GM’s 
Discretion. [Medium] 
Note: Pokedexes are typically given out at the start 
of the journey but they may lead to Poke edu Rolls 
mattering less.
Pokeball
Effect: You may Target either a willing Wild Pokemon or an 
unconscious Wild Pokemon and expend this Item in order to 
capture them. Once captured, this becomes an Essential Item 
while the Pokemon is in your Party. A Trainer may by default 
have up to 3 Pokeballs carried as Essential Items at a time to 
consist of their carried Pokemon/Party. [Small] [Consumable]
Note: Pokeball Items should only take an Item Slot when they’re 
empty. Don’t let people carry 8+ Pokemon in their Party.
Basic Pokefood
Effect: If expended with a Throw Maneuver, choose an 
unoccupied Space for the food to land. All Enemy Pokemon 
within 3 m of it must pass a Focus Check with a Tough CR (3). 
If any fail, one of them will use their next Standard Action 
to move to that space and eat it. If it wouldn’t make sense 
to logically move there (Such as being on a hazard), or the 
Pokemon has been tricked before in this Scene, the CR is 
reduced at GM Discretion. [Throwable] [Small] [Consumable]
Note: Pokemon may tend to only fall for bait once. Don’t let players 
throw a bunch of food at a boss and prevent it from ever attacking. 
Typed Pokefood
Effect: Upon this item’s creation, choose a Type. If expended 
with a Throw Maneuver, choose an unoccupied Space for the 
food to land. All Enemy Pokemon within 3 m of it must pass 
a Focus Check with a Tough CR (3). Pokemon that match the 
chosen type have a Bane to this Check. If any fail, one of them 
will use their next Standard Action to move to that space and 
eat it. If it wouldn’t make sense to logically move there (Such 
as being on a hazard), or the Pokemon has been tricked before 
in this Scene, the CR is reduced at GM Discretion. [Throwable] 
[Small] [Consumable] 
Pokepuff
Effect: When expended, choose a Pokemon. The next time 
they’re Socialized with as a Downtime Action, add 1 d 6 to the 
roll (This may exceed 6 d 6). A Pokemon cannot be under the 
effects of more than one Pokepuff at a time. This Item also has 
the effects of Basic Pokefood.[Consumable] [Small]
Note: This can be an easy way to bond with most Pokemon. 
Ingredients (Basic)
Effect: When created or noted down by a Player, designate 
what type of Items can be crafted using this item. Each 1 
Ingredient can be expended to craft up to $100 worth of Items 
in the designated category. [Resource] 
Note: This could be a good reward item to sprinkle around in the 
wild. Buying Ingredients allows Players to craft Items while they’re 
Journeying. While normally you can craft with pure money as 
it’s stated as just going to a nearby store to buy necessary items, 
sometimes Players are away from those resources. 
Ex: Ingredients (Tech Scrap) / Ingredients (Food)

title: Artisan Kit
body:
212212
Artisan Kit 
Effect: When buying this Item, choose a Topic. 
Whenever you Innovate or Research during a 
Downtime Phase and use an Exertion Modifier, if it’s 
for something that is related to this Topic, you reroll all 
dice that land on a 1. [Large]
Example: An Alchemy Kit for making new potions, 
Chemistry Kit for making altered potions or a Fashion Kit to 
innovate custom Clothes. 
Climbing Kit 
Effect: While this Item is in your Inventory, you do 
not need to make any Skill Checks in order to climb 
or scale vertical surfaces such as a slope. This may be 
equipped as if it were an [Equipment - Weapon] Item 
in order to ignore Movement Penalites from vertical 
surfaces that would be Slow Terrain. [Medium]
First Aid Kit 
Effect: The user is considered to have standard 
medical supplies that can stabilize injuries out in the 
field. As an Extended Action with around 5 Minutes 
of time, anyone with at least Adept Medicine Edu 
can cure any Physical Status Affliction. While this is in 
your Inventory, at the end of a Scene where Combat 
Occurred, the user and all Allies restore 3 Ticks of Hit 
Point. Multiple instances of the First Aid Kit or Mender 
Capability increase the Ticks restored by +1, instead of 
each seperately restoring 3. [Medium] 
Tool Kit 
Effect: Upon this Item’s Creation, choose a specific 
type of Action. This Item has the tools required to 
perform that Action and when making Skill Checks 
involved with that Action, you have a Boon. This 
cannot affect Skill Checks performed as a Downtime 
Action.  [Medium]
Note: You could also allow certain Tool Kits to be needed in 
order to do Downtime Actions such as a chemistry set for 
Innovation, however don’t let it improve their Skill Checks.  
Example: Lockpicking Kit (Picking Locks), Culinary Kit 
(Making Food), Mining Kit (Precise Excavation), Fishing Kit 
(Fishing in Wild), Navigator Kit (Tracking or Navigation), 
Potion Kit (Making Potions)”
Travel Set 
Effect: Upon this Item’s Creation, choose a type of 
Item that can be crafted. While this Item is in your 
Inventory, you have the tools to perform the Crafting 
Downtime Action while on a Journey. You need 
Ingredients equal to the Crafting Cost in order to 
create it. [Medium]
Example: Cooking for food items, Artificing for Artificer 
Items, Engineering for Pokeballs, etc. 
Greater Poultice 
Effect: Choose one of the following Effects to apply to 
an Adjacent Target. [Small] [Consumable] 

•  They restore 4 Ticks of Hit Points or 100 HP , 
whichever is higher .  

•  They are cured of 2 Status Afflictions. 
Note: Don’t let these be common until Trainer Level 5+
Hazard Bag 
Effect: When this Item is created, the GM will 
determine what type of Hazard it is (It can contain 
any Attack with the Hazard Keyword). When this 
Item is expended, the holder may use that Attack 
immediately as if they knew it. [Small] [Consumable]
Example: A Caltrop bag with the Attack Spikes, or a 
poisonous one with Toxic Spikes, or an Hazard Bag fluffed as 
a Smoke Ball which contains Smokescreen. 
Trap Set 
Effect: When this Item is created, designate a Target 
that it is designed to Trap and the Effects upon the 
Trap Triggering. This Item may be expended as a 
Downtime Action to set the Trap. A Luck Roll may be 
used to determine the success rate of the Trap or it 
may be an opposed Check of the Target to detect the 
Trap when relevant. [Medium] [Consumable]
Example: A Trainer setting traps for Pokemon that would 
ambush them at night to impair the would be ambushers. 
Something of this magnitude would cost $500. Another 
Trap could be putting a magic trap on a book so what 
whoever reads it triggers it. This may cost around $3000.
Tent 
Effect: While you’re on a Journey, you may use this 
Item to get a normal night’s rest. Up to 2 people may 
fit in one tent. [Large] 
Sleeping Bag 
Effect: While you’re on a Journey, you may use this 
Item to get a normal night’s rest. Only 1 person may 
rest in this. [Medium] 
Artificing Kit 
Effect: As a Downtime Action you may perform an 
Occult, Nature or Tech Edu Skill Check. If an area 
would be less likely to find shards, perform it with a 
Bane. if it would be more likely to find shards such as 
in a cave, perform it with a Boon. For each Success, 
you find a Shard Item. Whenever you gain a shard 
this way, roll a d 6 to determine the color . 1 is Red, 2 
is Orange, 3 is Yellow, 4 is Green, 5 is Blue, 6 is Violet.  
[Medium]

title: High Quality Light Armor
body:
214214
High Quality Light Armor 
Effect: While Equipped, the user has +10 Damage 
Reduction. You must be at least Level 15 to equip this. 
[Medium] [Equipment - Armor]
High Quality Heavy Armor 
Effect: While Equipped, the user has +20 Damage 
Reduction. You must be at least Level 15 to equip this. 
[Large] [Equipment - Armor]
Light Backpack 
Effect: While Equipped, the user has 2 more Inventory 
Slots. You can only put [Small] Items in this Inventory 
Slot. If this Item is Impaired, you cannot access any 
Items within these Slots. [Medium] [Equipment]
Note: This Item may be fluffed as any sort of storage device 
one would wear such as a suitcase or purse. If your Party 
plans on gathering items, put them in here!
Heavy Backpack 
Effect: While Equipped, the user has 6 more Inventory 
Slots. You can only put [Small] Items in these Inventory 
Slots. If this Item is Impaired, you cannot access any 
Items within these Slots. [Large] [Equipment]
Seed Bag 
Effect: As a Downtime Action, add 3 of the following 
Attacks to your Seed Bag or switch out any number 
of Attacks in the Bag with others listed Attacks. While 
Equipped, you may use the chosen Attacks as if they 
were on your Attack List. You cannot have more than 3 
Attacks in your Seed Bag. If this Item is Impaired, you 
cannot use any Attacks granted this way. The Available 
Attacks are: Leech Seed, Burn Powder, Mystic Powder, 
Sleep Powder, Stun Spore, Poison Powder [Large] 
[Equipment]
Cargo Bag 
Effect: While Equipped, the user has 4 Inventory 
Slots (Pokemon cannot use these Items). An adjacent 
Trainer may equip or use Items in these Slots as if they 
were in their own Inventory. Only Pokemon may equip 
this Item. Large Items cannot be put in these Slots if 
the user’s size is Small. [Large] [Pokemon]
Example: A Gogoat carrying some spare supplies but it’s at 
the cost of combat power!
Artisan Pack 
Effect: As an Extended Action, choose a [Small] Item. 
While Equipped, you treat that item as if it had the 
[Resource] Keyword within GM approval. If this Item 
is Impaired, you cannot access any Items within these 
Slots. [Medium] [Equipment]
Example: An Ingredient Bag, Berry Bag, Seed Bag, Potion 
Belt or possibly a Utility Belt. A Potion Belt could only equip 
Items with “Potion” in thier name.
Ranger Styler 
Effect: Outside of Combat, whenever a Pokemon 
would be in a state where they could be Captured by 
a Pokeball, you may use this Item to cause them to 
become a Companion. While Equipped, as a Standard 
Action you may Target an Enemy within 5 m and perform 
a Command or Charm Check opposed by their Focus. If 
they fail, choose one of the following Effects to apply: 
[Medium] [Equipment - Weapon]
 

• Guard Break - The next Attack that Targets them 
ignores Evasion. 

• Pacify - During their next Turn, the Target’s Damaging 
Attacks are resisted by an additional step. 

• Restrain - Until the end of their next Turn, the Target 
either becomes Trapped by an Ally or Yourself or has 
their Movement Value halved. The Ally must be within 
3 m of the Target to be Trapped. 
Note: If a Trainer starts as a Ranger Class, give them this.

following Attacks to apply to it. While this Item is 
equipped, the User may use those Attacks. If this Item 
is Large, instead choose three. [Large or Medium] 
[Equipment ]

Supersonic or Metal Sound”

title: Large Gadget
body:
215215
Large Gadget 
Effect: When this Item is created, the GM will 
determine what the effect of the Gadget is upon 
usage. While equipped, the user benefits from 
the effects of the Gadget. [Large] [Equipment] 
[Pokemon]
Note: Large Gadgets are more sustainable and reusable. 
Example: A Large Gadget could be a Mining Helmet that 
when worn provides the Glow Capability and can be reused.
Air Balloon 
Effect: This Item may only be equipped by Small 
Pokemon. While this Item is equipped, the User is 
immune to Attacks with the Groundsource Keyword 
and gains the Flier Capability. [Large] [Pokemon]
Note: Don’t let it pop. Let it be funny.
Assault Vest 
Effect: While this Item is Equipped, the User gains a 
Tick of Temporary Hit Points whenever they’re hit by 
a Physical Attack after Damage Calculations. [Large] 
[Equipment - Armor] [Pokemon]
Berserk Belt 
Effect: While this Item is Equipped, whenever the 
User causes an Enemy to faint via a Damaging Attack, 
they gain +1 CS to Attack or Special Attack. [Medium] 
[Equipment] [Pokemon]
Blessed Relic 
Effect: While this Item is Equipped, the User has +2 to 
Save Checks. [Medium] [Equipment] [Pokemon]
Covert Cloak 
Effect: While Equipped, Attacks against the user have 
a -2 Penalty to Effect Ranges. [Medium] [Equipment] 
[Pokemon]
Dodge Scarf 
Effect: While this Item is Equipped, the user has 
a bonus to Evasion equal to their Tier Level. As a 
Reaction + Movement Action, they may treat this 
bonus as Uncapped until the start of their next Turn 
[Equipment] [Large] [Pokemon]
Eject Module 
Effect: This Item may only be equipped by a Pokemon. 
While this Item is Equipped, whenever the User is hit 
with an Attack, after Damage Resolution they may 
choose to be recalled as a Reaction, Free Action. Their 
Trainer may then send out a new Pokemon as a Free 
Action in the same spot the holder was. This cannot 
be used if the User fainted as a result of the Triggering 
Attack. [Medium] [Equipment] [Pokemon]
Disguise 
Effect: If this Item is [Small], while Equipped, anyone 
who performs a Skill Check to discern your identity 
has a Bane on it. If this Item is [Large], while Equipped, 
you also roll an additional 1 d 6 to Skill Checks related 
to your False Identity.  [Small or Large] [Equipment]
Note: Price depends on the complexity of the Disguise. 
Should range anywhere between 2,000 - 8,000.
Jewelry 
Effect: This Item does nothing without being given an 
effect by the GM. [Small] [Equipment] [Pokemon]
Note: Jewelry such as a crown, ring or braclet should be 
given magical effects depending on where they come from 
and their price should vary as such. Usually between 3,000 
to 15,000. 
Example: An Amulet of Frost that grants the wearer the Ice 
Beam and Aurora Veil Attack while equipped.
Stylish Clothes 
Effect: Upon purchasing or crafting, the GM will 
declare what Skill this Item affects. If the Item is 
[Small], you gain a +1 d 6 while performing a Skill Check 
associated with that Skill, but cannot exceed 6 d 6. If 
the Item is [Large], you may also choose a Specialty as 
if you took the Skill Specialty Talent. While equipped, 
you have a Boon in that Specialty. This cannot affect 
Skill Checks performed as a Downtime Action. [Small 
or Large] [Equipment] [Pokemon]
Note: Small costs $1,500 | Large costs $3,000
Example: A Small Stylish Clothes could be a cute Scarf 
that increases Charm. A Large Stylish Clothes could be a 
Maid Dress that increases Charm and gives a Boon to any 
interaction with customers while working. 
Survival Clothes 
Effect: Upon purchase or crafting, the GM will declare 
a Naturewalk. While Equipped, the User has that 
Capability. [Medium] [Equipment]
Note: All possible Naturewalks are Ocean, Tundra, Desert, 
Urban, Grasslands, Forest, Mountain, Cave, Wetlands, and 
Space 
Example: Flippers for Ocean Terrain or Snow Boots for 
Tundra.
Small Gadget 
Effect: When this Item is created, the GM will 
determine what the effect of the Gadget is upon 
usage. If it grants a Capability, such as through the 
Tech Researcher Class, it lasts until the end of a 
Session or Scene, whichever is longer . [Medium] 
[Consumable] [Pokemon]
Note: Small Gadgets are meant to be temporary tools  
Example: A Small Gadget could be an Oil Lamp that 
provides Glow but has a limited amount of fuel. It also 
could mean a Torch and nothing technical.
Analytic Lens 
Effect: While this Item is Equipped, the User has +1 to 
Effect Ranges. [Medium] [Equipment] [Pokemon]

Companion Ball
Effect: As an Extended Action, Target any Pokemon 
you own to become bound by the Companion Ball 
(Limit 1). While you have this Item in your Inventory, 
the Targeted Pokemon is considered to be in your 
Party, ignoring the Limit of 3 Pokemon in a Party. 
Pokemon bound by this Ball cannot be used in Combat 
in any way. You can only have one Companion Ball in 
your Inventory at a time. At your GM’s Discretion, this 
Item could provide some small benefit based on the 
Pokemon inside. [Medium] 
Note: This is meant to enable small travel partners that you 
want to be with you but not necessarily be strong enough 
to battle. 
Example: Misty’s Togepi or Ash’s Pikachu would be prime 
examples of this. If the GM wants to grant an Effect, while 
Togepi is in your Inventory, the user’s Pokemon may use 
Metronome as if it were on their Attack list, but the Attack 
originates from Togepi.
Elemental Catalyst
Effect: When this Item is created, the GM will choose 
a Type. When this Item is expended, Target a Willing 
Pokemon. The Target becomes a Type Shift of the 
listed Type and follows the rules under that section 
to guide how they’re altered. They may either choose 
to add the listed Type (If they only have one Type), or 
replace one of their existing types with the listed Type. 
[Medium] [Consumable] 
Note: This Item can be fluffed to anything in your setting 
that would enable a Type to change. It could be a potion or 
a small emblem granted by Tapu Lele.
Elemental Enchantment
Effect: When this Item is created, the GM will choose 
an Attack. This Item may be expended to Target an 
[Equipment] Item and grant the chosen Attack. An 
Item can only benefit from up to two Attack this way. 
While an Item with an Elemental Enchantment is 
equipped, the holder may use the chosen Attack as 
if it were on their Attack List. If it is Damaging, it can 
also be used as if it were a Weapon Attack. [Medium] 
[Consumable] 
Note: The Price varies on the strength of the Attack. Razor 
Leaf could only be $2,000 while Flamethrower could be 
$5,000 and Draco Meteor could be $10,000.
Example: A Cloak of Illusions that has the Double Team 
Attack. A Blade of the Forest that has the Leaf Blade and 
Swords Dance Attack. A Mask of Mystery that grants the 
Hypnosis Attack.
Elemental Essence
Effect: When this Item is created, choose a Type. 
When this Item is expended, the Trainer who 
expended it gains the Elemental Afffinity Talent for 
the chosen Type. (This Talent does not take a slot) 
[Medium] [Consumable]
Note: This is any item that would contain enough elemental 
energy to enable an Elementalist Class (See Path of 
Elementalistm)
Note - Rewards & Treasures should tend to be unique to the setting and campaign
Ability Capsule
Effect: When this Item is created, the GM will choose 
any Ability. When this Item is expended, choose 
a Pokemon you own. The Target may choose that 
Ability whenever they would be able to learn one, 
instead of one from their natural Ability List. [Small] 
[Consumable]
Note: Be wary for balance level when handing this out. It’s 
mean to enable odd combos and unique Pokemon, not 
break the system by giving Wonder Guard to Spiritomb. This 
can also be used with Attacks instead of Abilities if desired.
Example: A Mismagius gets an Ability Capsule (Sentry 
Units). These Sentry units are fluffed as illusions of 
Mismagius that populate the field.
Book
Effect: When this Item is created, the GM will 
determine the effect of the book and its associated 
Skill that is used to read it. This Item may be studied 
as a Research Downtime Action with the Target 
Number determined by the GM. When the Downtime 
Project is finished, the Player will learn the contents 
of the book, leading to either information gained or 
a permanent boost to your Character, such as gaining 
a Specialty as if they had the Skill Specialty Talent 
[Small]
Example: A Player finds a book on an ancient Unown 
Language which is a TN 100 Occult Edu book. When fully 
studied, the Player now is able to discipher objects that 
have this language.

title: Ingredients (Unique)
body:
218218
Ingredients (Unique)
Effect: When created or noted down by a Player, 
designate what type of Items can be crafted using this 
item. Each 1 Ingredient can be expended to craft up to 
$500 worth of Items in the designated category. When 
an Item is created entirely with this Item, its effects 
may be altered based on the unique properties of this 
Item. [Resource] 
Note: This is a great basic item to throw around due to 
enabling player creativity with what they can craft.
Example: A Player finds an Ingredients (Unique) fluffed as 
a frozen gold ore found in an Ice Mountain. This serves as 
an Ingredients Item for Weapons or Tech Items but if they 
use entirely this Item, the effect will have some cold related 
effect. The Player makes a sword with this that starts with 
an Elemental Enhancement (Frozen Claw)
Mega Stone
Effect: When this Item is created, choose a Pokemon 
and an Ability on their Dex List. While Equipped by a 
Pokemon, the user may shift into their Mega form as 
a Swift Action. When they do so, they gain +1 CS in a 
Stat of their choice, then gain the chosen Ability until 
the end of the Scene. The User may not shift into their 
Mega Form during the Turn they used a Damaging 
Attack and they cannot use a Damaging Attatck for 
the rest of the Turn once they do shift into their Mega 
Form. [Medium] [Pokemon]
Note: This is temporary until the Book of Pokemon 
Gimmicks
Example: A Cameruptite could give Enduring Rage.
Pokemon Egg
Effect: When this Item is created, choose a Pokemon 
Species. At the end of each Game Day (A full set of 
time phases) and/or as a Downtime Action, roll 2 d 10 
and grant the Egg that many Nurture Points. If you 
have at least Expert Pokémon Education, instead 
roll 4 d 10. When this reaches 100 Nurture Points, 
it hatches into a Level 5 Pokemon of that Species. 
[Medium] 
Note: The cost of this is determined by how Rare the 
Pokemon is in your setting along with additional charges 
if it would hatch with a special quality. Common Pokemon 
would be $500. Rare Pokemon would be $2,000. Very 
Rare would be $5,000. A special Quality would range from 
$2,000 to $5,000 extra depending on effect.
Rare Candy
Effect: A Trainer or Pokemon may expend this Item 
to gain +3 SP and may gain benefits as if they were 
Targeted by a Training Downtime Action [Small] 
[Consumable]
Note: Make sure this stays a “Rare” item so it isn’t 
consistently accessible and they always have max SP .
Fossil
Effect: When this Item is created, choose a Pokemon 
Species. A person that has knowledge in the field 
of Paleontology may study this Item as an Research 
Downtime Action with a Downtime Subject of Poke 
Edu and a Target Number of 100. Once this project is 
completed, the Fossil may be restored to its former 
state, provided they have equipment to do so. The 
chosen Pokemon is hatched at Level 1 and if they 
aren’t Rock Type already, may alter into a Rock Type 
Shift. [Medium] 
Note: Fossils don’t need to be limited to just the canon 
Fossils like Cranidos and Anorith
Example: A Party finds a Bronzor fossil that is Rock Type 
instead of Steel, having a body of Iron filled Stone rather 
than pure Steel.
Gemstone
Effect: This Item has no effect unless otherwise given 
one. Depending on its Rarity it will be given a cost it 
could sell for . Common Gemstones sell for $1,000. 
Rare Gemstones sell for $3,000. Very Rare Gemstones 
sell for $5,000. [Small]
Note: Main point is to sell these as loot. This is a blanket 
item for stuff like Nuggets or Pearls. 
Harnessed Attack
Effect: When this Item is created, the GM will 
determine what Attack is harnessed in this Item. The
holder may expend this Item as a Standard action (Or 
Swift if they’re using the Versatile Effect) to use the 
Attack as if it were on their Attack List. If the Attack 
is Damaging, they may also choose to treat their 
Offensive Stat as if it were Double their Tier Value. 
[Medium] [Consumable]
Example: A Crystal that harnessed the power of a 
Thunderbolt, a heater that can use Overheat or a Pendant 
that can use Hurricane. The price should be around $500 
multiplied by the Attack’s Tier Level. 
 
You can also modify this Item to be treated as an 
[Equipment] Item and if you do, it removes the Consumable 
Keyword and allows them to use it once per Scene instead 
of its listed Frequency.
Gym Badge
Effect: When this Item is created, choose a Type. 
While Equipped, the user’s Attacks that match the 
chosen Type gain a bonus to Accuracy equal to their 
Tier Level. When you use the Training Downtime 
Action on your Pokemon you may teach them a Tutor 
Attack that matches the chosen Type, however, only 
one of your Pokemon may gain an Attack this way at a 
time. [Medium] [Equipment] [Pokemon]
Note: This is just a sample effect. Gym Badges could do 
anything related to the Gym.
