title: Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules (p.220)
body:
220220
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
Creating Weapons
Legendary Weapon
Legendary  Weapons  are  either  the  highest  class  or 
have some  significance  that  grant them  great power . 
Legendary Weapons require the holder to be at least 
Master Rank in its Qualifying Skill in order to equip it. 
When created, Legendary Weapons gain two Weapon 
Keywords of  their  choice. If it is [Medium] you  may 
grant it two Novice Weapon Attacks and one Advanced 
Weapon Attack and one Master Weapon Attack based 
off its Keywords. If it is [Large], you gain Novice Novice 
Weapon Attacks, two Advanced Weapon Attacks, and 
two Master Weapon Attacks. 
2. What are the Weapon’s Categories? 
Weapons  consist  of  three  different  Categories  that 
must be noted upon creation. Their Type, their Range, 
and  their  Size.  Modules  can  expand  the  number  of 
categories and keywords that a Weapon can possess, 
but here is the base list. 
Weapon Type
There  are  two  different  Types  of  Weapons, Martial 
and Arcane. Martial Weapons  can only  deal  Physical 
Damage  and  any  Damaging  Weapon  Attack  used 
through  this  Weapon  has  its  Category  changed  to 
Physical.  Typical  examples  could  include  a  Sword, 
Dagger or Spear . Arcane Weapons are the reverse, only 
dealing  Special  Damage  and  causing  their  Damaging 
Weapon  Attacks  to  become  the  Special  Category. 
Typical examples  could  include  a  Tome, Spellbook  or 
an Orb, but you could also have things like an Arcane 
Sword. 
Weapon Range
There  are  three  types  of  Weapon  Ranges,  each  of 
which determine the Range of your Basic Attacks and 
Weapon Attacks wherever WR is listed. If a Weapon is 
Melee, its Attacks all shift to Melee Range and all Blasts 
turn  to  Close  Blast,  but  the  Damage  Base  of  all  their 
Attacks increase by +2. If it is Short Ranged, its Attacks 
1. What is the Weapon’s Quality?
There  are  4  Tiers  of  Weapons,  each  of  which  are 
listed below. Depending on what Tier the Weapon is, 
it determines how much this Weapon can have when 
being created. 
Training Weapons
Training  Weapons  are  the  most  basic  of  Weapons, 
only for beginners. Players should start with a Training 
Weapon  if  the  Campaign  involves  Trainer  Combat. 
Training Weapons require no Skills to be able to equip 
it but gain no Weapon Keywords. When created, if it 
is [Medium] you may grant it a Novice Weapon Attack 
based  on  what  Keywords  it  ‘would  have’  or  other 
qualifiers. If it is [Large], you instead gain two.  
Simple Weapons
Simple  Weapons  are  also  basic  but  used  for  more 
serious combat and not just practice. Simple Weapons 
require  the  holder  to  be  at  least  Adept  Rank  in  its 
Qualifying  Skill  in  order  to  equip  it.  When  created, 
Simple  Weapons  gain  one  Weapon  Keyword  of  its 
choice. If it is [Medium]  you may grant it two Novice 
Weapon Attacks based on what Keywords it has. If it is 
[Large], you gain two Novice Weapon Attacks, and you 
gain an Advanced Weapon Attack.  
Fine Weapon
Fine Weapons are more refined and elegant weapons 
that  most  battlers  would  be  delighted  to  have.  Fine 
Weapons require the holder to be at least Expert Rank 
in its Qualifying Skill in order to equip it. When created, 
Fine  Weapons  gain  two  Weapon  Keywords  of  their 
choice. If it is [Medium] you may grant it two Novice 
Weapon  Attacks  and  one  Advanced  Weapon  Attack 
based  off  its  Keywords. If it is [Large],   you  gain  two 
Novice  Weapon Attacks, and  you  gain  two  Advanced 
Weapon Attacks.  
Do you want to know what’s crazier than making a Pokedex of 1000+ Pokemon? Making a Weapon Item List with 
every  single  item  a  Player may  want.  So  instead  of  making  a  hyper  niche  rwby-esque  scythe  gunblade,  PTE  will 
provide you with the rubric for creating your own weapons. Whenever you create a Weapon or Purchase one, all of 
the following criteria need to be met and answered.
Example (Custom): I made a Weapon called Bane of the Leviathan. It is a Martial, Melee, and Medium Weapon that is Simple 
in Quality. For Keywords, since it is supposed to be a Dagger, I gave it [Blessed] and [Serrated]. The GM allowed me to have it 
Blessed against Dragon Types instead of Ghost considering it’s the tooth of a Gyarados. For Weapon Attacks, I gave it Double 
Strike and Wounding Strike. 
Example (Arcane):  My  Player wants  a  Magic  Sword. This  weapon  is  Arcane,  Melee  and  Large  that  is  Simple  in  Quality. For 
Keywords I gave it [Enchanting] and [Sharp]. For Weapon Attacks I gave it Beatdown and Arcane Fury.

title: Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules (p.221)
body:
221221
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
4. What are its Keywords?
Each Weapon is able to gain Keywords to grant it effects, 
give  it  access  to  special  Attacks  and  distinguish  itself 
from other  Weapons. These  Keywords can be  granted 
to any Weapon, regardless of its Categories, so feel free 
to fluff it however you want. A Melee Serrated Weapon 
could  be  an  edged  dagger  while  a  Ranged  Serrated 
Weapon could be barbed arrows. 
[Ammo] - You start the Scene with 3 Ammo. Up to twice 
per Attack, As a Free Action you may use Ammo when 
using a Ranged Attack to grant it a bonus to Accuracy 
Rolls equal to your Tier Level for each Ammo expended. 
As a Swift + Movement Action when you have 0 Ammo, 
you regain 3 Ammo. Ranged Weapons Only.
[Barbed] - Weapon Attacks used through this Weapon 
have a 17+ Effect Range to cause their Target to become 
Slowed. If it already has a Slowed Effect Range, it is 
increased by +2. Martial Weapons Only.
[Blessed] - Upon this Weapon’s creation, a Type is 
chosen. As a Swift Action, when the User uses a Weapon 
Attack on this Weapon against a Pokemon of the chosen 
Type, it is one step more effective against them. An 
example is a sword that is blessed against Ghost Types.
[Blunt] - Weapon Attacks used through this Weapon 
have a 17+ Effect Range to cause their Target to become 
Dazed. If it already has a Dazed Effect Range, it is 
increased by +2. Martial Weapons Only.
[Concealed] - The First Weapon Attack you use through 
this Weapon during a Scene treats all Targets as if they 
were Vulnerable against them. Medium Weapons Only
[Cursed] - This Weapon does not count towards the limit 
of Keywords per Item. While the Holder has this Weapon 
Equipped, a negative effect applies to them based on the 
Curse applied to this Weapon and GM Discretion. How 
this Keyword is removed is up to the GM discretion but 
likely can be researched as a Downtime Action.
[Defensive] - While Equipped, The user has a bonus to 
Evasion against Adjacent Attacks or Ranged Attacks equal 
to your Tier Level. Which one it applies to is chosen upon 
the Weapon’s creation.
[Elemental] - Upon this Weapon’s creation, a Type 
is chosen. As a Swift Action, when the User uses a 
Weapon Attack through this Weapon, it deals Damage 
as if it were the chosen Type. 
all  shift  to  6  Meters for  its  Range  and  Blast  Turns to 
Ranged Blast. If it is Long Ranged, its Attacks all shift 
to 12 Meters for its Range and Blast Turns to Ranged 
Blast,  however  they  cannot  Target Adjacent  Enemies 
with their Weapon Attacks. 
Weapon Size
There are two Weapon Sizes which correspond to the 
Item’s Size and how many Inventory Slots it takes, Large 
or Medium. Depending on the Weapon’s Size, it grants 
different keywords and attacks or may even qualify for 
some Attacks!
3. What is its Qualifying Skill? 
Whenever  a  Weapon  is  created,  choose  a  Skill  to 
become its Qualifying Skill. Depending on its Weapon 
Quality, the holder will need that skill at a certain Rank 
in order to equip and use this Weapon. For example a 
Fine Weapon requires the qualifying skill to be at least 
Expert Rank. Depending on certain Weapon attributes 
you can usually determine what skill it should have. 
Martial Weapons
Combat  should  be  its  default  Skill.  Some  weapons 
however  can  have  alternate  qualifying  skills.  For 
example,  Heavy  greatswords  could  require  Athletics 
instead. A Dagger could require Stealth. A Rapier could 
require Acrobatics. A Bow could require Perception. 
Arcane Weapons
Occult  Education  should  be  its  default  Skill.  Some 
weapons however could have alternate qualifying skills 
based on its origin. For example, an Orb could require 
Focus. A Staff of the Forest could require Nature Edu. A 
Magitech Pistol could require Tech Edu.

title: Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules (p.222)
body:
222222
Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
[Serrated] - Weapon Attacks used through this 
Weapon have a 17+ Effect Range to cause their Target 
to gain the Wounded Affliction. If it already has a 
Bleed Effect Range, it is increased by +2. Martial 
Weapons Only.
[Sharp] - Weapon Attacks used through this Weapon 
have a Critical Hit Range of 18+. If it already has an 
extended range, increase it by +1. Martial Weapons 
Only.
[Shifting] - As a Swift Action, this Weapon changes 
from Melee to Short Range or Long Range, or from 
Short or Long Range to Melee or from Short Range 
to Long Range or vice versa. This Weapon has a set 
of learned Weapon Attacks while it’s in Melee and a 
different set while it’s in Ranged. 
[Soulbound] - The owner of this Weapon always 
knows where it is at all times. If they have an empty 
Weapon Equipment Slot, As a Free Action they may 
have the Weapon appear in their hands and Equip it. 
[Sundering] - On Martial Weapons, Weapon Attacks 
have a 15+ Effect Range to lower the Target’s Defense 
by -2 CS. On Arcane Weapons, this instead lowers 
Special Defense. 
[Throwable] - Melee Attacks on this Weapon may be 
used as if they had a Range of 6 m and gains the Smite 
Keyword while used that way, however after you use 
it this way, the Weapon is unequipped and lands in a 
space adjacent to the Target. 
 
[Enhancing] - All Weapon Attacks used through this 
Weapon gain a 15+ Effect Range to “Increase one Stat 
on the User by +1 CS” . Arcane Weapons Only
[Extended] - Melee Weapon Attacks used this 
Weapon are instead treated as 2 m. Melee Weapons 
Only
[Finesse] - Weapon Attacks used through this Weapon 
may have the Speed Stat used as an Offensive Stat 
instead of Attack, if desired.  Martial Weapons Only.
[Homing] - Ranged Weapon Attacks used through this 
Weapon may ignore Blocking Terrain breaking line 
of sight. Whenever you use a Line Weapon Attack, it 
doesn’t need to be a straight line and may be any path 
of connecting spaces. Arcane Weapons Only.
[Life Stealing] - Once per Scene as a Swift Action, 
when using a Damaging Weapon Attack through this 
Weapon, it gains the Drain Keyword.
[Mending] - As a Swift Action when using a Damaging 
Weapon Attack through this Weapon, all Targets do 
not take Damage. Instead, roll the Damage Roll based 
on the Attack’s Damage Base, not including Damage 
Modifiers or Offensive Stats. All Targets restore Hit 
Points equal to the result. Arcane Weapons Only.
[Oversized] - The User may use any Weapon Attack 
through this Weapon as if it were a Full Action. If they 
do, it gains the Smite Keyword. If it already had the 
Smite Keyword it gains the Sureshot Keyword. After 
Damage Calculations, the User can’t apply Speed or 
Bonus Evasion until the start of their next Turn. Large 
Weapons Only.
[Piercing] - Weapon Attacks used through this 
Weapon ignore half of the Target’s Damage Reduction 
and on a 15+, Targets can’t activate Attacks with the 
Shield Keyword against it. Martial Weapons Only.

Chapter 7 - Non-Combat Rules
223223
5. What Attacks will it Grant?
Each  Weapon  can  gain  access  to  Weapon  Attacks 
based on its Size and Quality (Listed in step 1). When a 
Weapon is created, look at the Weapon Attack Tab in 
the Attacks and Ability Reference Sheet in the following 
link. Weapon Attack Index
While looking at the list, see what attacks you’re able to 
learn then pick which ones! In order to have a Weapon 
Attack be  learned,  the  Weapon must meet  any listed 
Requirements such as mandatory Keywords .  For 
example,  you  can’t  take  Backswing  on  a  Sniper  Rifle 
(Large Long Ranged).
Once you have all of your Attacks that are applied to the 
Weapon, you can alter their Range and Damage Base if 
necessary based on their Keywords or Range. Anything 
listed  as  WT  is  replaced  with  the  corresponding 
Weapon Type, such  as  Physical for Martial.  Anything 
that is listed as WR is changed to your Weapon Range. 
Damage Base is then modified if it’s a Range like Melee.
 
Note: Weapon Effects only apply to Weapon Attacks granted 
by  that  Weapon  or  Attacks that  are  specified  to  be  used 
“Through” this Weapon. If you’re holding a Sundering Small 
Weapon and  a  Serrated Medium  Weapon, Attacks granted 
by the Sundering one won’t have the Serrated Effect.
Example (Simple Staff) - A Trainer is given a Staff of the Druids 
by their herbalist uncle in order to defend themselves in the wild. 
It is Simple Quality, which grants it two Novice Weapon Attacks 
and an Advanced Weapon Attack since it is [Large]. It is also an 
[Arcane] Weapon with the [Elemental] Keyword, allowing it to 
switch Attacks to the Grass Type. 
It gains the following Weapon Attacks: 

•  Energy Blast, Rending Spell, Mystic Ward
Example (Legendary Bow) - A Trainer is gifted a Legendary 
Longbow as a gift for their servitude towards Xerneas. It is 
Legendary Quality, which grants it two Novice, Advanced and 
Legendary Attacks since it is [Large]. It is also [Martial] Weapon 
with the [Soulbound] and [Blessed] Keyword against Dark Types. 
As a plot reward, the GM also allows it to have the Moonblast 
Attack but switched to Physical Category as a Weapon Attack.
It gains the following Weapon Attacks: 

•  Salvo, Take Aim, Deadly Strike, Reckless Strike, Deadly Volley, 
Grand Rupture

title: Chapter 8 - Misc Info
body:
224224
Chapter 8 - Misc Info
6. Anything that says its “Extends” Critical Hit Ranges 
or Effect Ranges counts towards the +6 limit of Effect 
Range  and  Critical  Hit  Modifiers  that  a  character can 
have.  They’re  essentially  the  same  thing  but  worded 
differently for sake of  grammar . Leaf  Blade  extending 
their Crit Range by +2 and changing from 17+ to 15+ 
counts as a +2 bonus to Crit Range toward their total of 
+6. If a Sceptile that uses Leaf Blade has its Critical Hit 
Range extended by +2, then has a +5 individual Critical 
Hit Modifer, then they can only apply +4 of their Bonus 
Crit Range towards that Attack. 
7. If something is granted to an Attack, it only applies 
towards the first specified instance and isn’t retained 
for  the  remainder  of  the  Scene  unless specified.   If 
a  Feature  would  say  “When  you  meet  this  Trigger, 
this  Attack gains the  Sureshot Keyword” , it  only  gains 
the  Keyword  for  the  Triggering instance,  not  for  the 
remainder of the Scene. If a Feature would say “When 
you  use  a  Rock  Attack you  can  do  a  thing  to  change 
its  type  to  to  Fire  instead” , this  only  applies  to  the 
Triggering Attack. 
8. Restrictions cannot be bypassed by order of 
operation.  If  anything  restricts  you  from  doing 
something,  some  Players may add  things  in  a  certain 
order to “Rules as written” allow them to bypass the 
restriction. Enforcement of this rule falls down to GM 
Discretion  and  Rules  as  Intended  instead  of  Rules  as 
Written. Some restrictions are specifically written such 
as Versatile Attacks being unable to be used if they used 
a  Damaging  Attack  before  and  preventing  one  from 
being used after . Others are more ambiguous such as 
being  an  Expert  Rank  that  gets  +1 d 6  to  a  Skill  Check 
and  another  +1 d 6  where  one  modifier  can  bypass 
(6 d 6)  and  the  other  cannot.  The  order  of  operations 
should be coordinated and approved by your GM on a 
case by case basis to determine what they see as fair, as 
there is no right answer in ambigous examples.
9. If an Effect with choices applies to multiple 
targets, you  may  choose a different choice for each 
target affected instead of just one choice applied to all 
of them. For example if all Targets in a Burst 2 gain +1 
CS in a Stat, one Pokemon can get Attack while another 
gets Defense. If a Close Blast 2 Attack says the Target 
loses -2  CS  in  Defense or  Special  Defense, one  target 
can lose defense while the other loses special defense. 
This  section  will  be  for  miscellaneous  rulings  that  I 
don’t  know  where  to  put  until  things  can  be  more 
streamlined to resolve issues. 
1. Unless  it  specifies  otherwise,  always round  down 
when halving values in this System. 
2. When  something  specifies  that  it  “Sets”  the  CS 
Value to a specific Value, it is treated as Increasing or 
Lowering the CS to that value. If a Pokemon is Burned 
and cannot increase their Defense CS, you cannot use 
an Effect that “Sets” their Defense CS to +2 CS because 
that would “Increase” it from its current value.
3. When an Effect has a timed duration and it is based 
on a specific Combatant, such as until the start of a user’s 
next Turn or the end of their next Turn,  the following 
case scenarios may occur which prevent a user’s “next 
turn” . Refer below on how to resolve it and remember 
that the GM may determine the approximate time in 
which an effect would expire regardless of rules. 
If the User Faints - It instead resolves at the end of the 
round in which the fainted user did not act
If the User is switched out -  it instead resolves at the 
Turn start (or end) of the combatant who replaced it.
4. At your GM’s Discretion, you may choose to ignore 
mechanical facets of your Character when you do not 
wish to apply it. Some examples are as follows. You may 
choose  to  be  automatically  hit  by  an  Attack and  not 
apply Evasion if desired. You may choose to be affected 
by  Electric  Attacks if  you  would  normally  be  Immune 
such  as  through  Volt Absorb  or  a  cinematic  moment 
like how Onix was soaked with water and affected by 
Pikachu when Ash faced Brock. 
This does not apply   for  ignoring  negative  parts  of 
an  Ability  such  as  ignoring  Contrary when  you would 
have  your  Combat  Stages  boosted  (And  conversely 
decreased).
5. No Effect of the same name can Stack .  Unless  it 
specifies  it  can  stack,  no  two  effects  with  the  same 
name  can  affect  a  combatant.  You  cannot  get  two 
abilities  with  the  same  name.  You  cannot  have  two 
Scope  Lens  equipped.  You  cannot  benefit  from  two 
Helping Hands at the same time. There may be some 
exceptions based on GM discretion. Additionally, Items 
with  the  same  name  but  different effects ignore  this 
such as Two Type Boosters with different Types.   
Clarifying Rules

title: Section Name
body:
Section Name
225225
10. As  a  rule  of  thumb, whenever an Attack is 
modified by a source during a Scene, it  is  treated 
as if it always had that change, but is not considered 
Natural.  If  an  Ally  uses  Flamethrower  and  an  allied 
Water Specialist uses Type Sync to make it a Water Type 
Attack, Flamethrower is now considered a Water Type 
Attack. This means it can no longer be affected by things 
that  only  a  Fire  Attack can  Trigger, but  it  can  Trigger 
things that a non-Natural Water Attack can Trigger . If a 
Pokemon uses a Melee attack through the Ranger Role, 
making it become 6, 1 Target, it cannot be affected by 
things reliant on it being a Melee Attack. Conversely, if 
an Attack is changed outside of a Scene in a permanent 
manner  such  as  through  the  Signature  Technique 
“Scattershot” , that changes the Natural qualities of the 
Attack. If a Trainer used this Technique on the “Hydro 
Pump” Attack, it is Naturally a 4, 2 Target Attack, not a 
Line 6 Attack, thus it cannot meet the trigger  “When 
you use a Line Attack” . As a rule of thumb, all Triggers 
happen simultaneously, so if one trigger’s Effect would 
render another to be illegal to trigger, it must be one or 
the other . This can get confusing so the GM is allowed 
to rule in edge cases, don’t rules lawyer it.
11. Players can ignore positive effects   at  GM 
Discretion.  For  example,  if  an  Attack  has  an  AC  and 
you’re targeting an  ally  it  can  auto  hit  them  because 
they aren’t actively evading it. If an Attack would Slide 
them away 2 m, they can choose to not apply the effect. 
If a Burn Effect would Trigger, you may choose for it to 
not apply.
12. When  a  Feature  or  Ability  says  something  like, 
“The  Triggering Attack’s Type  is  treated  as  if  it  were 
Water Type” , this effect only applies to the instance 
of the Attack being used .  If  they  used  that  with 
Flamethrower, after the  Attack resolves,  it  returns  to 
being  a  Fire  Type Attack. If  a  change  were  to  persist 
beyond that one Attack it would say “For the rest of the 
Scene” or something along those lines. I’m not going 
back to the whole “Attack” vs “Move” debate.

title: Chapter 8 - Misc Info (p.226)
body:
226226
Chapter 8 - Misc Info
PTE Roadmap

• Module | Path of the Mundane -  This Module will 
cover how to run a Campaign without Trainer’s being 
a  Fighter  in  combat.  These  Campaigns  will  be  more 
centric  on  the  anime  similarly  to  PTA  and  be  solely 
Pokemon Support  while  Trainers are on  the  backline. 
The basis of PTE is that Pokemon Trainers contribute to 
the fight, usually physically, but this Module will enable 
Campaigns that do not have Trainers being a physically 
active combatant. 

• Module | Path of Artisanry - This Module provides a 
much more in depth system of jobs and professions that 
can expand character depth and introduce systems that 
let Characters interact with economic aspects of their 
Character . GMs can use parts of this module that are 
relevant to their Players such as a Brewing system for 
an  Alchemist  or  Archeology  for a  Paleontologist. This 
Module includes elements such as Breeding, Farming, 
Fossils, Fishing, Enchanting, Alchemy, etc. 

• Quality of Life & Automation -  Depending on what 
issues GMs run into, as a community we may attempt 
to alleviate them as much as possible. This may include 
translations if  feasible, pokemon generators, creating 
digital assets, quicker statting process, and other tools 
that GMs or Players may benefit from. The streamlining 
will be consist but limited to our technical prowess.

• Server Staff -   During  this  Playtesting  period, 
structuring the server, advertising for more interested 
players  and  organizing  a  team  of  staff,  including 
moderators and developers, is one of the more crucial 
steps in these early phases, as right now there is a smalll 
“Official” Team. To anyone with TTRPG or Poke TTRPG 
experience, feel free to let us know your interest!

• Playtest Feedback - During PTE Version 1.0, we will be 
constantly monitoring feedback and general sentiment 
with  the  system.  Playtest  data  will  be  compiled  and 
the  future  balance  patches will  occur  to  reflect what 
changes are needed alongside smaller hotfix patches. 
If  Classes  would  need  reworks,  instead  of  changing 
it  immediately, we  would  compile  them  all  into  one 
balance update that is relatively infrequent.

• Small Hotfixes - Typos, minor quality of life changes 
and small adjustments will be the priority for now while 
modules are being made and larger reworks progress 
in the background. 

• VTT Implementation - It is a high priority to add the 
PTE  System  to  virutal  tabletops  such  as  Roll  20  and 
Foundry. We however are limited to the skillset of our 
development  team  and  progress  must  wait  until  we 
have  members  that  are  capable  of  coding  and  have 
experience  with  these  platforms.  However, once  we 
do, making the system playable on these platforms is 
a priority!

• Module | Path of the Divine - This  Module  will 
reintroduce  Legendary  and  Mythical  Pokemon  that 
have  powers  beyond  just  normal  Pokemon.  It  will 
include  gifts  that  they  can  bestow, tiers of  legendary 
strength,  and  ways  to  introduce  legends  as  divine 
bosses.  It  will  include  methods  of  servitude  and 
interacting with Legendaries in a divine manner, such 
as patronage or usurpation.

• New Canon Content - As soon as new game content 
comes  out  we  will  address  it  as  soon  as  possible 
on  whether  or  not  it  should  be  added  to  the  system 
and how it’ll  be implemented. New Pokemon such as 
Legends  ZA  and  Gen  10  will  be  rushed  to  immediate 
high priority as soon as it becomes available. 
As of today, the list below contains each piece of content that is planned to be added in the future along with their 
priority level to implementation
HIGH PRIORITY
 MODERATE PRIORITY

title: Chapter 8 - Misc Info (p.227)
body:
Chapter 8 - Misc Info

• Module | Path of the Eras - This Module will cover any 
facet of a Campaign with relevancy based on the age 
its played in, primarily ancient past and distant future. 
Tech Education will  gain many ways of  being  used  as 
GMs  can use  this  Module  to do  high  tech campaigns 
and Players can be put to the test if they’re thrown in 
an ancient world without modern technology such as 
the Pokeball. Classes and concepts will be introduced 
such  as  hacking,  high  tech  weapons  and  even  space 
travel or augmentation.

• Module | Book of Pokemon Gimmicks -   This 
Module will cover all of the various Pokemon Gimmicks 
that  have  been  added  over  the  years  and  how  to 
implement  them  into  your  Campaign.  This  includes 
Megas,  Terastralizing,  Z-Moves,  Burst  Pokemon, 
Contests, Shadow Pokemon, Totem Pokemon, Rangers, 
Dynamaxing, etc. As of right now they have temporary 
Items that can be implemented with GM nuance.

• Actual Play Update - Actual Play is not a major concern 
at the moment, however it is on our radar to someday 
polish the system so that it is easier to play via pen and 
paper . We highly recommend it be played digitally or 
using digital tools, however at this point we will focus 
on Player accessibility and make things easier for those 
who play in real life, such as consolidating dice values 
to more common dice, making printable assets such as 
physical Character Sheets instead of Digital ones, etc. 

• PTE 2 nd Edition - We currently are at a place where 
the  System  is  playable,  however  there  are  a  lot  of 
aspects that were carried over from PTU that I would 
like to eventually change over time. The scope however 
is  far  too  much  to  do  all  at  once,  considering  how 
intertwined  everything  is.  It  would  take  months  and 
possibly  years  to  complete  as  a  team  of  adults  with 
lives of our own.
While a community is being built and other aspects of 
the system are tested, we will be figuring out possible 
ways  to  change  fundamental  parts  of  the  system  to 
improve  it.  This  includes  possibly  the  Skill  System, 
Stats, Combat Math, Action System, and anything that 
is  affected by  those  core  factors.  These  changes  will 
not change the design principles of PTE and it will still 
remain PTE in its soul. 
This  will  always  be  slowly  developed  over  time,  but 
instead of not publishing the system until everything is 
remade from the ground up, weve decided to release 
what  we  have  while  the  larger  projects  are  chipped 
away at in the background. This way there isn’t a major 
update every month that has to be relearned.
LOW PRIORITY
